generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework that combines adversarial diversity, natural adversarial example generation, and robustness enhancement techniques to improve the resilience of deep neural networks (DNNs) against adversarial attacks. Building on the concept of hard positive generation and the psychometric perceptual adversarial similarity score (PASS), we propose a method that leverages semantically meaningful perturbations to create diverse adversarial examples, enhancing data augmentation strategies. By integrating generative adversarial networks (GANs), we generate natural and legible adversarial examples that lie on the data manifold, making them applicable to complex domains such as language and image classification. Furthermore, we incorporate insights from the analysis of universal adversarial perturbations and the geometry of decision boundaries to refine the robustness of DNNs. Our approach demonstrates improved robustness on benchmark datasets including MNIST, ImageNet, and black-box classifiers, while also addressing the limitations of current adversarial detection methods. Experimental results show that our method significantly enhances model robustness and provides a more comprehensive understanding of adversarial vulnerabilities in DNNs.

original_abstract: Rapid progress has been witnessed for human-object interaction (HOI) recognition, but most existing models are confined to single-stage reasoning pipelines. Considering the intrinsic complexity of the task, we introduce a cascade architecture for a multi-stage, coarse-to-fine HOI understanding. At each stage, an instance localization network progressively refines HOI proposals and feeds them into an interaction recognition network. Each of the two networks is also connected to its predecessor at the previous stage, enabling cross-stage information propagation. The interaction recognition network has two crucial parts: a relation ranking module for high-quality HOI proposal selection and a triple-stream classifier for relation prediction. With our carefully-designed human-centric relation features, these two modules work collaboratively towards effective interaction understanding. Further beyond relation detection on a bounding-box level, we make our framework flexible to perform fine-grained pixel-wise relation segmentation; this provides a new glimpse into better relation modeling. Our approach reached the $1^{st}$ place in the ICCV2019 Person in Context Challenge, on both relation detection and segmentation tasks. It also shows promising results on V-COCO.
generated_abstract: This paper presents a novel framework for detecting human-object interactions (HOI) by integrating multiple complementary approaches from recent literature. Building on the HO-RCNN architecture, which leverages interaction patterns to model spatial relations between humans and objects, we incorporate instance-centric attention mechanisms to dynamically focus on relevant image regions based on human and object appearances. Additionally, we integrate pairwise body-part attention to capture the collaborative nature of human interactions and enhance feature representation. Our model also employs a graph-based reasoning approach, inspired by GPNN and RPNN, to infer structured interaction triplets by capturing higher-order relationships and contextual dependencies. Furthermore, we introduce a knowledge-aware component that utilizes semantic regularities and external knowledge graphs to improve detection of rare interaction categories. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets such as HICO-DET, V-COCO, and HCVRD demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods, achieving robust and interpretable performance across diverse interaction scenarios.

original_abstract: It has been widely accepted that Graphics Processing Units (GPU) is one of promising schemes for encryption acceleration, in particular, the support of complex mathematical calculations such as integer and logical operations makes the implementation easier; however, complexes such as parallel granularity, memory allocation still imposes a burden on real world implementations. In this paper, we propose a new approach for Advanced Encryption Standard accelerations, including both encryption and decryption. Specifically, we adapt the Electronic Code Book mode for cryptographic transformation, look up table scheme for fast lookup, and a granularity of one state per thread for thread scheduling. Our experimental results offer researchers a good understanding on GPU architectures and software accelerations. In addition, both our source code and experimental results are freely available.
generated_abstract: This paper presents a novel application that combines GPU memory hierarchy analysis with cryptographic acceleration, leveraging insights from prior studies on GPU memory characteristics and AES encryption performance. By applying fine-grained microbenchmarking techniques to modern GPU architectures, we uncover detailed memory access patterns and cache behaviors, which are then utilized to optimize AES encryption implementations on GPUs. Our approach incorporates shared memory optimization strategies and parallelism techniques to achieve high throughput in AES encryption. Experimental results demonstrate that with optimized granularity and memory allocation, AES encryption on NVIDIA Pascal and Maxwell GPUs achieves throughputs up to 277 Gbps, significantly outperforming traditional implementations. This work provides a comprehensive framework for designing high-performance cryptographic accelerators on GPUs by integrating memory hierarchy insights with parallel algorithm design.

original_abstract: We present a novel classifier network called STEP, to classify perceived human emotion from gaits, based on a Spatial Temporal Graph Convolutional Network (ST-GCN) architecture. Given an RGB video of an individual walking, our formulation implicitly exploits the gait features to classify the emotional state of the human into one of four emotions: happy, sad, angry, or neutral. We use hundreds of annotated real-world gait videos and augment them with thousands of annotated synthetic gaits generated using a novel generative network called STEP-Gen, built on an ST-GCN based Conditional Variational Autoencoder (CVAE). We incorporate a novel push-pull regularization loss in the CVAE formulation of STEP-Gen to generate realistic gaits and improve the classification accuracy of STEP. We also release a novel dataset (E-Gait), which consists of $2,177$ human gaits annotated with perceived emotions along with thousands of synthetic gaits. In practice, STEP can learn the affective features and exhibits classification accuracy of 89% on E-Gait, which is 14 - 30% more accurate over prior methods.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel deep learning framework that integrates spectral graph convolutions, spatiotemporal residual networks, and motion-content decomposition for enhanced video generation and emotion recognition from human motion. By leveraging hierarchical clustering and graph Laplacian-based spectral methods, we extend convolutional architectures to efficiently model complex graph-structured data. Our approach incorporates spatiotemporal residual networks to capture both appearance and motion dynamics, while motion and content decomposition techniques enable precise control over video synthesis. Additionally, we apply covariance descriptors on the manifold of symmetric positive definite matrices to model emotional states from 3D body motion. The proposed framework demonstrates superior performance in video generation, action recognition, and emotion classification tasks, achieving state-of-the-art results on multiple benchmarks.

original_abstract: Coflow scheduling models communication requests in parallel computing frameworks where multiple data flows between shared resources need to be completed before computation can continue. In this paper, we introduce Path-based Coflow Scheduling, a generalized problem variant that considers coflows as collections of flows along fixed paths on general network topologies with node capacity restrictions. For this problem, we minimize the coflows' total weighted completion time. We show that flows on paths in the original network can be interpreted as hyperedges in a hypergraph and transform the path-based scheduling problem into an edge scheduling problem on this hypergraph. We present a $(2\lambda + 1)$-approximation algorithm when node capacities are set to one, where $\lambda$ is the maximum number of nodes in a path. For the special case of simultaneous release times for all flows, our result improves to a $(2\lambda)$-approximation. Furthermore, we generalize the result to arbitrary node constraints and obtain a $(2\lambda\Delta + 1)$- and a $(2\lambda\Delta)$-approximation in the case of general and zero release times, where $\Delta$ captures the capacity disparity between nodes.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel coflow scheduling framework that integrates advanced approximation algorithms with joint routing and bandwidth allocation strategies to minimize total weighted completion time in datacenter networks. Building on recent advances in asymptotically optimal approximation algorithms, improved linear programming formulations, and tight approximation bounds, we propose a unified approach that addresses both packet- and circuit-based coflows with and without pre-specified flow paths. Our method incorporates a randomized 2-approximation algorithm for general network topologies, an improved deterministic algorithm with approximation ratios of 5 and 4 for coflows with and without release dates, respectively, and a tight $(2+\epsilon)$-approximation for coflows with release times. Additionally, we integrate the CoRBA and CoRBA-fast algorithms to jointly optimize routing and bandwidth allocation, significantly reducing coflow completion times by up to 500% compared to existing methods. Experimental evaluations demonstrate that our approach achieves an average performance improvement of 22% over competing heuristics, with CoRBA-fast offering a practical, fast alternative with minimal performance degradation. This work provides a comprehensive and efficient solution for coflow scheduling in modern datacenter environments.

original_abstract: Differential Architecture Search (DARTS) is now a widely disseminated weight-sharing neural architecture search method. However, there are two fundamental weaknesses remain untackled. First, we observe that the well-known aggregation of skip connections during optimization is caused by an unfair advantage in an exclusive competition. Second, there is a non-negligible incongruence when discretizing continuous architectural weights to a one-hot representation. Because of these two reasons, DARTS delivers a biased solution that might not even be suboptimal. In this paper, we present a novel approach to curing both frailties. Specifically, as unfair advantages in a pure exclusive competition easily induce a monopoly, we relax the choice of operations to be collaborative, where we let each operation have an equal opportunity to develop its strength. We thus call our method Fair DARTS. Moreover, we propose a zero-one loss to directly reduce the discretization gap. Experiments are performed on two mainstream search spaces, in which we achieve new state-of-the-art networks on ImageNet. Our code is available on this https URL.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel and efficient framework for Neural Architecture Search (NAS) that integrates sequential model-based optimization, differentiable search strategies, and multinomial distribution learning to achieve state-of-the-art performance with significantly reduced computational cost. By combining the progressive search methodology of Progressive Neural Architecture Search with the differentiable relaxation of DARTS and the efficiency of Single-Path NAS, our approach enables the design of hardware-efficient convolutional networks with minimal search time. The proposed method employs a unified search space representation, a joint multinomial distribution for architecture sampling, and a dynamic pruning mechanism to enhance search stability and efficiency. Experiments on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet demonstrate that our framework achieves competitive classification accuracy while reducing search time by up to 5,000x compared to prior methods, making it highly suitable for large-scale and resource-constrained applications.

original_abstract: Deep neural networks form the basis of state-of-the-art models across a variety of application domains. Moreover, networks that are able to dynamically adapt the computational cost of inference are important in scenarios where the amount of compute or input data varies over time. In this paper, we propose Hierarchical Neural Ensembles (HNE), a novel framework to embed an ensemble of multiple networks by sharing intermediate layers using a hierarchical structure. In HNE we control the inference cost by evaluating only a subset of models, which are organized in a nested manner. Our second contribution is a novel co-distillation method to boost the performance of ensemble predictions with low inference cost. This approach leverages the nested structure of our ensembles, to optimally allocate accuracy and diversity across the ensemble members. Comprehensive experiments over the CIFAR and Ima-geNet datasets confirm the effectiveness of HNE in building deep networks with adaptive inference cost for image classification.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework that combines ensemble learning, adaptive inference, and efficient network design to achieve high accuracy with reduced computational cost. Building on diverse ensembling strategies, including parameter sharing via TreeNets and diversity-encouraging losses, we propose an end-to-end trainable system that dynamically selects and adapts network components during inference. Inspired by adaptive neural networks, we incorporate early exit mechanisms and network selection policies to minimize computation while maintaining accuracy. Additionally, we integrate network slimming and budgeted super networks to optimize model size, memory usage, and computational efficiency. Our approach demonstrates significant improvements in accuracy-efficiency trade-offs across multiple benchmark datasets, achieving state-of-the-art performance with reduced inference time and resource consumption.

original_abstract: There is great potential for damage from adversarial learning (AL) attacks on machine-learning based systems. In this paper, we provide a contemporary survey of AL, focused particularly on defenses against attacks on statistical classifiers. After introducing relevant terminology and the goals and range of possible knowledge of both attackers and defenders, we survey recent work on test-time evasion (TTE), data poisoning (DP), and reverse engineering (RE) attacks and particularly defenses against same. In so doing, we distinguish robust classification from anomaly detection (AD), unsupervised from supervised, and statistical hypothesis-based defenses from ones that do not have an explicit null (no attack) hypothesis; we identify the hyperparameters a particular method requires, its computational complexity, as well as the performance measures on which it was evaluated and the obtained quality. We then dig deeper, providing novel insights that challenge conventional AL wisdom and that target unresolved issues, including: 1) robust classification versus AD as a defense strategy; 2) the belief that attack success increases with attack strength, which ignores susceptibility to AD; 3) small perturbations for test-time evasion attacks: a fallacy or a requirement?; 4) validity of the universal assumption that a TTE attacker knows the ground-truth class for the example to be attacked; 5) black, grey, or white box attacks as the standard for defense evaluation; 6) susceptibility of query-based RE to an AD defense. We also discuss attacks on the privacy of training data. We then present benchmark comparisons of several defenses against TTE, RE, and backdoor DP attacks on images. The paper concludes with a discussion of future work.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework that combines robustness enhancement and adversarial detection techniques to address the vulnerability of deep neural networks (DNNs) to adversarial examples. Building on defensive distillation, which has been shown to be ineffective against advanced attacks, we propose an integrated approach that incorporates statistical detection methods and manifold-based adversarial example reconstruction. Our framework leverages the statistical properties of adversarial examples, as demonstrated by prior work, to identify and mitigate adversarial inputs through a detector network that approximates the manifold of normal examples. Additionally, we incorporate efficient defenses that reinforce the stability of DNN predictions against adversarial perturbations. Experimental results show that our method significantly improves robustness against a wide range of adversarial attacks, including universal perturbations and state-of-the-art targeted attacks, while maintaining high accuracy on clean data. The proposed approach is evaluated across multiple datasets and attack scenarios, demonstrating its effectiveness in both detection and mitigation of adversarial examples.

original_abstract: Object-based approaches for learning action-conditioned dynamics has demonstrated promise for generalization and interpretability. However, existing approaches suffer from structural limitations and optimization difficulties for common environments with multiple dynamic objects. In this paper, we present a novel self-supervised learning framework, called Multi-level Abstraction Object-oriented Predictor (MAOP), which employs a three-level learning architecture that enables efficient object-based dynamics learning from raw visual observations. We also design a spatial-temporal relational reasoning mechanism for MAOP to support instance-level dynamics learning and handle partial observability. Our results show that MAOP significantly outperforms previous methods in terms of sample efficiency and generalization over novel environments for learning environment models. We also demonstrate that learned dynamics models enable efficient planning in unseen environments, comparable to true environment models. In addition, MAOP learns semantically and visually interpretable disentangled representations.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework that combines object-centric visual predictive modeling, unsupervised learning of physical interactions, and compositional dynamics prediction to enable intelligent agents to plan and execute goal-directed actions in diverse and previously unseen environments. By integrating methods from visual interaction networks, relational neural expectation maximization, and object-oriented dynamics prediction, our approach learns interpretable, physics-based models directly from raw visual input without requiring labeled object information. The model decomposes scenes into latent object representations, predicts their future states through interaction-based dynamics, and generalizes across varying object layouts and novel environments. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our framework in simulating and planning complex physical interactions, such as billiards gameplay and robotic pushing tasks, using only unlabeled training data. Our results show that the combined model achieves superior generalization, accurate long-term trajectory prediction, and robust performance in real-world scenarios with unseen objects and configurations.

original_abstract: In this paper, we present work in progress on activity recognition and prediction in real homes using either binary sensor data or depth video data. We present our field trial and set-up for collecting and storing the data, our methods, and our current results. We compare the accuracy of predicting the next binary sensor event using probabilistic methods and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, include the time information to improve prediction accuracy, as well as predict both the next sensor event and its mean time of occurrence using one LSTM model. We investigate transfer learning between apartments and show that it is possible to pre-train the model with data from other apartments and achieve good accuracy in a new apartment straight away. In addition, we present preliminary results from activity recognition using low-resolution depth video data from seven apartments, and classify four activities - no movement, standing up, sitting down, and TV interaction - by using a relatively simple processing method where we apply an Infinite Impulse Response (IIR) filter to extract movements from the frames prior to feeding them to a convolutional LSTM network for the classification.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework that integrates spatiotemporal sequence modeling with sensor event prediction in smart home environments to enhance health monitoring for older adults. Drawing on the ConvLSTM architecture, originally developed for precipitation nowcasting, we adapt it to model complex spatiotemporal patterns in sensor data collected from a real-world smart home. The framework is combined with Bayesian network-based activity prediction and multiscale entropy analysis to improve the accuracy and robustness of event forecasting. Additionally, we incorporate high-resolution laser displacement sensors and 3D-printed structural models to simulate and validate the performance of the system under various conditions. The proposed approach is evaluated using real-world sensor data and demonstrates superior performance in predicting daily activities and detecting anomalies, offering a promising solution for independent aging and personalized health support.

original_abstract: Despite the recent progress in deep semi-supervised learning (Semi-SL), the amount of labels still plays a dominant role. The success in self-supervised learning (Self-SL) hints a promising direction to exploit the vast unlabeled data by leveraging an additional set of deterministic labels. In this paper, we propose Deep Self-Semi-Supervised learning (D$S^3$L), a flexible multi-task framework with shared parameters that integrates the rotation task in Self-SL with the consistency-based methods in deep Semi-SL. Our method is easy to implement and is complementary to all consistency-based approaches. The experiments demonstrate that our method significantly improves over the published state-of-the-art methods on several standard benchmarks, especially when fewer labels are presented.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework that combines semi-supervised learning with robust strategies for handling noisy labels, leveraging the strengths of Deep Co-Training, Temporal Ensembling, MentorNet, and dimensionality-driven learning. By integrating multiple views of data through co-training, we enhance model diversity and prevent collapse, while employing a dynamic curriculum learned by MentorNet to prioritize reliable samples during training. Additionally, we incorporate self-ensembling and label noise modeling techniques to improve consistency and robustness against incorrect labels. Our approach also adapts the loss function based on the dimensionality of the representation subspace, ensuring effective learning even with significant label noise. Experimental results on benchmark datasets such as CIFAR-10/100, SVHN, and ImageNet demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance in semi-supervised learning with noisy labels, significantly outperforming existing approaches.

original_abstract: We introduce natural adversarial examples -- real-world, unmodified, and naturally occurring examples that cause classifier accuracy to significantly degrade. We curate 7,500 natural adversarial examples and release them in an ImageNet classifier test set that we call ImageNet-A. This dataset serves as a new way to measure classifier robustness. Like l_p adversarial examples, ImageNet-A examples successfully transfer to unseen or black-box classifiers. For example, on ImageNet-A a DenseNet-121 obtains around 2% accuracy, an accuracy drop of approximately 90%. Recovering this accuracy is not simple because ImageNet-A examples exploit deep flaws in current classifiers including their over-reliance on color, texture, and background cues. We observe that popular training techniques for improving robustness have little effect, but we show that some architectural changes can enhance robustness to natural adversarial examples. Future research is required to enable robust generalization to this hard ImageNet test set.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to enhance the robustness of deep neural networks against adversarial examples by combining semantic adversarial example generation with feature denoising and global representation learning. Building on recent findings that adversarial examples are not easily detectable and that current defenses often fail under semantic perturbations, we propose a framework that integrates adversarial transformations based on color-space manipulation with feature denoising blocks to mitigate the impact of such attacks. Additionally, we incorporate a training strategy that penalizes local predictive power to encourage global, shape-based representations, improving generalization and robustness to both common corruptions and adversarial perturbations. Our experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate significant improvements in classification accuracy under adversarial and corrupted conditions, highlighting the effectiveness of combining semantic-aware adversarial training with robust feature learning.

original_abstract: We introduce a novel domain adaptation formulation from synthetic dataset (source domain) to real dataset (target domain) for the category of tasks with per-pixel predictions. The annotations of these tasks are relatively hard to acquire in the real world, such as single-view depth estimation or surface normal estimation. Our key idea is to introduce anchor tasks, whose annotations are (1) less expensive to acquire than the main task, such as facial landmarks and semantic segmentations; and (2) shared in availability for both synthetic and real datasets so that it serves as "anchor" between tasks; and finally (3) aligned spatially with main task annotations on a per-pixel basis so that it also serves as spatial anchor between tasks' outputs. To further utilize spatial alignment between the anchor and main tasks, we introduce a novel freeze approach that freezes the final layers of our network after training on the source domain so that spatial and contextual relationship between tasks are maintained when adapting on the target domain. We evaluate our methods on two pairs of datasets, performing surface normal estimation in indoor scenes and faces, using semantic segmentation and facial landmarks as anchor tasks separately. We show the importance of using anchor tasks in both synthetic and real domains, and that the freeze approach outperforms competing approaches, reaching results in facial images on par with the state-of-the-art system that leverages detailed facial appearance model.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel multi-task domain adaptation framework that combines attribute-based learning, cycle-consistent adversarial networks, and structured output adaptation to address the challenges of fine-grained object recognition in the wild. By leveraging annotated data from e-commerce and field guides, our approach adapts models to real-world scenarios with minimal labeled target data. The proposed method integrates a multi-task adaptation loss with discriminative patch representations and cycle-consistent domain adaptation to enhance feature alignment and task performance across domains. Experiments on a large-scale fine-grained dataset of car categories demonstrate significant improvements in accuracy, achieving a 19.1% performance gain in semi-supervised adaptation. Additionally, the framework is evaluated on semantic segmentation and cross-domain object detection tasks, showing robustness to domain shifts and superior performance over existing methods. The approach bridges the gap between synthetic and real-world data, enabling effective adaptation with minimal annotation effort.

original_abstract: Aggregating features in terms of different convolutional blocks or contextual embeddings has been proven to be an effective way to strengthen feature representations for semantic segmentation. However, most of the current popular network architectures tend to ignore the misalignment issues during the feature aggregation process caused by 1) step-by-step downsampling operations, and 2) indiscriminate contextual information fusion. In this paper, we explore the principles in addressing such feature misalignment issues and inventively propose Feature-Aligned Segmentation Networks (AlignSeg). AlignSeg consists of two primary modules, i.e., the Aligned Feature Aggregation (AlignFA) module and the Aligned Context Modeling (AlignCM) module. First, AlignFA adopts a simple learnable interpolation strategy to learn transformation offsets of pixels, which can effectively relieve the feature misalignment issue caused by multiresolution feature aggregation. Second, with the contextual embeddings in hand, AlignCM enables each pixel to choose private custom contextual information in an adaptive manner, making the contextual embeddings aligned better to provide appropriate guidance. We validate the effectiveness of our AlignSeg network with extensive experiments on Cityscapes and ADE20K, achieving new state-of-the-art mIoU scores of 82.6% and 45.95%, respectively. Our source code will be made available.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel semantic segmentation framework that integrates multi-scale context aggregation, global context encoding, and high-resolution refinement mechanisms to achieve state-of-the-art performance. Building on dilated convolutions for multi-scale feature extraction, atrous spatial pyramid pooling for contextual information, and the context encoding module for capturing global scene semantics, our approach further incorporates a refined encoder-decoder structure with residual connections to preserve spatial details. Additionally, we introduce an enhanced refinement mechanism inspired by RefineNet to recover high-resolution outputs while leveraging long-range dependencies. The proposed model demonstrates significant improvements in segmentation accuracy on benchmark datasets including PASCAL VOC 2012, PASCAL-Context, and ADE20K, achieving mIoU scores of 86.2%, 52.3%, and 0.561, respectively, with minimal additional computational overhead. The framework is validated through extensive experiments and is publicly available for further research and application.

original_abstract: The success of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) in computer vision applications has been accompanied by a significant increase of computation and memory costs, which prohibits its usage on resource-limited environments such as mobile or embedded devices. To this end, the research of CNN compression has recently become emerging. In this paper, we propose a novel filter pruning scheme, termed structured sparsity regularization (SSR), to simultaneously speedup the computation and reduce the memory overhead of CNNs, which can be well supported by various off-the-shelf deep learning libraries. Concretely, the proposed scheme incorporates two different regularizers of structured sparsity into the original objective function of filter pruning, which fully coordinates the global outputs and local pruning operations to adaptively prune filters. We further propose an Alternative Updating with Lagrange Multipliers (AULM) scheme to efficiently solve its optimization. AULM follows the principle of ADMM and alternates between promoting the structured sparsity of CNNs and optimizing the recognition loss, which leads to a very efficient solver (2.5x to the most recent work that directly solves the group sparsity-based regularization). Moreover, by imposing the structured sparsity, the online inference is extremely memory-light, since the number of filters and the output feature maps are simultaneously reduced. The proposed scheme has been deployed to a variety of state-of-the-art CNN structures including LeNet, AlexNet, VGG, ResNet and GoogLeNet over different datasets. Quantitative results demonstrate that the proposed scheme achieves superior performance over the state-of-the-art methods. We further demonstrate the proposed compression scheme for the task of transfer learning, including domain adaptation and object detection, which also show exciting performance gains over the state-of-the-arts.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework that combines filter-level pruning, structured sparsity, and network slimming techniques to achieve efficient and accurate deep neural network compression. By integrating global and dynamic filter pruning with channel-level sparsity enforcement, the proposed method enables simultaneous reduction in model size, computational operations, and memory footprint while maintaining high accuracy. The approach dynamically identifies and removes redundant filters across all layers, updates the saliency of pruned filters during training, and enforces structured sparsity to ensure compatibility with existing hardware and software infrastructures. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate significant improvements in efficiency, achieving up to 42% FLOPs reduction on ResNet-101 with minimal accuracy loss, and enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices without sacrificing performance.

original_abstract: In many real-time applications, the deployment of deep neural networks is constrained by high computational cost and efficient lightweight neural networks are widely concerned. In this paper, we propose that depthwise convolution (DWC) is used to expand the number of channels in a bottleneck block, which is more efficient than 1 x 1 convolution. The proposed Pointwise-Standard-Depthwise network (PSDNet) based on channel expansion with DWC has fewer number of parameters, less computational cost and higher accuracy than corresponding ResNet on CIFAR datasets. To design more efficient lightweight concolutional neural netwok, Depthwise-Pointwise-Depthwise inverted bottleneck block (DPD block) is proposed and DPDNet is designed by stacking DPD block. Meanwhile, the number of parameters of DPDNet is only about 60% of that of MobileNetV2 for networks with the same number of layers, but can achieve approximated accuracy. Additionally, two hyperparameters of DPDNet can make the trade-off between accuracy and computational cost, which makes DPDNet suitable for diverse tasks. Furthermore, we find the networks with more DWC layers outperform the networks with more 1x1 convolution layers, which indicates that extracting spatial information is more important than combining channel information.
generated_abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to building efficient and accurate deep convolutional neural networks by combining the strengths of deep architectures, channel pruning, and structured sparse kernel designs. Drawing on the success of very deep networks, we leverage residual learning to enable training of deeper models while maintaining computational efficiency. To reduce model complexity, we apply channel pruning techniques that iteratively remove redundant filters, significantly lowering the number of parameters and computational costs without sacrificing accuracy. Additionally, we integrate interleaved low-rank group convolutions to further enhance efficiency by combining structured sparsity with low-rank decomposition. Our experiments demonstrate that the proposed method achieves state-of-the-art performance on benchmark datasets such as ImageNet, CIFAR, and COCO, with substantial reductions in model size and inference time, making it highly suitable for deployment on resource-constrained systems.

original_abstract: Societal bias towards certain communities is a big problem that affects a lot of machine learning systems. This work aims at addressing the racial bias present in many modern gender recognition systems. We learn race invariant representations of human faces with an adversarially trained autoencoder model. We show that such representations help us achieve less biased performance in gender classification. We use variance in classification accuracy across different races as a surrogate for the racial bias of the model and achieve a drop of over 40% in variance with race invariant representations.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework that combines adversarial learning, attribute disentanglement, and bias mitigation techniques to address representation fairness and cross-modal translation in machine learning systems. Drawing on methods for adversarial representation learning, we develop a flexible model that minimizes sensitive attribute information in learned representations, ensuring fairness in decision-making and data anonymization. We integrate attribute disentanglement techniques to enable controlled manipulation of visual and textual attributes, allowing for intuitive user-driven modifications. Additionally, we incorporate corpus-level constraints and debiasing strategies to reduce gender and racial biases in both natural language processing and visual recognition tasks. Our approach is further extended to unsupervised cross-lingual translation using monolingual corpora only, demonstrating robust performance without parallel data. The proposed framework is evaluated across multiple domains, including sentiment analysis, image manipulation, and machine translation, showing significant improvements in fairness, bias reduction, and task performance.

original_abstract: While generalizing well over natural inputs, neural networks are vulnerable to adversarial inputs. Existing defenses against adversarial inputs have largely been detached from the real world. These defenses also come at a cost to accuracy. Fortunately, there are invariances of an object that are its salient features; when we break them it will necessarily change the perception of the object. We find that applying invariants to the classification task makes robustness and accuracy feasible together. Two questions follow: how to extract and model these invariances? and how to design a classification paradigm that leverages these invariances to improve the robustness accuracy trade-off? The remainder of the paper discusses solutions to the aformenetioned questions.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel defense framework that combines manifold-based detection, universal perturbation analysis, and robust optimization to address the vulnerability of deep learning systems to adversarial examples in both digital and physical domains. Building on prior work demonstrating the existence of universal perturbations and the limitations of obfuscated gradient defenses, we propose a two-pronged approach that leverages geometric properties of input data to distinguish adversarial samples from benign ones. Our method incorporates a reformer network inspired by MagNet, which reconstructs adversarial examples by projecting them back toward the data manifold, while also incorporating adversarial training techniques derived from robust optimization to improve model resilience. We evaluate our framework on multiple benchmark datasets and demonstrate its effectiveness against a wide range of attacks, including white-box, gray-box, and physical-world scenarios. Furthermore, we analyze the trade-off between robustness and standard accuracy, showing that our approach achieves a favorable balance by encouraging the model to learn more task-relevant features. Our results suggest that combining geometric and optimization-based defenses offers a promising direction for building more secure and reliable deep learning systems.

original_abstract: Recent advances in deep neural networks (DNNs) have led to object detectors that can rapidly process pictures or videos, and recognize the objects that they contain. Despite the promising progress by industrial manufacturers such as Amazon and Google in commercializing deep learning-based object detection as a standard computer vision service, object detection systems - similar to traditional software - may still produce incorrect results. These errors, in turn, can lead to severe negative outcomes for the users of these object detection systems. For instance, an autonomous driving system that fails to detect pedestrians can cause accidents or even fatalities. However, principled, systematic methods for testing object detection systems do not yet exist, despite their importance. #R##N#To fill this critical gap, we introduce the design and realization of MetaOD, the first metamorphic testing system for object detectors to effectively reveal erroneous detection results by commercial object detectors. To this end, we (1) synthesize natural-looking images by inserting extra object instances into background images, and (2) design metamorphic conditions asserting the equivalence of object detection results between the original and synthetic images after excluding the prediction results on the inserted objects. MetaOD is designed as a streamlined workflow that performs object extraction, selection, and insertion. Evaluated on four commercial object detection services and four pretrained models provided by the TensorFlow API, MetaOD found tens of thousands of detection defects in these object detectors. To further demonstrate the practical usage of MetaOD, we use the synthetic images that cause erroneous detection results to retrain the model. Our results show that the model performance is increased significantly, from an mAP score of 9.3 to an mAP score of 10.5.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework that combines real-time object detection with synthetic data generation to enhance detection performance in scenarios with limited labeled data. Building on the YOLO architecture for its speed and efficiency, we integrate domain randomization techniques to generate synthetic images that align with the feature representations learned by pre-trained deep networks. By leveraging the insights from recent works on synthetic data training and pre-trained image features, our approach freezes the feature extraction layers of a pre-trained network and trains only the detection layers using synthetically generated images. This method significantly reduces the dependency on large annotated datasets while maintaining high detection accuracy. Experimental results on standard benchmarks demonstrate that our framework achieves competitive performance compared to state-of-the-art detectors, while offering flexibility in training with minimal real-world data. The proposed approach bridges the reality gap by ensuring synthetic images are optimized for detector-specific features, enabling robust and efficient object detection across diverse environments.

original_abstract: Despite recent impressive results on single-object and single-domain image generation, the generation of complex scenes with multiple objects remains challenging. In this paper, we start with the idea that a model must be able to understand individual objects and relationships between objects in order to generate complex scenes well. Our layout-to-image-generation method, which we call Object-Centric Generative Adversarial Network (or OC-GAN), relies on a novel Scene-Graph Similarity Module (SGSM). The SGSM learns representations of the spatial relationships between objects in the scene, which lead to our model's improved layout-fidelity. We also propose changes to the conditioning mechanism of the generator that enhance its object instance-awareness. Apart from improving image quality, our contributions mitigate two failure modes in previous approaches: (1) spurious objects being generated without corresponding bounding boxes in the layout, and (2) overlapping bounding boxes in the layout leading to merged objects in images. Extensive quantitative evaluation and ablation studies demonstrate the impact of our contributions, with our model outperforming previous state-of-the-art approaches on both the COCO-Stuff and Visual Genome datasets. Finally, we address an important limitation of evaluation metrics used in previous works by introducing SceneFID -- an object-centric adaptation of the popular Fr{e}chet Inception Distance metric, that is better suited for multi-object images.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for controllable and high-fidelity text-to-image synthesis by integrating attention mechanisms, scene graph reasoning, and layout-based generation. Building on attentional GANs, scene graph processing, and layout-aware image generation, our approach enables fine-grained control over object placement, appearance, and relationships through a multi-stage pipeline. The model first parses text descriptions into scene graphs, then generates spatial layouts using graph convolution and bounding box prediction, and finally synthesizes realistic images with a cascaded refinement network enhanced by object-driven attention and disentangled semantics. A semi-parametric strategy is employed to incorporate pre-defined object crops, ensuring visual consistency and diversity. The framework is trained with a combination of adversarial losses, layout consistency terms, and semantic matching objectives. Extensive experiments on Visual Genome and COCO-Stuff demonstrate significant improvements in Inception Score, Diversity Score, and Frechet Inception Distance, outperforming state-of-the-art methods while supporting interactive and incremental image generation based on scene graphs.

original_abstract: We present a novel approach to tackle domain adaptation between synthetic and real data. Instead, of employing "blind" domain randomization, i.e., augmenting synthetic renderings with random backgrounds or changing illumination and colorization, we leverage the task network as its own adversarial guide toward useful augmentations that maximize the uncertainty of the output. To this end, we design a min-max optimization scheme where a given task competes against a special deception network to minimize the task error subject to the specific constraints enforced by the deceiver. The deception network samples from a family of differentiable pixel-level perturbations and exploits the task architecture to find the most destructive augmentations. Unlike GAN-based approaches that require unlabeled data from the target domain, our method achieves robust mappings that scale well to multiple target distributions from source data alone. We apply our framework to the tasks of digit recognition on enhanced MNIST variants, classification and object pose estimation on the Cropped LineMOD dataset as well as semantic segmentation on the Cityscapes dataset and compare it to a number of domain adaptation approaches, thereby demonstrating similar results with superior generalization capabilities.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel domain adaptation framework for semantic segmentation that combines adversarial learning, geometric guidance, and privileged information from simulation to address cross-domain generalization challenges. Building on recent advances in unsupervised domain adaptation, we propose a method that leverages synthetic data enriched with geometric information to bridge the domain gap between synthetic and real-world images. Our approach incorporates a dual-level adaptation strategy: on the input side, we enhance image translation networks with geometric cues to generate realistic-style images, while on the output side, we jointly perform semantic segmentation and depth estimation with adversarial training to preserve the correlation between depth and semantics. Additionally, we integrate privileged information from simulators, such as depth maps, to guide the adaptation process and improve feature alignment. The proposed method is evaluated on multiple synthetic-to-real datasets, including Virtual KITTI to KITTI and SYNTHIA to Cityscapes, achieving significant performance improvements over existing methods that rely solely on semantic labels or adversarial objectives. Our results demonstrate the effectiveness of combining geometric information, adversarial learning, and simulation-based privileged data for robust cross-domain semantic segmentation.

original_abstract: Humans can only interact with part of the surrounding environment due to biological restrictions. Therefore, we learn to reason the spatial relationships across a series of observations to piece together the surrounding environment. Inspired by such behavior and the fact that machines also have computational constraints, we propose \underline{CO}nditional \underline{CO}ordinate GAN (COCO-GAN) of which the generator generates images by parts based on their spatial coordinates as the condition. On the other hand, the discriminator learns to justify realism across multiple assembled patches by global coherence, local appearance, and edge-crossing continuity. Despite the full images are never generated during training, we show that COCO-GAN can produce \textbf{state-of-the-art-quality} full images during inference. We further demonstrate a variety of novel applications enabled by teaching the network to be aware of coordinates. First, we perform extrapolation to the learned coordinate manifold and generate off-the-boundary patches. Combining with the originally generated full image, COCO-GAN can produce images that are larger than training samples, which we called "beyond-boundary generation". We then showcase panorama generation within a cylindrical coordinate system that inherently preserves horizontally cyclic topology. On the computation side, COCO-GAN has a built-in divide-and-conquer paradigm that reduces memory requisition during training and inference, provides high-parallelism, and can generate parts of images on-demand.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework that combines conditional generative adversarial networks (cGANs) with projection discriminators, spectral normalization, and progressive growing techniques to achieve high-resolution, semantically controlled image synthesis and manipulation. By incorporating conditional information through a projection-based discriminator, we enhance the fidelity of class-conditional image generation. Spectral normalization is applied to stabilize training, while progressive growing enables the generation of high-resolution images with unprecedented quality and diversity. Additionally, we extend the framework to support interactive semantic editing through object instance segmentation and parametric transformations, allowing for dynamic manipulation of image content. Our approach achieves state-of-the-art results on multiple benchmark datasets, demonstrating superior performance in both image synthesis and editing tasks.

original_abstract: Modeling relations between languages can offer understanding of language characteristics and uncover similarities and differences between languages. Automated methods applied to large textual corpora can be seen as opportunities for novel statistical studies of language development over time, as well as for improving cross-lingual natural language processing techniques. In this work, we first propose how to represent textual data as a directed, weighted network by the text2net algorithm. We next explore how various fast, network-topological metrics, such as network community structure, can be used for cross-lingual comparisons. In our experiments, we employ eight different network topology metrics, and empirically showcase on a parallel corpus, how the methods can be used for modeling the relations between nine selected languages. We demonstrate that the proposed method scales to large corpora consisting of hundreds of thousands of aligned sentences on an of-the-shelf laptop. We observe that on the one hand properties such as communities, capture some of the known differences between the languages, while others can be seen as novel opportunities for linguistic studies.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework that integrates persistent topology, graph embedding, and multilingual language representations to explore the structural and typological properties of world languages. Building on persistent homology analysis of syntactic parameters, we extend the investigation to incorporate network representation learning techniques, enabling the embedding of linguistic data into low-dimensional spaces while preserving both syntactic and typological features. Using SuperPivot, we analyze tense typology across over 1000 languages, leveraging multilingual corpora and BERT-based language representations to uncover correlations between structural similarity and embedding space proximity. Our approach reveals how persistent homology generators in language families like Indo-European and Niger-Congo relate to broader network structures and typological patterns, while also demonstrating the utility of graph embedding methods in capturing linguistic relationships. This work bridges computational linguistics, network science, and topological data analysis, offering new insights into the interplay between language structure, evolution, and representation.

original_abstract: Long Short-Term Memory Recurrent Neural Networks (LSTM-RNN) are one of the most powerful dynamic classifiers publicly known. The network itself and the related learning algorithms are reasonably well documented to get an idea how it works. This paper will shed more light into understanding how LSTM-RNNs evolved and why they work impressively well, focusing on the early, ground-breaking publications. We significantly improved documentation and fixed a number of errors and inconsistencies that accumulated in previous publications. To support understanding we as well revised and unified the notation used.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel end-to-end speech recognition system that integrates attention-based mechanisms with advanced recurrent neural network architectures to improve performance on long and variable-length utterances. Building on the success of attention-based models in machine translation and speech recognition, we incorporate location-aware attention and a Clockwork RNN (CW-RNN) to enhance temporal modeling and robustness to long input sequences. Additionally, we employ a Grid LSTM architecture to better capture multidimensional dependencies in speech signals. The proposed system is evaluated on the TIMIT phoneme recognition task, achieving a phoneme error rate of 17.6%, demonstrating significant improvements over previous attention-based models and establishing a new benchmark for robust and scalable speech recognition.

original_abstract: Non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) has been considered as a study-item in 3GPP for 5G new radio (NR). However, it was decided not to continue with it as a work-item, and to leave it for possible use in beyond 5G. In this paper, we first review the discussions that ended in such decision. Particularly, we present simulation comparisons between the NOMA and multi-user multiple-input-multiple-output (MU-MIMO), where the possible gain of NOMA, compared to MU-MIMO, is negligible. Then, we propose a number of methods to reduce the implementation complexity and delay of both uplink (UL) and downlink (DL) NOMA-based transmission, as different ways to improve its efficiency. Here, particular attention is paid to reducing the receiver complexity, the cost of hybrid automatic repeat request as well as the user pairing complexity. As demonstrated, different smart techniques can be applied to improve the energy efficiency and the end-to-end transmission delay of NOMA-based systems.
generated_abstract: This paper presents a novel framework that integrates dynamic user clustering, power allocation, signal alignment, and low-complexity iterative detection techniques to enhance the performance of non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) in both uplink and downlink MIMO systems. By leveraging the channel gain differences among users, a sub-optimal user grouping scheme is proposed to optimize cluster formation, while closed-form power allocation solutions are derived to maximize system throughput under SIC and power constraints. A signal alignment-based MIMO-NOMA framework is introduced to improve spectral efficiency and manage interference in multi-cell environments. Furthermore, a capacity-approaching iterative LMMSE detection method is employed, which is matched with irregular repeat-accumulate codes to achieve near-optimal performance with low complexity. The proposed framework is validated through simulations, demonstrating significant improvements in throughput, fairness, and robustness under various channel conditions and system loads, making it a promising solution for future 5G and beyond networks.

original_abstract: Over the past 15 years, the volume, richness and quality of data collected from the combined social networking platforms has increased beyond all expectation, providing researchers from a variety of disciplines to use it in their research. Perhaps more impactfully, it has provided the foundation for a range of new products and services, transforming industries such as advertising and marketing, as well as bringing the challenges of sharing personal data into the public consciousness. But how to make sense of the ever-increasing volume of big social data so that we can better understand and improve the user experience in increasingly complex, data-driven digital systems. This link with usability and the user experience of data-driven system bridges into the wider field of HCI, attracting interdisciplinary researchers as we see the demand for consumer technologies, software and systems, as well as the integration of social networks into our everyday lives. The fact that the data largely posted on social networks tends to be textual, provides a further link to linguistics, psychology and psycholinguistics to better understand the relationship between human behaviours offline and online. #R##N#In this thesis, we present a novel conceptual framework based on a complex digital system using collected longitudinal datasets to predict system status based on the personality traits and emotions extracted from text posted by users. The system framework was built using a dataset collected from an online scholarship system in which 2000 students had their digital behaviour and social network behaviour collected for this study. We contextualise this research project with a wider review and critical analysis of the current psycholinguistics, artificial intelligence and human-computer interaction literature, which reveals a gap of mapping and understanding digital profiling against system status.
generated_abstract: This paper presents a novel framework that integrates emotion detection, personality recognition, and opinion analysis to enhance user-centered modeling in digital environments. Drawing on advances in natural language processing and machine learning, the approach combines techniques for identifying emotional tone, personality traits, and product opinions from textual data, including social media and online reviews. By leveraging large-scale datasets and open-vocabulary methods, the framework enables more accurate modeling of user behavior, sentiment, and personality, which can be used to improve user experience design, personalized recommendations, and social network analysis. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the integrated model in capturing complex user interactions and providing deeper insights into human behavior across diverse digital platforms.

original_abstract: Unsupervised domain adaptation aims to transfer knowledge from a source domain to a target domain so that the target domain data can be recognized without any explicit labelling information for this domain. One limitation of the problem setting is that testing data, despite having no labels, from the target domain is needed during training, which prevents the trained model being directly applied to classify unseen test instances. We formulate a new cross-domain classification problem arising from real-world scenarios where labelled data is available for a subset of classes (known classes) in the target domain, and we expect to recognize new samples belonging to any class (known and unseen classes) once the model is learned. This is a generalized zero-shot learning problem where the side information comes from the source domain in the form of labelled samples instead of class-level semantic representations commonly used in traditional zero-shot learning. We present a unified domain adaptation framework for both unsupervised and zero-shot learning conditions. Our approach learns a joint subspace from source and target domains so that the projections of both data in the subspace can be domain invariant and easily separable. We use the supervised locality preserving projection (SLPP) as the enabling technique and conduct experiments under both unsupervised and zero-shot learning conditions, achieving state-of-the-art results on three domain adaptation benchmark datasets: Office-Caltech, Office31 and Office-Home.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel deep domain adaptation framework that integrates domain invariance, discriminative feature learning, and transferable representation alignment to address challenges in unsupervised and semi-supervised cross-domain adaptation. Building on recent advances in adversarial learning, joint distribution alignment, and residual transfer networks, our approach combines an adaptation layer with domain confusion loss, joint maximum mean discrepancy (JMMD) for distribution alignment, and instance- and center-based discriminative feature learning to enhance both domain invariance and classification performance. Additionally, we incorporate a soft label distribution matching loss to facilitate simultaneous transfer across domains and tasks, even with limited labeled target data. The proposed method is implemented through an augmented neural network architecture that enables efficient training via backpropagation. Extensive experiments on standard benchmark datasets demonstrate that our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance, outperforming existing methods in both visual domain adaptation and cross-modality classification tasks.

original_abstract: The aim of this work is learning to reshape the object in an input image to an arbitrary new shape, by just simply providing a single reference image with an object instance in the desired shape. We propose a new Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) architecture for such an object reshaping problem, named ReshapeGAN. The network can be tailored for handling all kinds of problem settings, including both within-domain (or single-dataset) reshaping and cross-domain (typically across mutiple datasets) reshaping, with paired or unpaired training data. The appearance of the input object is preserved in all cases, and thus it is still identifiable after reshaping, which has never been achieved as far as we are aware. We present the tailored models of the proposed ReshapeGAN for all the problem settings, and have them tested on 8 kinds of reshaping tasks with 13 different datasets, demonstrating the ability of ReshapeGAN on generating convincing and superior results for object reshaping. To the best of our knowledge, we are the first to be able to make one GAN framework work on all such object reshaping tasks, especially the cross-domain tasks on handling multiple diverse datasets. We present here both ablation studies on our proposed ReshapeGAN models and comparisons with the state-of-the-art models when they are made comparable, using all kinds of applicable metrics that we are aware of.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework that combines conditional generative adversarial networks (cGANs), deep convolutional GANs (DCGANs), and adversarial feature learning to enable high-resolution, semantically controlled image synthesis and interactive manipulation. Building on the ability of cGANs to generate realistic images from semantic label maps and the unsupervised representation learning capabilities of DCGANs, we propose an enhanced multi-scale architecture with a novel adversarial loss function to improve synthesis quality and resolution. Additionally, inspired by bidirectional GANs, we incorporate object instance segmentation and inverse mapping capabilities to allow for interactive editing of generated images, such as object removal, addition, and category modification. Our approach also supports diverse outputs from the same input, enabling user-driven appearance editing. Evaluation through human studies demonstrates significant improvements in both visual quality and resolution compared to existing methods, showcasing the potential of this integrated framework for advanced image synthesis and manipulation tasks.

original_abstract: Recent success of machine learning in many domains has been overwhelming, which often leads to false expectations regarding the capabilities of behavior learning in robotics. In this survey, we analyze the current state of machine learning for robotic behaviors. We will give a broad overview of behaviors that have been learned and used on real robots. Our focus is on kinematically or sensorially complex robots. That includes humanoid robots or parts of humanoid robots, for example, legged robots or robotic arms. We will classify presented behaviors according to various categories and we will draw conclusions about what can be learned and what should be learned. Furthermore, we will give an outlook on problems that are challenging today but might be solved by machine learning in the future and argue that classical robotics and other approaches from artificial intelligence should be integrated more with machine learning to form complete, autonomous systems.
generated_abstract: This paper presents a novel end-to-end learning framework that integrates perception, control, and decision-making for complex robotic manipulation tasks. Drawing on recent advances in deep reinforcement learning, visuomotor policy training, and hand-eye coordination, the approach enables robots to learn dexterous in-hand manipulation, real-time grasping, and autonomous navigation through large-scale data collection and simulation-to-reality transfer. By combining deep convolutional networks with reinforcement learning algorithms that support asynchronous off-policy updates and natural policy gradients, the framework achieves robust performance on high-dimensional manipulation tasks, including object reorientation, door opening, and multi-fingered grasping. The method is evaluated on both simulated and real-world robotic platforms, demonstrating effective generalization across novel objects, environments, and robot morphologies, while reducing reliance on human demonstrations and hand-engineered components.

original_abstract: We present a novel deep neural network architecture for end-to-end scene flow estimation that directly operates on large-scale 3D point clouds. Inspired by Bilateral Convolutional Layers (BCL), we propose novel DownBCL, UpBCL, and CorrBCL operations that restore structural information from unstructured point clouds, and fuse information from two consecutive point clouds. Operating on discrete and sparse permutohedral lattice points, our architectural design is parsimonious in computational cost. Our model can efficiently process a pair of point cloud frames at once with a maximum of 86K points per frame. Our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance on the FlyingThings3D and KITTI Scene Flow 2015 datasets. Moreover, trained on synthetic data, our approach shows great generalization ability on real-world data and on different point densities without fine-tuning.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel deep learning framework that integrates spectral convolutional networks, sparse convolutional operations, and hierarchical feature learning to address complex tasks in 3D shape segmentation and scene flow estimation. Building on recent advances in graph-structured data processing, we extend spectral networks with graph estimation procedures to handle irregular 3D point cloud data. Our approach incorporates submanifold sparse convolutions and permutohedral lattice-based operations to efficiently process sparse and non-uniform data, while leveraging hierarchical architectures inspired by PointNet++ and SyncSpecCNN to capture multi-scale features. Additionally, we adapt the concept of synchronized spectral convolutions and spatial pyramid networks to enable accurate and efficient estimation of scene flow from 3D point clouds. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our framework achieves state-of-the-art performance in 3D semantic segmentation and scene flow estimation, while maintaining computational efficiency and robustness to varying data densities.

original_abstract: Detecting adversarial examples currently stands as one of the biggest challenges in the field of deep learning. Adversarial attacks, which produce adversarial examples, increase the prediction likelihood of a target class for a particular data point. During this process, the adversarial example can be further optimized, even when it has already been wrongly classified with 100% confidence, thus making the adversarial example even more difficult to detect. For this kind of adversarial examples, which we refer to as over-optimized adversarial examples, we discovered that the logits of the model provide solid clues on whether the data point at hand is adversarial or genuine. In this context, we first discuss the masking effect of the softmax function for the prediction made and explain why the logits of the model are more useful in detecting over-optimized adversarial examples. To identify this type of adversarial examples in practice, we propose a non-parametric and computationally efficient method which relies on interquartile range, with this method becoming more effective as the image resolution increases. We support our observations throughout the paper with detailed experiments for different datasets (MNIST, CIFAR-10, and ImageNet) and several architectures.
generated_abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to enhancing the robustness of deep neural networks (DNNs) against adversarial examples by combining adversarial training with advanced attack algorithms and detection circumvention techniques. Building on prior work that demonstrates the vulnerability of DNNs to adversarial examples in both digital and physical domains, we propose a scalable adversarial training framework inspired by large-scale applications on ImageNet. Our method incorporates insights from recent studies that reveal the limitations of defensive distillation, obfuscated gradients, and softmax-based evaluation of adversarial strength, which have been shown to provide a false sense of security. We demonstrate that adversarial examples generated using DeepFool and other state-of-the-art methods can be effectively used in adversarial training to improve model robustness. Furthermore, we address the issue of adversarial transferability and show that single-step attacks are more effective for black-box scenarios. Our experiments also highlight the importance of evaluating defenses using high-confidence adversarial examples and show that existing detection methods can be bypassed with tailored loss functions. Finally, we propose a predictive distance measure to assess the vulnerability of input samples to adversarial perturbations, offering a new perspective for evaluating and improving the security of DNNs in adversarial settings.

original_abstract: Generative adversarial networks conditioned on simple textual image descriptions are capable of generating realistic-looking images. However, current methods still struggle to generate images based on complex image captions from a heterogeneous domain. Furthermore, quantitatively evaluating these text-to-image synthesis models is still challenging, as most evaluation metrics only judge image quality but not the conformity between the image and its caption. To address the aforementioned challenges we introduce both a new model that explicitly models individual objects within an image and a new evaluation metric called Semantic Object Accuracy (SOA) that specifically evaluates images given an image caption. Our model adds an object pathway to both the generator and the discriminator to explicitly learn features of individual objects. The SOA uses a pre-trained object detector to evaluate if a generated image contains objects that are specifically mentioned in the image caption, e.g. whether an image generated from "a car driving down the street" contains a car. Our evaluation shows that models which explicitly model individual objects outperform models which only model global image characteristics. However, the SOA also shows that despite this increased performance current models still struggle to generate images that contain realistic objects of multiple different domains.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for controllable and semantically aligned text-to-image synthesis by integrating hierarchical layout inference, scene graph reasoning, and region-phrase attention mechanisms. Building on recent advances in semantic layout generation, adversarial training, and controllable image synthesis, our approach decomposes the generation process into a multi-stage pipeline: first, a semantic layout is inferred from text using a coarse-to-fine object bounding box generator; second, a scene graph is constructed to explicitly model object relationships and spatial arrangements; and finally, a region-phrase attention-based generator synthesizes high-resolution images while maintaining semantic consistency with the input text. To enhance realism and controllability, we incorporate a hierarchically nested adversarial network and a visual-semantic similarity measure for feedback. Additionally, a crop refinement network and object-image fuser are introduced to allow fine-grained manipulation of object appearances and interactions. Extensive experiments on Visual Genome, COCO-Stuff, and MS-COCO demonstrate that our method significantly improves image quality, semantic alignment, and diversity compared to existing approaches, while enabling user-controlled generation through layout and scene graph modifications.

original_abstract: We present a method for optimal coordination of multiple vehicle teams when multiple endpoint configurations are equally desirable, such as seen in the autonomous assembly of formation flight. The individual vehicles' positions in the formation are not assigned a priori and a key challenge is to find the optimal configuration assignment along with the optimal control and trajectory. Commonly, assignment and trajectory planning problems are solved separately. We introduce a new multi-vehicle coordination paradigm, where the optimal goal assignment and optimal vehicle trajectories are found simultaneously from a viscosity solution of a single Hamilton-Jacobi (HJ) partial differential equation (PDE), which provides a necessary and sufficient condition for global optimality. Intrinsic in this approach is that individual vehicle dynamic models need not be the same, and therefore can be applied to heterogeneous systems. Numerical methods to solve the HJ equation have historically relied on a discrete grid of the solution space and exhibits exponential scaling with system dimension, preventing their applicability to multiple vehicle systems. By utilizing a generalization of the Hopf formula, we avoid the use of grids and present a method that exhibits polynomial scaling in the number of vehicles.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach for time-optimal trajectory planning of heterogeneous multi-vehicle systems in dynamic environments, combining sequential path planning with online sensing and adaptive control. By leveraging the double-obstacle Hamilton-Jacobi-Isaacs variational inequality, we enable safe sequential planning for vehicles with varying dynamics and asymmetric collision constraints, while incorporating time-delay compensation through a level set approach. The generalized Hopf formula is used to efficiently solve high-dimensional Hamilton-Jacobi equations without grid-based discretization, allowing for polynomial-time complexity scaling. Additionally, we integrate optimal task assignment with trajectory planning using a conflict-based search framework, enabling joint optimization of path and task allocation for large heterogeneous robot teams. The proposed method demonstrates scalability, computational efficiency, and robustness in complex, real-time scenarios.

original_abstract: In contrast to the literature where local patterns in 3D point clouds are captured by customized convolutional operators, in this paper we study the problem of how to effectively and efficiently project such point clouds into a 2D image space so that traditional 2D convolutional neural networks (CNNs) such as U-Net can be applied for segmentation. To this end, we are motivated by graph drawing and reformulate it as an integer programming problem to learn the topology-preserving graph-to-grid mapping for each individual point cloud. To accelerate the computation in practice, we further propose a novel hierarchical approximate algorithm. With the help of the Delaunay triangulation for graph construction from point clouds and a multi-scale U-Net for segmentation, we manage to demonstrate the state-of-the-art performance on ShapeNet and PartNet, respectively, with significant improvement over the literature. Code is available at https://github.com/Zhang-VISLab.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel neural network architecture for efficient and effective processing of 3D point clouds by integrating advanced convolutional mechanisms and graph-based operations. Building on recent advances such as EdgeConv, kernel correlation, spherical kernels, annular convolution, and dense contextual representations, our approach combines the strengths of local geometric feature extraction, hierarchical spatial reasoning, and permutation-invariant processing. The proposed architecture employs dynamic graph convolution, point-set kernels, and annular convolution to capture fine-grained local structures and global shape properties, while leveraging dense connections to aggregate multi-scale contextual information. Additionally, an octree-guided framework is incorporated to handle sparse and irregular point distributions efficiently.
