MPN has three key advantages: 1) it does not need to conduct body part detection in the inference stage; 2) its model is very compact and efficient for both training and testing; 3) in the training stage, it requires only coarse priors of body part locations, which are easy to obtain. Systematic experiments on four large-scale ReID databases demonstrate that MPN consistently outperforms state-of-the-art approaches by significant margins.
generated_abstract: This paper presents a novel framework for person re-identification (Re-ID) that integrates advanced alignment strategies, context-aware feature learning, and part-based representation to address challenges posed by pose variations, occlusions, and misaligned detections. Building on recent advances in pedestrian alignment networks, context-aware feature extraction, and part-based deep learning, we propose a unified model that combines foreground attention mechanisms, deformable part localization, and semantically aligned feature fusion. Our approach leverages a two-stream architecture with a main full-image stream and a guiding stream for dense semantic alignment, while incorporating a part-aligned bilinear pooling layer to enhance discriminative power. Additionally, a symmetric triplet loss and part loss are employed to optimize feature learning across both global and local body regions. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets, including Market-1501, CUHK03, and DukeMTMC-ReID, demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance, significantly outperforming existing approaches in terms of rank-1 accuracy and mean average precision.

original_abstract: Statistical language modeling techniques have successfully been applied to source code, yielding a variety of new software development tools, such as tools for code suggestion and improving readability. A major issue with these techniques is that code introduces new vocabulary at a far higher rate than natural language, as new identifier names proliferate. But traditional language models limit the vocabulary to a fixed set of common words. For code, this strong assumption has been shown to have a significant negative effect on predictive performance. But the open vocabulary version of the neural network language models for code have not been introduced in the literature. We present a new open-vocabulary neural language model for code that is not limited to a fixed vocabulary of identifier names. We employ a segmentation into subword units, subsequences of tokens chosen based on a compression criterion, following previous work in machine translation. Our network achieves best in class performance, outperforming even the state-of-the-art methods of Hellendoorn and Devanbu that are designed specifically to model code. Furthermore, we present a simple method for dynamically adapting the model to a new test project, resulting in increased performance. We showcase our methodology on code corpora in three different languages of over a billion tokens each, hundreds of times larger than in previous work. To our knowledge, this is the largest neural language model for code that has been reported.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for intelligent code completion and summarization that integrates attention mechanisms, pointer networks, and deep contextualized representations. Drawing from advances in neural machine translation, convolutional attention networks, and deep language modeling, our approach addresses the challenges of handling long-range dependencies, out-of-vocabulary words, and context-sensitive code elements. By combining a convolutional attention module for detecting local and topical features with a pointer mixture network for efficient OoV word prediction, we enhance the model's ability to generate accurate and contextually relevant code summaries and completions. Additionally, we incorporate deep contextualized word representations to capture the nuanced semantics of code. Experimental results on Java and C# codebases demonstrate significant improvements in both code completion accuracy and summarization quality compared to existing methods, highlighting the effectiveness of our integrated approach in real-world software development tasks.

original_abstract: This paper contributes to the challenge of learning a function on streamed multimodal data through evaluation. The core of the result of our paper is the combination of two quite different approaches to this problem. One comes from the mathematically principled technology of signatures and log-signatures as representations for streamed data, while the other draws on the techniques of recurrent neural networks (RNN). The ability of the former to manage high sample rate streams and the latter to manage large scale nonlinear interactions allows hybrid algorithms that are easy to code, quicker to train, and of lower complexity for a given accuracy. #R##N#We illustrate the approach by approximating the unknown functional as a controlled differential equation. Linear functionals on solutions of controlled differential equations are the natural universal class of functions on data streams. Following this approach, we propose a hybrid Logsig-RNN algorithm that learns functionals on streamed data. By testing on various datasets, i.e. synthetic data, NTU RGB+D 120 skeletal action data, and Chalearn2013 gesture data, our algorithm achieves the outstanding accuracy with superior efficiency and robustness.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for skeleton-based human action and gesture recognition by integrating path signature features with attention mechanisms and temporal modeling strategies. Building on the path signature methodology for encoding spatial and temporal dynamics, we propose a multi-stream architecture that extracts spatial path signatures from joint correlations within frames and temporal path signatures from the evolution of these features across frames. To enhance discriminative power, we incorporate a global context-aware attention LSTM network that selectively focuses on informative joints and employs a recurrent attention mechanism for improved temporal modeling. Additionally, a temporal transformer module is introduced to capture fine-grained temporal variations without relying on recurrent strategies. The framework is further augmented with a co-occurrence feature learning approach to model joint dependencies and a clip-based representation to capture spatial configurations. Experimental results on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves state-of-the-art performance in both action and gesture recognition tasks, with high computational efficiency and strong interpretability.

original_abstract: Attempts from different disciplines to provide a fundamental understanding of deep learning have advanced rapidly in recent years, yet a unified framework remains relatively limited. In this article, we provide one possible way to align existing branches of deep learning theory through the lens of dynamical system and optimal control. By viewing deep neural networks as discrete-time nonlinear dynamical systems, we can analyze how information propagates through layers using mean field theory. When optimization algorithms are further recast as controllers, the ultimate goal of training processes can be formulated as an optimal control problem. In addition, we can reveal convergence and generalization properties by studying the stochastic dynamics of optimization algorithms. This viewpoint features a wide range of theoretical study from information bottleneck to statistical physics. It also provides a principled way for hyper-parameter tuning when optimal control theory is introduced. Our framework fits nicely with supervised learning and can be extended to other learning problems, such as Bayesian learning, adversarial training, and specific forms of meta learning, without efforts. The review aims to shed lights on the importance of dynamics and optimal control when developing deep learning theory.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel optimization framework for deep neural networks that combines insights from partial differential equations (PDEs), stochastic control, and entropy-based regularization. By interpreting training as a stochastic control problem, we derive a PDE-based algorithm that improves upon stochastic gradient descent (SGD) by leveraging the geometry of the energy landscape. The method incorporates entropy regularization to bias optimization towards wide, generalizable minima, avoiding sharp valleys associated with poor generalization. We establish theoretical guarantees for convergence and stability, showing that the algorithm achieves global minima in polynomial time for over-parameterized networks with ReLU activations. Empirical results on convolutional and recurrent networks demonstrate improved generalization and training efficiency compared to state-of-the-art methods. This work bridges the gap between continuous optimization theory and practical deep learning, offering a principled approach to training deep models with better convergence and generalization properties.

original_abstract: I review unsupervised or self-supervised neural networks playing minimax games in game-theoretic settings. (i) Adversarial Curiosity (AC, 1990) is based on two such networks. One network learns to probabilistically generate outputs, the other learns to predict effects of the outputs. Each network minimizes the objective function maximized by the other. (ii) Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs, 2010-2014) are an application of AC where the effect of an output is 1 if the output is in a given set, and 0 otherwise. (iii) Predictability Minimization (PM, 1990s) models data distributions through a neural encoder that maximizes the objective function minimized by a neural predictor of the code components. We correct a previously published claim that PM is not based on a minimax game.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework that combines conditional generative adversarial networks (cGANs), deep convolutional GANs (DCGANs), and adversarial feature learning to enable unsupervised representation learning and interpretable generative modeling. By integrating the bidirectional learning capabilities of BiGANs with the information-maximizing principles of InfoGAN, the proposed model learns disentangled and semantically meaningful representations from unlabeled data. Furthermore, the framework incorporates reinforcement learning strategies inspired by curiosity-driven exploration and random network distillation to enhance the agent's ability to discover and generate complex visual patterns. The model is evaluated on a range of tasks, including image synthesis, feature learning, and program synthesis for images, demonstrating its effectiveness in generating high-quality, interpretable outputs across diverse datasets. The approach also enables the synthesis of brushstroke paintings and sketch drawings, showcasing its versatility in creative applications.

original_abstract: We introduce a new memory architecture, Bayesian Relational Memory (BRM), to improve the generalization ability for semantic visual navigation agents in unseen environments, where an agent is given a semantic target to navigate towards. BRM takes the form of a probabilistic relation graph over semantic entities (e.g., room types), which allows (1) capturing the layout prior from training environments, i.e., prior knowledge, (2) estimating posterior layout at test time, i.e., memory update, and (3) efficient planning for navigation, altogether. We develop a BRM agent consisting of a BRM module for producing sub-goals and a goal-conditioned locomotion module for control. When testing in unseen environments, the BRM agent outperforms baselines that do not explicitly utilize the probabilistic relational memory structure
generated_abstract: This paper presents a novel framework for vision-and-language navigation that integrates semantic priors, hybrid reinforcement learning, and topological mapping to enable efficient and generalizable navigation in complex, real-world environments. Building on prior works that address data inefficiency, generalization across scenes, and task-oriented language grounding, we propose a unified architecture that combines a goal-aware actor-critic model with a Gated-Attention mechanism for language understanding, a graph-based localization system, and a planned-ahead hybrid reinforcement learning approach. Our method leverages semantic knowledge through graph convolutional networks, enhances data efficiency with auxiliary tasks, and bridges model-free and model-based learning to improve adaptability to unseen environments. Evaluated on both simulated and real-world benchmarks, our approach demonstrates superior performance in navigating diverse indoor and city-scale environments, executing natural language instructions, and generalizing to novel scenes with minimal fine-tuning.

original_abstract: Low bit-width integer weights and activations are very important for efficient inference, especially with respect to lower power consumption. We propose Monte Carlo methods to quantize the weights and activations of pre-trained neural networks without any re-training. By performing importance sampling we obtain quantized low bit-width integer values from full-precision weights and activations. The precision, sparsity, and complexity are easily configurable by the amount of sampling performed. Our approach, called Monte Carlo Quantization (MCQ), is linear in both time and space, with the resulting quantized, sparse networks showing minimal accuracy loss when compared to the original full-precision networks. Our method either outperforms or achieves competitive results on multiple benchmarks compared to previous quantization methods that do require additional training.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework that combines binary, ternary, and low-bitwidth quantization techniques to enable efficient training and inference of deep neural networks (DNNs) on resource-constrained hardware. Building on methods such as BinaryConnect, Ternary Weight Networks (TWNs), DoReFa-Net, Trained Ternary Quantization (TTQ), and LQ-Nets, we propose a unified approach that jointly trains DNNs with discrete weights and activations while maintaining high accuracy. Our method employs stochastic binarization, ternary quantization, and learned quantizers to reduce computational complexity by replacing multiplications with bit-operations, and integrates low-bitwidth gradients and integer-based dataflow for both training and inference. Experimental results on benchmark datasets including MNIST, CIFAR-10, SVHN, and ImageNet demonstrate that our approach achieves performance comparable to full-precision models while significantly reducing model size and computational requirements, making it highly suitable for deployment on low-power and embedded systems.

original_abstract: Many recent works demonstrated that Deep Learning models are vulnerable to adversarial examples.Fortunately, generating adversarial examples usually requires white-box access to the victim model, and the attacker can only access the APIs opened by cloud platforms. Thus, keeping models in the cloud can usually give a (false) sense of security.Unfortunately, cloud-based image classification service is not robust to simple transformations such as Gaussian Noise, Salt-and-Pepper Noise, Rotation and Monochromatization. In this paper,(1) we propose one novel attack method called Image Fusion(IF) attack, which achieve a high bypass rate,can be implemented only with OpenCV and is difficult to defend; and (2) we make the first attempt to conduct an extensive empirical study of Simple Transformation (ST) attacks against real-world cloud-based classification services. Through evaluations on four popular cloud platforms including Amazon, Google, Microsoft, Clarifai, we demonstrate that ST attack has a success rate of approximately 100% except Amazon approximately 50%, IF attack have a success rate over 98% among different classification services. (3) We discuss the possible defenses to address these security challenges.Experiments show that our defense technology can effectively defend known ST attacks.
generated_abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to generating highly effective and transferable adversarial examples that combine spatial transformations with query-efficient black-box attack strategies. Building on recent advances in adversarial robustness, we demonstrate that neural networks remain vulnerable to adversarial examples even when trained with robust optimization techniques or data augmentation. Our method leverages spatial transformations, such as rotations and translations, which are perceptually realistic and difficult to defend against, in conjunction with query-efficient black-box attack algorithms that require minimal interaction with the target model. We evaluate our approach on multiple cloud-based image classification services, achieving near-perfect success rates in bypassing security measures. Furthermore, we introduce a transferability test based on high-confidence adversarial examples that can break defensive mechanisms such as defensive distillation. Our results highlight the limitations of current defense strategies and provide a benchmark for future research on robust neural network design.

original_abstract: Automated driving systems (ADSs) promise a safe, comfortable and efficient driving experience. However, fatalities involving vehicles equipped with ADSs are on the rise. The full potential of ADSs cannot be realized unless the robustness of state-of-the-art improved further. This paper discusses unsolved problems and surveys the technical aspect of automated driving. Studies regarding present challenges, high-level system architectures, emerging methodologies and core functions: localization, mapping, perception, planning, and human machine interface, were thoroughly reviewed. Furthermore, the state-of-the-art was implemented on our own platform and various algorithms were compared in a real-world driving setting. The paper concludes with an overview of available datasets and tools for ADS development.
generated_abstract: This paper presents a novel end-to-end deep learning framework for autonomous driving that integrates multi-sensor data fusion, real-time 3D object detection, and behavior prediction. Building on recent advances in deep learning for highway perception, end-to-end learning, and 3D object detection from LiDAR point clouds, we propose a system that combines convolutional neural networks (CNNs) with fully convolutional architectures and voxel-based encoders to achieve robust and efficient perception. Our approach leverages both RGB images and LiDAR data, utilizing a multi-view 3D detection network and a probabilistic uncertainty-aware detector to enhance accuracy and safety. Additionally, we incorporate a real-time 3D object detection method based on the Bird's Eye View (BEV) representation and an end-to-end learning model trained on large-scale video datasets to predict driving behavior. The system is evaluated on the KITTI benchmark and demonstrates state-of-the-art performance in 3D object detection, path generation, and uncertainty estimation, while maintaining real-time operation at over 30 frames per second. This work bridges the gap between perception and control, offering a comprehensive solution for safe and efficient autonomous driving.

original_abstract: In the world of big data, many people find it difficult to access the information they need quickly and accurately. In order to overcome this, research on the system that recommends information accurately to users is continuously conducted. Collaborative Filtering is one of the famous algorithms among the most used in the industry. However, collaborative filtering is difficult to use in online systems because user recommendation is highly volatile in recommendation quality and requires computation using large matrices. To overcome this problem, this paper proposes a method similar to database queries and a clustering method (Contents Navigator) originating from a complex network.
generated_abstract: This paper presents a novel recommendation framework that integrates deep learning, sequence modeling, and collaborative filtering to address the challenges of information overload and cold start problems in recommender systems. Drawing on recent advances in deep learning-based recommendation models, sequence-to-sequence learning, and distributed word representations, we propose a unified architecture that combines recurrent neural networks for capturing sequential user behavior, matrix factorization for modeling global user preferences, and deep neural networks for extracting item content features. Our approach also incorporates techniques for learning distributed representations of items and phrases, enhancing the system's ability to understand and recommend new or under-rated items. Experimental results on MovieLens and Netflix datasets demonstrate that our model outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both general and sequential recommendation tasks, while effectively addressing cold start issues through the integration of content-based and collaborative filtering approaches. This work provides a comprehensive solution that bridges the gap between traditional and deep learning-based recommender systems, offering new perspectives for future research in this domain.

original_abstract: We propose a new and completely data-driven approach for generating an unconstrained illumination invariant representation of images. Our method trains a neural network with a specialized triplet loss designed to emphasize actual scene changes while downplaying changes in illumination. For this purpose we use the BigTime image dataset, which contains static scenes acquired at different times. We analyze the attributes of our representation, and show that it improves patch matching and rigid registration over state-of-the-art illumination invariant representations. We point out that the utility of our method is not restricted to handling illumination invariance, and that it may be applied for generating representations which are invariant to general types of nuisance, undesired, image variants.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework that combines deep metric learning with intrinsic image decomposition using triplet and siamese networks. Building on recent advances in triplet network architectures for learning discriminative image representations, we propose an end-to-end approach that integrates these models with unsupervised learning strategies for single-image intrinsic decomposition. By leveraging illumination-varying image sequences, our method learns albedo and shading components without requiring ground truth annotations, using a siamese training scheme with cross-image consistency constraints. Additionally, we incorporate global loss functions to enhance generalization and improve embedding quality, as demonstrated on benchmark datasets for both metric learning and intrinsic decomposition tasks. Our results show that the proposed framework outperforms existing methods in both accuracy and robustness, offering a unified solution for learning meaningful image representations and decomposing intrinsic image properties.

original_abstract: Visual Indoor Navigation (VIN) task has drawn increasing attentions from the data-driven machine learning communities especially with the recent reported success from learning-based methods. Due to the innate complexity of this task, researchers have tried approaching the problem from a variety of different angles, the full scope of which has not yet been captured within an overarching report. In this survey, we discuss the representative work of learning-based approaches for visual navigation and its related tasks. Firstly, we summarize the current work in terms of task representations and applied methods along with their properties. We then further identify and discuss lingering issues impeding the performance of VIN tasks and motivate future research in these key areas worth exploring in the future for the community.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for target-driven visual navigation that integrates semantic priors, hybrid reinforcement learning, and cognitive mapping to achieve robust and generalizable navigation in both simulated and real-world environments. By unifying map-based spatial reasoning with landmark-based execution, the proposed method leverages a learned path planner, feature synthesis engine, and goal-driven controller to navigate efficiently in novel scenes. Additionally, it incorporates self-supervised auxiliary reasoning tasks to enhance semantic understanding and improve generalization across unseen environments. The framework also integrates a hybrid model-free and model-based reinforcement learning approach, enabling planned-ahead navigation and better adaptation to real-world dynamics. Furthermore, semantic knowledge is embedded through graph convolutional networks and object relation graphs, allowing the agent to exploit functional scene priors for efficient exploration and target localization. The proposed method demonstrates significant improvements in navigation success rate, generalization to new scenes and objects, and adaptability to real-world conditions, as validated through extensive experiments in AI2-THOR and other benchmark environments.

original_abstract: Classical approaches for one-class problems such as one-class SVM (Scholkopf et al., 1999) and isolation forest (Liu et al., 2008) require careful feature engineering when applied to structured domains like images. To alleviate this concern, state-of-the-art methods like DeepSVDD (Ruff et al., 2018) consider the natural alternative of minimizing a classical one-class loss applied to the learned final layer representations. However, such an approach suffers from the fundamental drawback that a representation that simply collapses all the inputs minimizes the one class loss; heuristics to mitigate collapsed representations provide limited benefits. In this work, we propose Deep Robust One Class Classification (DROCC) method that is robust to such a collapse by training the network to distinguish the training points from their perturbations, generated adversarially. DROCC is motivated by the assumption that the interesting class lies on a locally linear low dimensional manifold. Empirical evaluation demonstrates DROCC's effectiveness on two different one-class problem settings and on a range of real-world datasets across different domains - images(CIFAR and ImageNet), audio and timeseries, offering up to 20% increase in accuracy over the state-of-the-art in anomaly detection.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel deep anomaly detection framework that integrates geometric transformation-based learning, semi-supervised strategies, outlier exposure, and self-supervised pre-training to enhance detection accuracy and robustness. By training a multi-class model to distinguish between various geometric transformations of normal data, the framework leverages auxiliary knowledge to generate effective feature detectors. To improve generalization, we incorporate Outlier Exposure, using a large auxiliary dataset of out-of-distribution examples during training. Additionally, we employ self-supervised learning to strengthen model robustness against adversarial examples and input corruptions, while semi-supervised techniques are used to incorporate limited labeled data for better performance. The proposed method is evaluated on multiple benchmark datasets, demonstrating significant improvements in anomaly detection accuracy compared to existing approaches, particularly in handling near-distribution outliers and diverse data modalities.

original_abstract: Gaze correction aims to redirect the person's gaze into the camera by manipulating the eye region, and it can be considered as a specific image resynthesis problem. Gaze correction has a wide range of applications in real life, such as taking a picture with staring at the camera. In this paper, we propose a novel method that is based on the inpainting model to learn from the face image to fill in the missing eye regions with new contents representing corrected eye gaze. Moreover, our model does not require the training dataset labeled with the specific head pose and eye angle information, thus, the training data is easy to collect. To retain the identity information of the eye region in the original input, we propose a self-guided pretrained model to learn the angle-invariance feature. Experiments show our model achieves very compelling gaze-corrected results in the wild dataset which is collected from the website and will be introduced in details. Code is available at this https URL.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a unified framework that combines advanced GAN training techniques, multi-domain image translation, exemplar-based in-painting, and high-resolution semantic image synthesis to enable versatile and high-quality image generation and manipulation. Building on state-of-the-art methods such as StarGAN, ExGANs, and conditional GANs with multi-scale architectures, our approach integrates exemplar information, disentangled representations, and self-supervised learning to achieve flexible, high-resolution image synthesis, multi-attribute facial manipulation, and accurate in-painting while preserving object identity. The model supports both supervised and unsupervised training, enabling robust performance across diverse tasks including facial expression synthesis, semantic editing, and multi-domain translation. Experimental results demonstrate superior visual quality, resolution, and flexibility compared to existing methods, validated through human evaluations and benchmark datasets.

original_abstract: The lack of large-scale real datasets with annotationsmakes transfer learning a necessity for video activity under-standing. Within this scope, we aim at developing an effec-tive method for low-shot transfer learning for first-personaction classification. We leverage independently trained lo-cal visual cues to learn representations that can be trans-ferred from a source domain providing primitive action la-bels to a target domain with only a handful of examples.Such visual cues include object-object interactions, handgrasps and motion within regions that are a function of handlocations. We suggest a framework based on meta-learningto appropriately extract the distinctive and domain invari-ant components of the deployed visual cues, so to be able totransfer action classification models across public datasetscaptured with different scene configurations. We thoroughlyevaluate our methodology and report promising results overstate-of-the-art action classification approaches for bothinter-class and inter-dataset transfer.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for action recognition in videos that integrates visual attention mechanisms, spatiotemporal feature learning, and object-level reasoning. Building on recent advances in attention-based models, two-stream architectures, and temporal relational reasoning, our approach combines a soft attention module with a Temporal Relation Network (TRN) to dynamically focus on relevant video segments and reason about temporal dependencies. Additionally, we incorporate object detection to enable fine-grained reasoning about interactions between actors and objects at the semantic level. The proposed model is evaluated on multiple benchmark datasets, including UCF-101, HMDB-51, Something-Something, Jester, Charades, and EPIC Kitchens, achieving state-of-the-art performance while demonstrating interpretability through visualizations of attention maps and learned object interactions. Our results highlight the effectiveness of combining attention, temporal reasoning, and object-level understanding for robust and interpretable action recognition.

original_abstract: Record Linkage is an essential part of almost all real-world systems that consume data coming from different sources, structured and unstructured. Typically no common key is available in order to connect the records. Often massive data cleaning and data integration processes have to be completed before any data analytics and further processing can be performed. Though record linkage is often seen as a somewhat tedious necessary step, it is able to reveal valuable insights of the data at hand. These insights guide further analytic approaches over the data and support data visualization. In this work we focus on company entity matching, where company name, location and industry are taken into account. The matching is done on the fly to accommodate realtime processing of streamed data. Our contribution is a system that uses rule-based matching algorithms for scoring operations which we extend with a machine learning approach to account for short company names. We propose an end-to-end highly scalable enterprise-grade system. Linkage time is greatly reduced by efficient decomposition of the search space using MinHash. High linkage accuracy is reached by the proposed thorough scoring process of the matching candidates. Based on two real world ground truth datasets, we show that our approach reaches a recall of 91% compared to 86% for baseline approaches. These results are achieved while scaling linearly with the number of nodes used in the system.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach that combines sequence tagging with efficient set similarity estimation techniques to enhance entity resolution (ER) in large-scale data integration tasks. Building on bidirectional LSTM-CRF models for accurate sequence tagging and leveraging advanced minwise hashing algorithms such as SuperMinHash and optimal densification techniques, we propose a hybrid framework that improves the precision and efficiency of ER. Our method effectively captures contextual information for entity attributes using bidirectional LSTMs and CRF layers, while employing optimized hashing techniques to manage and compare large sets of entity records with reduced computational overhead and storage requirements. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms traditional ER methods in terms of accuracy and scalability, making it a promising solution for real-world data integration challenges.

original_abstract: Autonomous Wireless Sensors (AWSs) are at the core of every Wireless Sensor Network (WSN). Current AWS technology allows the development of many IoT-based applications, ranging from military to bioengineering and from industry to education. The energy optimization of AWSs depends mainly on: Structural, functional, and application specifications. The holistic design methodology addresses all the factors mentioned above. In this sense, we propose an original solution based on a novel architecture that duplicates the transceivers and also the power source using a hybrid storage system. By identifying the consumption needs of the transceivers, an appropriate methodology for sizing and controlling the power flow for the power source is proposed. The paper emphasizes the fusion between information, communication, and energy consumption of the AWS in terms of spectrum information through a set of transceiver testing scenarios, identifying the main factors that influence the sensor node design and their inter-dependencies. Optimization of the system considers all these factors obtaining an energy efficient AWS, paving the way towards autonomous sensors by adding an energy harvesting element to them.
generated_abstract: This paper presents a novel antenna design for Internet of Things (IoT) applications, integrating slitted patch antenna structures with RF wireless power transfer (WPT) capabilities to enhance performance in multi-frequency and multi-technology environments. By leveraging the radiation pattern optimization of slitted patch antennas and incorporating ground effect analysis, the proposed design improves signal strength and directional control. Furthermore, the integration of AC computing-enabled receiver architecture allows for simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT), enhancing energy efficiency and computational performance. The design is evaluated using electromagnetic simulation software and experimental RF propagation analysis, demonstrating improved data rate, energy harvesting efficiency, and robustness in diverse IoT deployment scenarios. The results highlight the potential of combining advanced antenna design with green RF-WPT technologies to support future sustainable and interoperable IoT networks.

original_abstract: Grounding language to visual relations is critical to various language-and-vision applications. In this work, we tackle two fundamental language-and-vision tasks: image-text matching and image captioning, and demonstrate that neural scene graph generators can learn effective visual relation features to facilitate grounding language to visual relations and subsequently improve the two end applications. By combining relation features with the state-of-the-art models, our experiments show significant improvement on the standard Flickr30K and MSCOCO benchmarks. Our experimental results and analysis show that relation features improve downstream models' capability of capturing visual relations in end vision-and-language applications. We also demonstrate the importance of learning scene graph generators with visually relevant relations to the effectiveness of relation features.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework that integrates scene graph generation, phrase localization, and cross-modal retrieval to enhance visual understanding and textual description of images. By combining associative embeddings for graph generation, dynamic multi-level alignment of objects, phrases, and captions, and stacked cross-attention mechanisms for image-text matching, our approach captures both local and global semantic relationships. The model leverages generative processes to learn grounded and abstract features, enabling improved performance in scene graph generation, phrase localization, and cross-modal retrieval. Experimental results demonstrate significant improvements over existing methods on benchmark datasets, including state-of-the-art performance in scene graph generation, visual relationship detection, and cross-modal retrieval tasks.

original_abstract: We present an overview of the EmotionX 2019 Challenge, held at the 7th International Workshop on Natural Language Processing for Social Media (SocialNLP), in conjunction with IJCAI 2019. The challenge entailed predicting emotions in spoken and chat-based dialogues using augmented EmotionLines datasets. EmotionLines contains two distinct datasets: the first includes excerpts from a US-based TV sitcom episode scripts (Friends) and the second contains online chats (EmotionPush). A total of thirty-six teams registered to participate in the challenge. Eleven of the teams successfully submitted their predictions performance evaluation. The top-scoring team achieved a micro-F1 score of 81.5% for the spoken-based dialogues (Friends) and 79.5% for the chat-based dialogues (EmotionPush).
generated_abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to contextual emotion detection in multi-party conversations by integrating the EmotionLines dataset with advanced BERT-based models tailored for dialogue understanding. Building on prior works that highlight the challenges of capturing emotional context and the effectiveness of pre-trained language models, we propose a dynamic contextual emotion classifier that leverages self-attention mechanisms and weighted loss functions to address class imbalance and contextual dependencies. Our model is fine-tuned on the EmotionLines dataset, which provides granular emotion labels for each utterance in dialogues from Friends and Facebook messenger logs. Experimental results demonstrate significant improvements in micro-F1 scores compared to existing methods, showcasing the potential of combining rich emotional datasets with state-of-the-art contextual modeling techniques for more accurate and nuanced emotion recognition in natural conversations.

original_abstract: We investigate spatio-temporal event analysis using point processes. Inferring the dynamics of event sequences spatiotemporally has many practical applications including crime prediction, social media analysis, and traffic forecasting. In particular, we focus on spatio-temporal Hawkes processes that are commonly used due to their capability to capture excitations between event occurrences. We introduce a novel inference framework based on randomized transformations and gradient descent to learn the process. We replace the spatial kernel calculations by randomized Fourier feature-based transformations. The introduced randomization by this representation provides flexibility while modeling the spatial excitation between events. Moreover, the system described by the process is expressed within closed-form in terms of scalable matrix operations. During the optimization, we use maximum likelihood estimation approach and gradient descent while properly handling positivity and orthonormality constraints. The experiment results show the improvements achieved by the introduced method in terms of fitting capability in synthetic and real datasets with respect to the conventional inference methods in the spatio-temporal Hawkes process literature. We also analyze the triggering interactions between event types and how their dynamics change in space and time through the interpretation of learned parameters.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework that integrates reinforcement learning (RL) with multivariate spatiotemporal Hawkes processes to enhance network reconstruction and event prediction from complex spatiotemporal point process data. Building on nonparametric methods for network inference and semi-parametric models for spatiotemporal dynamics, our approach combines the flexibility of RL with the expressive power of Hawkes processes to model both the temporal evolution and spatial dependencies of events. By parameterizing the intensity function using neural networks and employing a reward mechanism based on maximum mean discrepancy, we achieve robust estimation of latent network structures and improved forecasting of event occurrences. The method is validated on synthetic and real-world datasets, including social media interactions, crime events, and emergency calls, demonstrating superior performance in capturing clustering phenomena, reconstructing underlying networks, and predicting future events compared to existing parametric and nonparametric approaches. This work provides a unified and scalable approach for analyzing and forecasting spatiotemporal event data in diverse application domains.

original_abstract: Object segmentation and object tracking are fundamental research area in the computer vision community. These two topics are diffcult to handle some common challenges, such as occlusion, deformation, motion blur, and scale variation. The former contains heterogeneous object, interacting object, edge ambiguity, and shape complexity. And the latter suffers from difficulties in handling fast motion, out-of-view, and real-time processing. Combining the two problems of video object segmentation and tracking (VOST) can overcome their respective difficulties and improve their performance. VOST can be widely applied to many practical applications such as video summarization, high definition video compression, human computer interaction, and autonomous vehicles. This article aims to provide a comprehensive review of the state-of-the-art tracking methods, and classify these methods into different categories, and identify new trends. First, we provide a hierarchical categorization existing approaches, including unsupervised VOS, semi-supervised VOS, interactive VOS, weakly supervised VOS, and segmentation-based tracking methods. Second, we provide a detailed discussion and overview of the technical characteristics of the different methods. Third, we summarize the characteristics of the related video dataset, and provide a variety of evaluation metrics. Finally, we point out a set of interesting future works and draw our own conclusions.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for semi-supervised video object segmentation that integrates one-shot learning, online adaptation, motion guidance, and visual memory mechanisms. Building on the OSVOS and OnAVOS approaches, our method employs a fully-convolutional neural network to transfer generic semantic knowledge from ImageNet to the task of foreground segmentation, while incorporating online adaptation to handle dynamic changes in object appearance. Additionally, motion cues are leveraged through optical flow and spatio-temporal propagation to enhance segmentation accuracy, and a visual memory module captures the evolution of objects over time, improving temporal coherence. The framework also incorporates part-based tracking and reference-guided mask propagation to achieve fast and accurate segmentation. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets such as DAVIS, FBMS-59, and SegTrack v2 demonstrate that our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance in terms of intersection-over-union scores while maintaining high computational efficiency.

original_abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) is expected to require more effective and efficient wireless communications than ever before. For this reason, techniques such as spectrum sharing and dynamic spectrum access will soon become essential components of the IoT wireless communication process. In this vision, IoT devices must be able to not only learn to autonomously extract spectrum knowledge on-the-fly from the network but also leverage such knowledge to dynamically change appropriate wireless parameters (e.g., frequency band, symbol modulation, coding rate, route selection etc) to reach the network's optimal operating point. To address the above challenges, much research has been devoted to exploring the use of machine learning to address problems in the IoT wireless communications domain. The reason behind machine learning's popularity is that it provides a general framework to solve very complex problems where a model of the phenomenon being learned is too complex to derive or too dynamic to be summarized in mathematical terms. This work provides a comprehensive survey of the state of the art in the application of machine learning techniques to address key problems in IoT wireless communications with an emphasis on its ad hoc networking aspect. First, we present extensive background notions on machine learning techniques. Then, by adopting a bottom-up approach, we examine existing work on machine learning for the IoT at the physical, data-link and network layer of the protocol stack. Thereafter, we discuss directions taken by the community towards hardware implementation to ensure the feasibility of these techniques. Finally, we provide a series of research challenges associated with the applications of machine learning techniques for IoT wireless communications.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework that integrates deep learning techniques for wireless signal identification, channel estimation, and dynamic spectrum access in heterogeneous wireless networks. Building upon recent advances in convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for wireless interference identification and modulation recognition, we propose an end-to-end deep learning architecture that combines CNN-based signal classification with deep reinforcement learning (DRL) for adaptive medium access control (MAC) protocols. The system leverages raw IQ data and frequency domain representations to achieve robust signal detection and classification across multiple wireless standards, including IEEE 802.11 b/g, 802.15.4, and 802.15.1, with classification accuracy exceeding 95% at signal-to-noise ratios above −5 dB. Furthermore, the DRL-based MAC protocol, DLMA, enables autonomous coexistence with diverse MAC protocols such as TDMA and ALOHA without prior knowledge of their operation, demonstrating fast convergence and robustness in dynamic environments. The proposed framework also incorporates deep learning for channel estimation and signal detection in OFDM systems, achieving performance comparable to minimum mean-square error estimators while reducing dependency on explicit channel state information. This integrated approach offers a promising solution for future wireless systems requiring high accuracy, adaptability, and efficient spectrum utilization.

original_abstract: Deep Convolutional Neural Network (DCNNs) come to be the most widely used solution for most computer vision related tasks, and one of the most important application scenes is face verification. Due to its high-accuracy performance, deep face verification models of which the inference stage occurs on cloud platform through internet plays the key role on most prectical scenes. However, two critical issues exist: First, individual privacy may not be well protected since they have to upload their personal photo and other private information to the online cloud backend. Secondly, either training or inference stage is time-comsuming and the latency may affect customer experience, especially when the internet link speed is not so stable or in remote areas where mobile reception is not so good, but also in cities where building and other construction may block mobile signals. Therefore, designing lightweight networks with low memory requirement and computational cost is one of the most practical solutions for face verification on mobile platform. In this paper, a novel mobile network named SeesawFaceNets, a simple but effective model, is proposed for productively deploying face recognition for mobile devices. Dense experimental results have shown that our proposed model SeesawFaceNets outperforms the baseline MobilefaceNets, with only {\bf66\%}(146M VS 221M MAdds) computational cost, smaller batch size and less training steps, and SeesawFaceNets achieve comparable performance with other SOTA model e.g. mobiface with only {\bf54.2\%}(1.3M VS 2.4M) parameters and {\bf31.6\%}(146M VS 462M MAdds) computational cost, It is also eventually competitive against large-scale deep-networks face recognition on all 5 listed public validation datasets, with {\bf6.5\%}(4.2M VS 65M) parameters and {\bf4.35\%}(526M VS 12G MAdds) computational cost.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel lightweight and efficient convolutional neural network architecture, named DenseShuffleNet, that combines the advantages of DenseNet, ShuffleNet, and network slimming techniques to achieve superior performance on mobile devices. By integrating dense connections for enhanced feature propagation and reusability with ShuffleNet's efficient pointwise group convolutions and channel shuffle operations, DenseShuffleNet significantly reduces computational cost while maintaining high accuracy. Furthermore, network slimming is applied to automatically prune redundant channels, further reducing model size and inference latency. Extensive experiments on ImageNet classification and MS COCO object detection demonstrate that DenseShuffleNet outperforms existing mobile CNNs such as MobileNet and ShuffleNet in terms of both accuracy and efficiency, achieving a notable reduction in computational operations and memory usage without sacrificing performance. The proposed architecture is particularly well-suited for real-time applications on resource-constrained mobile and embedded platforms.

original_abstract: Deep neural networks have been playing an essential role in the task of Visual Question Answering (VQA). Until recently, their accuracy has been the main focus of research. Now there is a trend toward assessing the robustness of these models against adversarial attacks by evaluating the accuracy of these models under increasing levels of noisiness in the inputs of VQA models. In VQA, the attack can target the image and/or the proposed query question, dubbed main question, and yet there is a lack of proper analysis of this aspect of VQA. In this work, we propose a new method that uses semantically related questions, dubbed basic questions, acting as noise to evaluate the robustness of VQA models. We hypothesize that as the similarity of a basic question to the main question decreases, the level of noise increases. To generate a reasonable noise level for a given main question, we rank a pool of basic questions based on their similarity with this main question. We cast this ranking problem as a LASSO optimization problem. We also propose a novel robustness measure Rscore and two large-scale basic question datasets in order to standardize robustness analysis of VQA models. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed evaluation method is able to effectively analyze the robustness of VQA models. To foster the VQA research, we will publish our proposed datasets.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for Visual Question Answering (VQA) that integrates multi-modal learning, hierarchical attention mechanisms, and external knowledge sources to enhance the accuracy and robustness of image-based question answering systems. Building on recent advances in convolutional neural networks (CNNs), co-attention models, and Bayesian reasoning under uncertainty, our approach employs a hierarchical co-attention mechanism to jointly reason about image and question representations, while incorporating external knowledge from general knowledge bases to address complex and context-dependent queries. Additionally, we introduce a multi-world Bayesian framework to handle uncertainty in image perception and reasoning, enabling the system to provide diverse and probabilistic answers. The proposed model is evaluated on benchmark datasets including DAQUAR, COCO-QA, and VQA, achieving state-of-the-art performance while demonstrating superior handling of ambiguous and complex questions.

original_abstract: We tackle the challenge of disentangled representation learning in generative adversarial networks (GANs) from the perspective of regularized optimal transport (OT). Specifically, a smoothed OT loss gives rise to an implicit transportation plan between the latent space and the data space. Based on this theoretical observation, we exploit a structured regularization on the transportation plan to encourage a prescribed latent subspace to be informative. This yields the formulation of a novel informative OT-based GAN. By convex duality, we obtain the equivalent view that this leads to perturbed ground costs favoring sparsity in the informative latent dimensions. Practically, we devise a stable training algorithm for the proposed informative GAN. Our experiments support the hypothesis that such regularizations effectively yield the discovery of disentangled and interpretable latent representations. Our work showcases potential power of a regularized OT framework in the context of generative modeling through its access to the transport plan. Further challenges are addressed in this line.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel generative model that combines the interpretability of InfoGAN with the stability and efficiency of optimal transport-based GANs, leveraging advancements in Wasserstein GANs, MMD GANs, and Sinkhorn divergences. By integrating information-maximizing latent representations with a robust training framework based on regularized optimal transport, the proposed model achieves stable and high-quality generation while enabling disentangled and interpretable feature learning. The method employs a modified mini-batch energy distance that combines adversarially learned features with entropic regularization, allowing for efficient gradient computation and improved convergence. Experimental results on benchmark datasets such as MNIST, CIFAR-10, and CelebA demonstrate that the model outperforms existing GAN variants in both generation quality and interpretability of latent representations, offering a promising direction for deep generative modeling with structured and meaningful latent spaces.

original_abstract: Evaluating the readability of a text can significantly facilitate the precise expression of information in a written form. The formulation of text readability assessment demands the identification of meaningful properties of the text and correct conversion of features to the right readability level. Sophisticated features and models are being used to evaluate the comprehensibility of texts accurately. Still, these models are challenging to implement, heavily language-dependent, and do not perform well on short texts. Deep reinforcement learning models are demonstrated to be helpful in further improvement of state-of-the-art text readability assessment models. The main contributions of the proposed approach are the automation of feature extraction, loosening the tight language dependency of text readability assessment task, and efficient use of text by finding the minimum portion of a text required to assess its readability. The experiments on Weebit, Cambridge Exams, and Persian readability datasets display the model's state-of-the-art precision, efficiency, and the capability to be applied to other languages.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework that combines reinforcement learning, transfer learning, and interactive feedback mechanisms to enhance text simplification and readability assessment for second language learners. Building on prior work in readability estimation, neural machine translation, and sentence simplification, we propose a deep reinforcement learning model that leverages simulated human feedback and domain adaptation techniques to optimize text simplification for L2 learners. Our approach integrates a generator-evaluator architecture with a self-critic policy gradient method, enabling the model to learn from partial translation feedback and adapt dynamically to user preferences. Additionally, we incorporate a joint estimation of word and document readability using graph convolutional networks to improve the fluency and simplicity of generated texts. Experimental results demonstrate that our model significantly outperforms existing systems in terms of readability scores, simplification quality, and user interaction efficiency, achieving a PCC of 0.938 and reducing human feedback requests to an average of five per input.

original_abstract: Adversarial attacks on video recognition models have been explored recently. However, most existing works treat each video frame equally and ignore their temporal interactions. To overcome this drawback, a few methods try to select some key frames, and then perform attacks based on them. Unfortunately, their selecting strategy is independent with the attacking step, therefore the resulting performance is limited. In this paper, we aim to attack video recognition task in the black-box setting. The difference is, we think the frame selection phase is closely relevant with the attacking phase. The reasonable key frames should be adjusted according to the feedback of attacking threat models. Based on this idea, we formulate the black-box video attacks into the Reinforcement Learning (RL) framework. Specifically, the environment in RL is set as the threat models, and the agent in RL plays the role of frame selecting and video attacking simultaneously. By continuously querying the threat models and receiving the feedback of predicted probabilities (reward), the agent adjusts its frame selection strategy and performs attacks (action). Step by step, the optimal key frames are selected and the smallest adversarial perturbations are achieved. We conduct a series of experiments with two mainstream video recognition models: C3D and LRCN on the public UCF-101 and HMDB-51 datasets. The results demonstrate that the proposed method can significantly reduce the perturbation of adversarial examples and attacking on the sparse video frames can have better attack effectiveness than attacking on each frame.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for generating transferable and temporally sparse adversarial perturbations in real-time video classification systems, combining insights from adversarial attacks on deep learning models, sparse perturbations for videos, and black-box attack methodologies. Building on recent advances in adversarial example generation, we propose a GAN-based approach that exploits temporal correlations to create stealthy perturbations affecting targeted activities while leaving others largely intact. Our method leverages sparse adversarial perturbations, where minimal frame modifications propagate across the video sequence, significantly reducing the computational cost and enhancing imperceptibility. Furthermore, we extend the concept of transferability to video recognition models, enabling effective black-box attacks with fewer queries to the target model. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate high fooling rates with minimal perceptible changes, highlighting the vulnerability of real-time video systems to such attacks. This work provides a foundation for evaluating and improving the robustness of video-based AI systems against adversarial threats.

original_abstract: Domain adaptation performance of a learning algorithm on a target domain is a function of its source domain error and a divergence measure between the data distribution of these two domains. We present a study of various distance-based measures in the context of NLP tasks, that characterize the dissimilarity between domains based on sample estimates. We first conduct analysis experiments to show which of these distance measures can best differentiate samples from same versus different domains, and are correlated with empirical results. Next, we develop a DistanceNet model which uses these distance measures, or a mixture of these distance measures, as an additional loss function to be minimized jointly with the task's loss function, so as to achieve better unsupervised domain adaptation. Finally, we extend this model to a novel DistanceNet-Bandit model, which employs a multi-armed bandit controller to dynamically switch between multiple source domains and allow the model to learn an optimal trajectory and mixture of domains for transfer to the low-resource target domain. We conduct experiments on popular sentiment analysis datasets with several diverse domains and show that our DistanceNet model, as well as its dynamic bandit variant, can outperform competitive baselines in the context of unsupervised domain adaptation.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel domain adaptation framework that integrates multiple state-of-the-art techniques to enhance transfer learning across disparate domains. Building on deep transfer networks, joint adaptation networks, and adversarial discriminative domain adaptation, the proposed method combines shared feature extraction with domain confusion loss, joint distribution alignment using maximum mean discrepancy, and task-specific classifier discrepancy to achieve domain invariance. By incorporating residual transfer networks and associative domain adaptation principles, the framework explicitly models domain shifts and aligns feature distributions in reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces. The approach leverages both supervised and unsupervised learning strategies, enabling effective adaptation with minimal labeled target data. Experimental results on standard benchmark datasets demonstrate significant improvements in classification accuracy and adaptation efficiency compared to existing methods, establishing the proposed framework as a robust and scalable solution for cross-domain learning tasks.

original_abstract: Mobile edge caching can effectively reduce service delay but may introduce information staleness, calling for timely content refreshing. However, content refreshing consumes additional transmission resources and may degrade the delay performance of mobile systems. In this work, we propose a freshness-aware refreshing scheme to balance the service delay and content freshness measured by Age of Information (AoI). Specifically, the cached content items will be refreshed to the up-to-date version upon user requests if the AoI exceeds a certain threshold (named as refreshing window). The average AoI and service delay are derived in closed forms approximately, which reveals an AoI-delay tradeoff relationship with respect to the refreshing window. In addition, the refreshing window is optimized to minimize the average delay while meeting the AoI requirements, and the results indicate to set a smaller refreshing window for the popular content items. Extensive simulations are conducted on the OMNeT++ platform to validate the analytical results. The results indicate that the proposed scheme can restrain frequent refreshing as the request arrival rate increases, whereby the average delay can be reduced by around 80% while maintaining the AoI below one second in heavily-loaded scenarios.
generated_abstract: This paper presents a novel framework that integrates energy efficiency, context-aware caching, and dynamic content popularity prediction to optimize edge caching in dense heterogeneous cellular networks. By combining caching strategies that consider base station sleeping, content popularity fluctuations, and user context, we propose a cooperative caching mechanism that enhances network throughput while reducing energy consumption and service latency. Our approach leverages context-aware proactive caching algorithms to adaptively update cache content based on user behavior and location, and incorporates location-customized caching schemes to maximize content hit rates under varying traffic conditions. Additionally, we analyze the impact of cache size, backhaul capacity, and interference levels on energy efficiency and propose an optimal cache capacity that maximizes network performance. The proposed framework is validated through extensive simulations, demonstrating significant improvements in energy efficiency, content freshness, and delivery latency compared to existing caching strategies.

original_abstract: Accompanied by the successful progress of deep representation learning, convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have been widely applied to improve the accuracy of polarimetric synthetic aperture radar (PolSAR) image classification. However, in most applications, the difference between PolSAR image and optical image is rarely considered. The design of most existing network structures is not tailored to the characteristics of PolSAR image data and complex-valued data of PolSAR image are simply equated to real-valued data to adapt to the existing mainstream network pipeline to avoid complex-valued operations. These make CNNs unable to perform their full capabilities in the PolSAR image classification tasks. In this paper, we focus on finding a better input form of PolSAR image data and designing special CNN structures that are more compatible with PolSAR image. Considering the relationship between complex number and its amplitude and phase, we extract the amplitude and phase of the complex-valued PolSAR image data as input to maintain the integrity of the original information while avoiding the current immature complex-valued operations, and a novel multi-task CNN framework is proposed to adapt to novel form of input data. Furthermore, in order to better explore the unique phase information in the PolSAR image data, depthwise separable convolutions are applied to the proposed multi-task CNN model. Experiments on three benchmark datasets not only prove that using amplitude and phase information as input does contribute to the improvement of classification accuracy, but also verify the effectiveness of the proposed methods for amplitude and phase input.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel deep convolutional network architecture that integrates the strengths of residual learning, dense connectivity, and spatial pyramid pooling to achieve state-of-the-art performance in both image classification and semantic segmentation tasks. By combining residual blocks with dense connections, the proposed architecture enhances feature propagation and alleviates the vanishing gradient problem, while spatial pyramid pooling enables flexible input sizes and robust feature aggregation across multiple scales. Additionally, dilated convolutions are incorporated to maintain resolution while capturing multi-scale contextual information. The model is evaluated on benchmark datasets including ImageNet, PASCAL VOC, and COCO, demonstrating significant improvements in accuracy and efficiency compared to existing methods. The architecture's modular design and effective parameter usage make it a versatile foundation for a wide range of visual recognition tasks.

original_abstract: Big data production in industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) is evident due to the massive deployment of sensors and Internet of Things (IoT) devices. However, big data processing is challenging due to limited computational, networking and storage resources at IoT device-end. Big data analytics (BDA) is expected to provide operational- and customer-level intelligence in IIoT systems. Although numerous studies on IIoT and BDA exist, only a few studies have explored the convergence of the two paradigms. In this study, we investigate the recent BDA technologies, algorithms and techniques that can lead to the development of intelligent IIoT systems. We devise a taxonomy by classifying and categorising the literature on the basis of important parameters (e.g. data sources, analytics tools, analytics techniques, requirements, industrial analytics applications and analytics types). We present the frameworks and case studies of the various enterprises that have benefited from BDA. We also enumerate the considerable opportunities introduced by BDA in IIoT.We identify and discuss the indispensable challenges that remain to be addressed as future research directions as well.
generated_abstract: This paper presents a novel integrated framework that combines the Internet of Things (IoT), edge computing, big data analytics, and business process management systems (BPMS) to address the challenges of managing and optimizing large-scale, heterogeneous IoT environments. Drawing on recent advancements in IoT marketplace dynamics, edge computing capabilities, and big data analytics architectures, the proposed framework introduces a scalable and efficient system for real-time data processing, anomaly detection, and decision-making in industrial and urban applications. The framework leverages the Graph of Virtual Actors (GOVA) architecture for handling noninvariant challenges in IoT data, integrates edge computing for localized processing, and incorporates mobile cloud BPMS for managing complex IoT workflows. Additionally, it addresses data ingestion challenges through a heterogeneous device data model, ensuring seamless integration of diverse IoT data sources. The paper also explores opportunities for industrial big data analytics and cyber-physical systems (CPS) in smart manufacturing and service innovation. Finally, it identifies open research challenges, including privacy, data integration, and system scalability, offering a roadmap for future research and development in the IoT domain.

original_abstract: Online advertising has been a long-standing concern for user privacy and overall web experience. Several techniques have been proposed to block ads, mostly based on filter-lists and manually-written rules. While a typical ad blocker relies on manually-curated block lists, these inevitably get out-of-date, thus compromising the ultimate utility of this ad blocking approach. In this paper we present Percival, a browser-embedded, lightweight, deep learning-powered ad blocker. Percival embeds itself within the browser's image rendering pipeline, which makes it possible to intercept every image obtained during page execution and to perform blocking based on applying machine learning for image classification to flag potential ads. Our implementation inside both Chromium and Brave browsers shows only a minor rendering performance overhead of 4.55%, demonstrating the feasibility of deploying traditionally heavy models (i.e. deep neural networks) inside the critical path of the rendering engine of a browser. We show that our image-based ad blocker can replicate EasyList rules with an accuracy of 96.76%. To show the versatility of the Percival's approach we present case studies that demonstrate that Percival 1) does surprisingly well on ads in languages other than English; 2) Percival also performs well on blocking first-party Facebook ads, which have presented issues for other ad blockers. Percival proves that image-based perceptual ad blocking is an attractive complement to today's dominant approach of block lists
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel defense framework that combines adversarial training, logit pairing, and certified robustness techniques to enhance the resilience of deep learning models against adversarial attacks. Building on large-scale adversarial training methods applied to ImageNet, we incorporate adversarial logit pairing to improve accuracy on adversarial examples while mitigating the label leaking effect. Additionally, we integrate certified robustness via differential privacy and convex outer adversarial polytopes to provide theoretical guarantees against norm-bounded perturbations. Our approach demonstrates significant improvements in robustness against both white-box and black-box attacks, achieving state-of-the-art results on ImageNet with minimal performance degradation on clean data. The framework is scalable, efficient, and effective in defending against a wide range of adversarial strategies, including single-step and multi-step attacks, while maintaining strong generalization capabilities.

original_abstract: Machine learning in context of physical systems merits a re-examination of the learning strategy. In addition to data, one can leverage a vast library of physical prior models (e.g. kinematics, fluid flow, etc) to perform more robust inference. The nascent sub-field of \emph{physics-based learning} (PBL) studies the blending of neural networks with physical priors. While previous PBL algorithms have been applied successfully to specific tasks, it is hard to generalize existing PBL methods to a wide range of physics-based problems. Such generalization would require an architecture that can adapt to variations in the correctness of the physics, or in the quality of training data. No such architecture exists. In this paper, we aim to generalize PBL, by making a first attempt to bring neural architecture search (NAS) to the realm of PBL. We introduce a new method known as physics-based neural architecture search (PhysicsNAS) that is a top-performer across a diverse range of quality in the physical model and the dataset.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel deep learning framework that integrates physics-based modeling with advanced neural network architectures to address a broad range of inverse problems in computational imaging. Building on unrolled optimization with deep priors, physics-based generative adversarial models, and direct inversion with CNNs, the proposed method combines the strengths of physical models and data-driven learning to achieve robust and efficient solutions for ill-posed imaging tasks. The framework is demonstrated on diverse applications, including sparse-view X-ray computed tomography, lensless imaging, phase retrieval under low-light conditions, and image restoration. By incorporating physical constraints into the learning process and leveraging multiresolution decomposition and residual learning, the method outperforms state-of-the-art techniques in terms of reconstruction quality, speed, and generalization across different imaging modalities. Experimental results on synthetic and real-world data validate the effectiveness of the approach, highlighting its potential for practical deployment in real-time and resource-constrained imaging systems.

original_abstract: The notion of uncertainty is of major importance in machine learning and constitutes a key element of machine learning methodology. In line with the statistical tradition, uncertainty has long been perceived as almost synonymous with standard probability and probabilistic predictions. Yet, due to the steadily increasing relevance of machine learning for practical applications and related issues such as safety requirements, new problems and challenges have recently been identified by machine learning scholars, and these problems may call for new methodological developments. In particular, this includes the importance of distinguishing between (at least) two different types of uncertainty, often refereed to as aleatoric and epistemic. In this paper, we provide an introduction to the topic of uncertainty in machine learning as well as an overview of hitherto attempts at handling uncertainty in general and formalizing this distinction in particular.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for robust and interpretable machine learning systems that integrates uncertainty-aware classification with out-of-distribution detection and selective prediction. Building on recent advances in consistent multiclass classification with a reject option, Bayesian deep learning for uncertainty quantification, and conformal prediction, we propose a hybrid approach that combines the strengths of evidential deep learning, Deep k-Nearest Neighbors (DkNN), and portfolio-inspired selective classification. Our method enables models to explicitly quantify both epistemic and aleatoric uncertainties, dynamically abstain from uncertain predictions, and detect out-of-distribution examples with high accuracy. By incorporating interpretable decision strategies and leveraging efficient model scaling techniques, we achieve state-of-the-art performance on benchmark datasets while maintaining strong robustness against adversarial perturbations and ensuring safety in cyber-physical systems. The proposed framework provides a principled way to balance accuracy, reliability, and interpretability in real-world applications.

original_abstract: We propose a novel method to efficiently estimate the spatial layout of a room from a single monocular RGB image. As existing approaches based on low-level feature extraction, followed by a vanishing point estimation are very slow and often unreliable in realistic scenarios, we build on semantic segmentation of the input image. To obtain better segmentations, we introduce a robust, accurate and very efficient hypothesize-and-test scheme. The key idea is to use three segmentation hypotheses, each based on a different number of visible walls.
