Our goal is to show that AutoML can go further: it is possible today to automatically discover complete machine learning algorithms just using basic mathematical operations as building blocks. We demonstrate this by introducing a novel framework that significantly reduces human bias through a generic search space. Despite the vastness of this space, evolutionary search can still discover two-layer neural networks trained by backpropagation. These simple neural networks can then be surpassed by evolving directly on tasks of interest, e.g. CIFAR-10 variants, where modern techniques emerge in the top algorithms, such as bilinear interactions, normalized gradients, and weight averaging. Moreover, evolution adapts algorithms to different task types: e.g., dropout-like techniques appear when little data is available. We believe these preliminary successes in discovering machine learning algorithms from scratch indicate a promising new direction for the field.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a unified framework for automated deep learning that jointly optimizes neural network architectures, hyperparameters, and optimization algorithms using a combination of reinforcement learning, gradient-based methods, and evolutionary strategies. By integrating advances from neural architecture search, differentiable architecture search, and learned optimization, our approach enables the end-to-end discovery of high-performing models tailored to specific tasks. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our method on image classification and language modeling benchmarks, achieving state-of-the-art performance with significantly reduced computational cost compared to existing techniques. Our framework supports modular and programmable search spaces, allowing for flexible application across diverse domains, and introduces novel optimization strategies that generalize across tasks. The proposed method not only automates the design of deep learning systems but also enhances their adaptability and efficiency in real-world applications.

original_abstract: In this paper, we study the resource allocation and trajectory design for secure unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-enabled communication systems, where multiple multi-purpose UAV base stations are dispatched to provide secure communications to multiple legitimate ground users (GUs) in the existence of multiple eavesdroppers (Eves). Specifically, by leveraging orthogonal frequency division multiple access (OFDMA), active UAV base stations can communicate to their desired ground users via the assigned subcarriers while idle UAV base stations can serve as jammer simultaneously for communication security provisioning. To achieve fairness in secure communication, we maximize the average minimum secrecy rate per user by jointly optimizing the communication/jamming subcarrier allocation policy and the trajectory of UAVs, while taking into account the constraints on the minimum safety distance among multiple UAVs, the maximum cruising speed, the initial/final locations, and the existence of cylindrical no-fly zones (NFZs). The design is formulated as a mixed integer non-convex optimization problem which is generally intractable. Subsequently, a computationally-efficient iterative algorithm is proposed to obtain a suboptimal solution. Simulation results illustrate that the performance of the proposed iterative algorithm can significantly improve the average minimum secrecy rate compared to various baseline schemes.
generated_abstract: This paper presents a novel framework for secure UAV communications by integrating trajectory optimization, power control, and cooperative jamming strategies to enhance physical-layer security in the presence of multiple eavesdroppers. Building on prior works that focus on trajectory design and power allocation, we extend the problem to include cooperative jamming by a secondary UAV, which transmits jamming signals to degrade eavesdropper channels. The proposed approach jointly optimizes the trajectories and transmit powers of both the legitimate UAV and the jammer, while considering practical constraints such as no-fly zones, maximum speed, and energy efficiency. To address the non-convexity of the optimization problem, we employ an iterative algorithm based on block coordinate descent, successive convex optimization, and the S-procedure. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method significantly improves the average worst-case secrecy rate and secrecy energy efficiency compared to existing benchmark schemes, while effectively handling uncertainties in eavesdropper locations and ensuring compliance with operational constraints.

original_abstract: Exact pattern matching in labeled graphs is the problem of searching paths of a graph $G=(V,E)$ that spell the same string as the given pattern $P[1..m]$. This basic problem can be found at the heart of more complex operations on variation graphs in computational biology, query operations in graph databases, and analysis of heterogeneous networks, where the nodes of some paths must match a sequence of labels or types. In our recent work we described a conditional lower bound stating that the exact pattern matching problem in labeled graphs cannot be solved in less than quadratic time, namely, $O(|E|^{1 - \epsilon} \, m)$ time or $O(|E| \, m^{1 - \epsilon})$ time for any constant $\epsilon>0$, unless the Strong Exponential Time Hypothesis (SETH) is false. The result holds even if node labels and pattern $P$ are drawn from a binary alphabet, and $G$ is restricted to undirected graphs of maximum degree three or directed acyclic graphs of maximum sum of indegree and outdegree three. It was left open what happens on undirected graphs of maximum degree two, i.e., when the pattern can have a zig-zag match in a (cyclic) bidirectional string. Also, the reduction created a non-determistic directed acyclic graph, and it was left open if determinism would make the problem easier. In this work, we show through the Orthogonal Vectors hypothesis (OV) that the same conditional lower bound holds even for these restricted cases.
generated_abstract: We present a novel approach for exact pattern matching in labeled graphs by combining techniques from Wheeler graph theory and conditional lower bounds under the Strong Exponential Time Hypothesis (SETH). Leveraging the path coherence property of Wheeler graphs, we design a framework that enables efficient indexing and querying of graph-based languages. Our results show that, despite the NP-completeness of recognizing general Wheeler graphs, the problem becomes tractable for deterministic finite automata (DFAs), allowing for polynomial-time minimization and prefix sorting. We demonstrate that exact pattern matching on graphs with binary labels and bounded degree cannot be solved in strongly subquadratic time unless SETH is false, aligning with known hardness results for string-based problems such as edit distance and longest common subsequence. Furthermore, we show that our framework can be used to improve the runtime of the Viterbi algorithm for Hidden Markov Models under certain conditions, and we provide a unified perspective on the complexity of regular expression matching and graph-based pattern matching. Our work bridges the gap between theoretical lower bounds and practical algorithms, offering new insights into the limits of efficient computation on structured data.

original_abstract: Detection identifies objects as axis-aligned boxes in an image. Most successful object detectors enumerate a nearly exhaustive list of potential object locations and classify each. This is wasteful, inefficient, and requires additional post-processing. In this paper, we take a different approach. We model an object as a single point --- the center point of its bounding box. Our detector uses keypoint estimation to find center points and regresses to all other object properties, such as size, 3D location, orientation, and even pose. Our center point based approach, CenterNet, is end-to-end differentiable, simpler, faster, and more accurate than corresponding bounding box based detectors. CenterNet achieves the best speed-accuracy trade-off on the MS COCO dataset, with 28.1% AP at 142 FPS, 37.4% AP at 52 FPS, and 45.1% AP with multi-scale testing at 1.4 FPS. We use the same approach to estimate 3D bounding box in the KITTI benchmark and human pose on the COCO keypoint dataset. Our method performs competitively with sophisticated multi-stage methods and runs in real-time.
generated_abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel object detection framework that integrates the strengths of single-shot detection, scale-aware feature learning, and bottom-up keypoint estimation. Building on SSD's efficient single-stage detection, TridentNet's multi-branch architecture for handling scale variation, and CornerNet's and Bottom-Up Detection's keypoint-based approaches, our method combines scale-specific feature maps with a unified keypoint estimation strategy to detect objects as paired corners and grouped extreme points. This approach eliminates the need for anchor boxes and region proposals while maintaining high accuracy across varying object scales and sizes. Experimental results on the COCO and PASCAL VOC datasets demonstrate competitive performance with state-of-the-art methods, achieving a mean average precision (mAP) of 48.8% on COCO test-dev, while maintaining real-time inference speeds. Our framework provides a flexible and unified solution for accurate and efficient object detection.

original_abstract: We show that there is a sequence of explicit multilinear polynomials $P_n(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\in \mathbb{R}[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ with non-negative coefficients that lies in monotone VNP such that any monotone algebraic circuit for $P_n$ must have size $\exp(\Omega(n)).$ This builds on (and strengthens) a result of Yehudayoff (2018) who showed a lower bound of $\exp(\tilde{\Omega}(\sqrt{n})).$
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel application combining insights from knowledge compilation, communication complexity, and expander graph theory. Leveraging the exponential lower bounds on DNNF size for expander-based CNFs and the hierarchical complexity results from multi-partition communication protocols, we demonstrate that certain classes of Boolean functions derived from expander graphs are inherently intractable for both DNNF representations and multi-partition protocols. By integrating the zig-zag product construction for expanders with the entropy wave intuition, we design a family of functions that exhibit strong separations in computational complexity across different models, including tropical circuits and dynamic programming. These results not only resolve open questions in knowledge compilation and communication complexity but also highlight the fundamental role of expander graphs in delineating complexity boundaries in algebraic and Boolean computation.

original_abstract: We tackle the problem of Human Locomotion Forecasting, a task for jointly predicting the spatial positions of several keypoints on the human body in the near future under an egocentric setting. In contrast to the previous work that aims to solve either the task of pose prediction or trajectory forecasting in isolation, we propose a framework to unify the two problems and address the practically useful task of pedestrian locomotion prediction in the wild. Among the major challenges in solving this task is the scarcity of annotated egocentric video datasets with dense annotations for pose, depth, or egomotion. To surmount this difficulty, we use state-of-the-art models to generate (noisy) annotations and propose robust forecasting models that can learn from this noisy supervision. We present a method to disentangle the overall pedestrian motion into easier to learn subparts by utilizing a pose completion and a decomposition module. The completion module fills in the missing key-point annotations and the decomposition module breaks the cleaned locomotion down to global (trajectory) and local (pose keypoint movements). Further, with Quasi RNN as our backbone, we propose a novel hierarchical trajectory forecasting network that utilizes low-level vision domain specific signals like egomotion and depth to predict the global trajectory. Our method leads to state-of-the-art results for the prediction of human locomotion in the egocentric view.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework that integrates spatio-temporal graph structures with deep recurrent neural networks (RNNs) and game-theoretic principles to model and predict complex human and pedestrian dynamics in interactive environments. By leveraging the hierarchical structure of spatio-temporal graphs, the proposed method enables the modeling of high-level interactions and dependencies among agents, while RNNs provide the temporal modeling capability essential for motion prediction. Additionally, the framework incorporates social and physical attention mechanisms to account for both the implicit cooperation among pedestrians and the influence of environmental context. The model is evaluated on multiple benchmark datasets, demonstrating significant improvements in accuracy, diversity, and realism of predicted trajectories compared to state-of-the-art methods. The approach is further extended to handle first-person video scenarios and long-term motion prediction, showcasing its versatility and effectiveness in a wide range of applications, including autonomous navigation and intelligent driving assistance systems.

original_abstract: Deep neural networks and in particular, deep neural classifiers have become an integral part of many modern applications. Despite their practical success, we still have limited knowledge of how they work and the demand for such an understanding is evergrowing. In this regard, one crucial aspect of deep neural network classifiers that can help us deepen our knowledge about their decision-making behavior is to investigate their decision boundaries. Nevertheless, this is contingent upon having access to samples populating the areas near the decision boundary. To achieve this, we propose a novel approach we call Deep Decision boundary Instance Generation (DeepDIG). DeepDIG utilizes a method based on adversarial example generation as an effective way of generating samples near the decision boundary of any deep neural network model. Then, we introduce a set of important principled characteristics that take advantage of the generated instances near the decision boundary to provide multifaceted understandings of deep neural networks. We have performed extensive experiments on multiple representative datasets across various deep neural network models and characterized their decision boundaries.
generated_abstract: This paper presents a novel framework that combines insights from the analysis of neural network decision boundaries, adversarial robustness, and automated testing methodologies to enhance the reliability and interpretability of deep learning systems. Building on findings that highlight the discontinuous nature of deep networks and the vulnerability to adversarial examples, we propose a unified approach that leverages curvature regularization, boundary entropy analysis, and gradient-based optimization to systematically detect and mitigate adversarial vulnerabilities. Our method, which integrates neuron coverage metrics and multi-resolution perturbation analysis, enables efficient identification of corner cases and adversarial inputs across diverse domains, including image and text processing. Furthermore, we demonstrate how curvature-based regularization can improve model robustness by promoting quasi-linear behavior in decision boundaries, while zoNNscan provides a principled way to quantify boundary uncertainty. Experimental results on multiple datasets show that our approach not only identifies previously undetected adversarial behaviors but also improves model accuracy and robustness, offering a comprehensive solution for testing and securing deep learning systems in safety-critical applications.

original_abstract: Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) learn filters in order to capture local correlation patterns in feature space. In this paper we propose to revert to learning combinations of preset spectral filters by switching to CNNs with harmonic blocks. We rely on the use of the Discrete Cosine Transform (DCT) filters which have excellent energy compaction properties and are widely used for image compression. The proposed harmonic blocks rely on DCT-modeling and replace conventional convolutional layers to produce partially or fully harmonic versions of new or existing CNN architectures. We demonstrate how the harmonic networks can be efficiently compressed in a straightforward manner by truncating high-frequency information in harmonic blocks which is possible due to the redundancies in the spectral domain. We report extensive experimental validation demonstrating the benefits of the introduction of harmonic blocks into state-of-the-art CNN models in image classification, segmentation and edge detection applications.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel deep convolutional neural network architecture that combines the strengths of residual learning, clustered convolutional kernels, and efficient model scaling to achieve state-of-the-art performance in image recognition and transfer learning tasks. By integrating residual blocks for improved depth, clustered kernel optimization for automatic architecture refinement, and compound scaling techniques for balanced model growth, our approach significantly enhances accuracy while maintaining computational efficiency. Experimental results on ImageNet, CIFAR-100, and COCO demonstrate superior performance compared to existing models, with notable improvements in top-1 accuracy, inference speed, and parameter efficiency. Additionally, the proposed architecture exhibits strong transferability across diverse datasets, achieving new benchmarks in classification and object detection.

original_abstract: Visual navigation tasks in real-world environments often require both self-motion and place recognition feedback. While deep reinforcement learning has shown success in solving these perception and decision-making problems in an end-to-end manner, these algorithms require large amounts of experience to learn navigation policies from high-dimensional data, which is generally impractical for real robots due to sample complexity. In this paper, we address these problems with two main contributions. We first leverage place recognition and deep learning techniques combined with goal destination feedback to generate compact, bimodal image representations that can then be used to effectively learn control policies from a small amount of experience. Second, we present an interactive framework, CityLearn, that enables for the first time training and deployment of navigation algorithms across city-sized, realistic environments with extreme visual appearance changes. CityLearn features more than 10 benchmark datasets, often used in visual place recognition and autonomous driving research, including over 100 recorded traversals across 60 cities around the world. We evaluate our approach on two CityLearn environments, training our navigation policy on a single traversal. Results show our method can be over 2 orders of magnitude faster than when using raw images, and can also generalize across extreme visual changes including day to night and summer to winter transitions.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel visual place recognition and navigation framework that integrates deep learning, semantic understanding, and robustness to viewpoint and appearance changes. Building on recent advances in CNN-based place recognition, semantic-aware descriptors, and reinforcement learning, we propose a system that combines spatial and sequential filtering, omnidirectional vision, and cross-view policy learning to achieve accurate and invariant place recognition under extreme conditions. Our approach leverages semantic segmentation for place categorization, utilizes a large-scale dataset for training viewpoint-invariant features, and incorporates reinforcement learning for end-to-end navigation in complex, real-world environments. Experimental results on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate significant improvements in recall, precision, and navigation accuracy, particularly in scenarios with large viewpoint changes and environmental variations. The proposed method enables robust, map-free navigation in cities and supports generalization across unseen environments, offering a promising direction for autonomous systems and intelligent agents.

original_abstract: In this paper, we propose Weight Standardization (WS) to accelerate deep network training. WS is targeted at the micro-batch training setting where each GPU typically has only 1-2 images for training. The micro-batch training setting is hard because small batch sizes are not enough for training networks with Batch Normalization (BN), while other normalization methods that do not rely on batch knowledge still have difficulty matching the performances of BN in large-batch training. Our WS ends this problem because when used with Group Normalization and trained with 1 image/GPU, WS is able to match or outperform the performances of BN trained with large batch sizes with only 2 more lines of code. In micro-batch training, WS significantly outperforms other normalization methods. WS achieves these superior results by standardizing the weights in the convolutional layers, which we show is able to smooth the loss landscape by reducing the Lipschitz constants of the loss and the gradients. The effectiveness of WS is verified on many tasks, including image classification, object detection, instance segmentation, video recognition, semantic segmentation, and point cloud recognition. The code is available here: https://github.com/joe-siyuan-qiao/WeightStandardization.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel deep learning architecture that combines the strengths of residual learning, dense connectivity, and advanced normalization techniques to achieve state-of-the-art performance in image recognition and related tasks. Building on residual networks, which enable the training of substantially deeper models, and dense connections, which enhance feature propagation and reuse, we incorporate Switchable Normalization (SN) and its sparse variant (SSN) to address the limitations of traditional normalization methods. These normalization strategies allow the model to dynamically select the most appropriate normalization scheme for each layer, ensuring robustness across varying batch sizes and reducing redundant computations. Our approach is evaluated on multiple benchmark datasets, including ImageNet, COCO, and Cityscapes, where it demonstrates superior accuracy and efficiency compared to existing methods. The proposed architecture not only advances the understanding of normalization techniques but also provides a flexible and powerful framework for future research in deep learning.

original_abstract: This paper proposes a novel weakly-supervised semantic segmentation method using image-level label only. The class-specific activation maps from the well-trained classifiers are used as cues to train a segmentation network. The well-known defects of these cues are coarseness and incompleteness. We use super-pixel to refine them, and fuse the cues extracted from both a color image trained classifier and a gray image trained classifier to compensate for their incompleteness. The conditional random field is adapted to regulate the training process and to refine the outputs further. Besides initializing the segmentation network, the previously trained classifier is also used in the testing phase to suppress the non-existing classes. Experimental results on the PASCAL VOC 2012 dataset illustrate the effectiveness of our method.
generated_abstract: This paper presents a novel weakly supervised semantic segmentation framework that integrates multiple strategies for improving localization accuracy and segmentation quality using only image-level labels. By combining foreground/background masks derived from pre-trained network activations, class-specific pixel discovery through saliency and attention maps, and iterative refinement using seeded region growing and object feature mining, our approach effectively addresses the challenges of weak supervision. The proposed method incorporates principles of seeding, expanding, and constraining segmentations, while leveraging saliency-guided expansion and deep seeded region growing to generate accurate pixel-level annotations. Experimental results on the PASCAL VOC 2012 dataset demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance, with an mIoU of 63.2% on the test set, outperforming existing weakly supervised approaches.

original_abstract: We investigate a framework for machine reading, inspired by real world information-seeking problems, where a meta question answering system interacts with a black box environment. The environment encapsulates a competitive machine reader based on BERT, providing candidate answers to questions, and possibly some context. To validate the realism of our formulation, we ask humans to play the role of a meta-answerer. With just a small snippet of text around an answer, humans can outperform the machine reader, improving recall. Similarly, a simple machine meta-answerer outperforms the environment, improving both precision and recall on the Natural Questions dataset. The system relies on joint training of answer scoring and the selection of conditioning information.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework that combines synthetic question generation with adversarial evaluation and active question reformulation to enhance the robustness and accuracy of reading comprehension systems. Building on the Stanford Question Answering Dataset (SQuAD) and its adversarial extension SQuAD 2.0, we generate synthetic question-answer pairs using roundtrip consistency to expand training data and improve model generalization. We incorporate adversarial examples to evaluate and strengthen models against deceptive text, ensuring they can distinguish between answerable and unanswerable questions. Additionally, we integrate an active question reformulation agent trained via reinforcement learning to iteratively refine queries and improve answer quality. Our approach demonstrates significant improvements in F1 scores on SQuAD 2.0 and Natural Questions (NQ), while also showing resilience against adversarial perturbations. The framework enables scalable, interactive question answering by jointly learning retrieval and comprehension, and it outperforms existing methods in both open-domain and adversarial settings.

original_abstract: Over any discrete memoryless channel, we build codes such that: for one, their block error probabilities and code rates scale like random codes'; and for two, their encoding and decoding complexities scale like polar codes'. Quantitatively, for any constants $\pi,\rho>0$ such that $\pi+2\rho 1$, no such codes exist for generic channels regardless of alphabet and complexity.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel coding scheme that combines the principles of relaxed polar codes with advanced kernel-based polarization techniques to achieve near-optimal scaling and significantly improved finite-length performance. By relaxing the polarization of both very good and very bad bit-channels, we reduce the encoding and decoding complexities while maintaining the capacity-achieving property. The use of large kernels enables the construction of polar codes with a scaling exponent approaching the optimal value of 2, achieving block lengths of $O(1/\varepsilon^{2+\delta})$ for a given gap $\varepsilon$ to capacity. The proposed method generalizes polarization to arbitrary discrete memoryless channels and demonstrates improved error performance and reduced latency for both binary erasure and additive white Gaussian noise channels. The resulting codes offer quasi-linear complexity in construction, encoding, and decoding, making them highly efficient for practical implementation.

original_abstract: Community detection is a fundamental problem in social network analysis consisting, roughly speaking, in dividing social actors (modelled as nodes in a social graph) with certain social connections (modelled as edges in the social graph) into densely knitted and highly related groups with each group well separated from the others. Classical approaches for community detection usually deal only with the structure of the network and ignore features of the nodes, although major real-world networks provide additional actors' information such as age, gender, interests, etc., traditionally called node attributes. It is known that the attributes may clarify and enrich the knowledge about the actors and give sense to the detected communities. This has led to a relatively novel direction in community detection --- constructing algorithms that use both the structure and the attributes of the network (modelled already via a node-attributed graph) to yield more informative and qualitative results. During the last decade many methods based on different ideas and techniques have appeared in this direction. Although there exist some partial overviews of them, a recent survey is a necessity as the growing number of the methods may cause uncertainty in practice. In this paper we aim at clarifying the overall situation by proposing a clear classification of the methods and providing a comprehensive survey of the available results. We not only group and analyse the corresponding methods but also focus on practical aspects, including the information which methods outperform others and which datasets and quality measures are used for evaluation.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel community detection framework that integrates network structure, node attributes, and contextual knowledge to uncover overlapping and semantically coherent communities in attributed networks. Building on existing methods that combine topological and attribute-based information, we propose a coupled node similarity model that captures hierarchical interactions between attributes, nodes, and network structure. Additionally, we incorporate knowledge graphs to enhance the contextual relevance of node attributes, enabling the discovery of communities defined by abstract concepts. Our approach formulates the community detection problem as a nonnegative matrix factorization task, leveraging both attribute-enhanced node similarity and community structure embedding. Extensive experiments on real-world and synthetic attributed networks demonstrate that our method significantly outperforms state-of-the-art algorithms in terms of accuracy, robustness to noise, and ability to detect overlapping communities. The proposed framework provides a scalable and interpretable solution for analyzing complex networks with rich node features.

original_abstract: A set of about 80 researchers, practitioners, and federal agency program managers participated in the NSF-sponsored Grand Challenges in Resilience Workshop held on Purdue campus on March 19-21, 2019. The workshop was divided into three themes: resilience in cyber, cyber-physical, and socio-technical systems. About 30 attendees in all participated in the discussions of cyber resilience. This article brings out the substantive parts of the challenges and solution approaches that were identified in the cyber resilience theme. In this article, we put forward the substantial challenges in cyber resilience in a few representative application domains and outline foundational solutions to address these challenges. These solutions fall into two broad themes: resilience-by-design and resilience-by-reaction. We use examples of autonomous systems as the application drivers motivating cyber resilience. We focus on some autonomous systems in the near horizon (autonomous ground and aerial vehicles) and also a little more distant (autonomous rescue and relief). #R##N#For resilience-by-design, we focus on design methods in software that are needed for our cyber systems to be resilient. In contrast, for resilience-by-reaction, we discuss how to make systems resilient by responding, reconfiguring, or recovering at runtime when failures happen. We also discuss the notion of adaptive execution to improve resilience, execution transparently and adaptively among available execution platforms (mobile/embedded, edge, and cloud). For each of the two themes, we survey the current state, and the desired state and ways to get there. We conclude the paper by looking at the research challenges we will have to solve in the short and the mid-term to make the vision of resilient autonomous systems a reality.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework that combines adversarial training, formal safety analysis, and automated testing to enhance the robustness and reliability of deep neural networks (DNNs) in adversarial settings. Building on recent advances in adversarial example generation, such as DeepFool and the limitations of defensive distillation, we propose an integrated approach that leverages adversarial training at scale, as demonstrated on ImageNet, to improve resistance against both single-step and multi-step attacks. We incorporate formal safety analysis techniques to rigorously verify robustness properties and identify concrete counterexamples, enabling the detection of adversarial vulnerabilities in large-scale DNNs. Additionally, we integrate coverage-guided fuzzing methods, as exemplified by TensorFuzz, to systematically uncover rare input behaviors that may lead to misclassifications. Our framework also utilizes neuron coverage and differential behavior optimization, as introduced in DeepXplore, to ensure comprehensive testing of DNNs. By combining these approaches, we demonstrate significant improvements in robustness, safety verification, and error detection, offering a comprehensive solution for deploying DNNs in security- and safety-critical applications.

original_abstract: In this paper, we consider the problem of solving semantic tasks such as `Visual Question Answering' (VQA), where one aims to answers related to an image and `Visual Question Generation' (VQG), where one aims to generate a natural question pertaining to an image. Solutions for VQA and VQG tasks have been proposed using variants of encoder-decoder deep learning based frameworks that have shown impressive performance. Humans however often show generalization by relying on exemplar based approaches. For instance, the work by Tversky and Kahneman suggests that humans use exemplars when making categorizations and decisions. In this work, we propose the incorporation of exemplar based approaches towards solving these problems. Specifically, we incorporate exemplar based approaches and show that an exemplar based module can be incorporated in almost any of the deep learning architectures proposed in the literature and the addition of such a block results in improved performance for solving these tasks. Thus, just as the incorporation of attention is now considered de facto useful for solving these tasks, similarly, incorporating exemplars also can be considered to improve any proposed architecture for solving this task. We provide extensive empirical analysis for the same through various architectures, ablations, and state of the art comparisons.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel end-to-end framework for Visual Question Answering (VQA) that integrates multimodal convolutional networks, stacked attention mechanisms, and question-guided spatial reasoning. By combining the strengths of CNN-based image and question encoding, stacked attention networks for progressive reasoning, and spatial attention for region selection, our model effectively captures both visual and linguistic features while reasoning about their interactions. Additionally, we incorporate external knowledge sources to address complex questions that require information beyond the image content. The proposed architecture is evaluated on benchmark datasets including DAQUAR, COCO-QA, and VQA, achieving state-of-the-art performance and demonstrating superior accuracy and robustness in answering a wide range of image-based questions.

original_abstract: The problem of generalizing deep neural networks from multiple source domains to a target one is studied under two settings: When unlabeled target data is available, it is a multi-source unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) problem, otherwise a domain generalization (DG) problem. We propose a unified framework termed domain adaptive ensemble learning (DAEL) to address both problems. A DAEL model is composed of a CNN feature extractor shared across domains and multiple classifier heads each trained to specialize in a particular source domain. Each such classifier is an expert to its own domain and a non-expert to others. DAEL aims to learn these experts collaboratively so that when forming an ensemble, they can leverage complementary information from each other to be more effective for an unseen target domain. To this end, each source domain is used in turn as a pseudo-target-domain with its own expert providing supervision signal to the ensemble of non-experts learned from the other sources. For unlabeled target data under the UDA setting where real expert does not exist, DAEL uses pseudo-label to supervise the ensemble learning. Extensive experiments on three multi-source UDA datasets and two DG datasets show that DAEL improves the state-of-the-art on both problems, often by significant margins. The code is released at \url{this https URL}.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for unsupervised domain adaptation that integrates multiple state-of-the-art techniques to enhance feature transferability and classification performance across domains. Building on joint adaptation networks, adversarial discriminative domain adaptation, contrastive adaptation networks, and maximum classifier discrepancy methods, our approach combines distribution alignment strategies with task-specific decision boundary modeling to address misalignment and ambiguity in feature spaces. By incorporating a unified embedding subspace learning mechanism, residual transfer networks, and conditional adversarial training, the proposed method effectively reduces domain discrepancy while preserving discriminative power. The framework is trained end-to-end with an alternating update strategy and achieves superior performance on benchmark datasets for image classification and semantic segmentation, demonstrating robustness to large domain shifts and improved generalization capabilities.

original_abstract: Studying the ways in which language is gendered has long been an area of interest in sociolinguistics. Studies have explored, for example, the speech of male and female characters in film and the language used to describe male and female politicians. In this paper, we aim not to merely study this phenomenon qualitatively, but instead to quantify the degree to which the language used to describe men and women is different and, moreover, different in a positive or negative way. To that end, we introduce a generative latent-variable model that jointly represents adjective (or verb) choice, with its sentiment, given the natural gender of a head (or dependent) noun. We find that there are significant differences between descriptions of male and female nouns and that these differences align with common gender stereotypes: Positive adjectives used to describe women are more often related to their bodies than adjectives used to describe men.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel application of adaptive optimization techniques in mitigating gender bias within natural language processing models. Building on the Adam optimization algorithm, we propose a framework that integrates corpus-level constraints and debiasing strategies to reduce the amplification of gender stereotypes in word embeddings and structured prediction models. By leveraging the computational efficiency and adaptability of Adam, our method effectively calibrates models trained on biased datasets, such as those found in social media and web corpora, while preserving their performance on core tasks. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach on benchmark datasets, showing significant reductions in gender bias without compromising model accuracy. Furthermore, we incorporate insights from social theory and lexical variation studies to better understand the interplay between language use, social networks, and gender identity, offering a multidisciplinary perspective on bias mitigation in AI systems.

original_abstract: Spatial modulation (SM) is an innovative and promising digital modulation technology that strikes an appealing trade-off between spectral efficiency and energy efficiency with a simple design philosophy. SM enjoys plenty of benefits and shows great potential to fulfill the requirements of future wireless communications. The key idea behind SM is to convey additional information typically through the ON/OFF states of transmit antennas and simultaneously save the implementation cost by reducing the number of radio frequency chains. As a result, the SM concept can have widespread effects on diverse applications and can be applied in other signal domains such as frequency/time/code/angle domain or even across multiple domains. This survey provides a comprehensive overview of the latest results and progresses in SM research. Specifically, the fundamental principles, variants of system design, and enhancements of SM are described in detail. Furthermore, the integration of the SM family with other promising techniques, applications to emerging communication systems, and extensions to new signal domains are also extensively studied.
generated_abstract: This paper presents a novel integrated framework combining spatial modulation (SM) with non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) and generalized spatial modulation (GSM) techniques to enhance the spectral efficiency and system performance of downlink multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) communications. By leveraging the index modulation concept of SM and the power domain multiplexing of NOMA, the proposed scheme effectively mitigates inter-user interference while maintaining high bandwidth efficiency. The framework incorporates a unified precoding design for GSM systems, which is applicable for all antenna activation configurations and significantly improves error performance. Additionally, a computationally efficient encoding method and low-complexity detection algorithms are introduced to reduce implementation complexity. The achievable spectral efficiency is characterized using mutual information (MI) and validated through theoretical analysis and simulation results, demonstrating significant performance gains over conventional orthogonal multiple access and antenna-grouping-based schemes in various channel conditions.

original_abstract: In person re-identification (Re-ID), supervised methods usually need a large amount of expensive label information, while unsupervised ones are still unable to deliver satisfactory identification performance. In this paper, we introduce a novel person Re-ID task called unsupervised cross-camera person Re-ID, which only needs the within-camera (intra-camera) label information but not cross-camera (inter-camera) labels which are more expensive to obtain. In real-world applications, the intra-camera label information can be easily captured by tracking algorithms or few manual annotations. In this situation, the main challenge becomes the distribution discrepancy across different camera views, caused by the various body pose, occlusion, image resolution, illumination conditions, and background noises in different cameras. To address this situation, we propose a novel Adversarial Camera Alignment Network (ACAN) for unsupervised cross-camera person Re-ID. It consists of the camera-alignment task and the supervised within-camera learning task. To achieve the camera alignment, we develop a Multi-Camera Adversarial Learning (MCAL) to map images of different cameras into a shared subspace. Particularly, we investigate two different schemes, including the existing GRL (i.e., gradient reversal layer) scheme and the proposed scheme called "other camera equiprobability" (OCE), to conduct the multi-camera adversarial task. Based on this shared subspace, we then leverage the within-camera labels to train the network. Extensive experiments on five large-scale datasets demonstrate the superiority of ACAN over multiple state-of-the-art unsupervised methods that take advantage of labeled source domains and generated images by GAN-based models. In particular, we verify that the proposed multi-camera adversarial task does contribute to the significant improvement.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel unsupervised cross-dataset person re-identification framework that integrates multiple advanced techniques for domain adaptation and feature learning. Building on methods such as transfer learning of spatio-temporal patterns, attribute-identity joint learning, mid-level feature alignment, tracklet association, camera-aware domain adaptation, adversarial transfer, and view-invariant subspace learning, our approach combines these strategies into a unified model to address the challenges of domain discrepancy, lack of labeled data, and intra-/inter-dataset variations. The proposed method leverages both visual and semantic features, incorporates camera-specific adaptation, and utilizes unsupervised learning mechanisms to enhance feature generalization and discriminative power across different domains. Experimental results on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that our framework significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art unsupervised and domain adaptation methods for person re-identification.

original_abstract: This paper addresses unsupervised domain adaptation, the setting where labeled training data is available on a source domain, but the goal is to have good performance on a target domain with only unlabeled data. Like much of previous work, we seek to align the learned representations of the source and target domains while preserving discriminability. The way we accomplish alignment is by learning to perform auxiliary self-supervised task(s) on both domains simultaneously. Each self-supervised task brings the two domains closer together along the direction relevant to that task. Training this jointly with the main task classifier on the source domain is shown to successfully generalize to the unlabeled target domain. The presented objective is straightforward to implement and easy to optimize. We achieve state-of-the-art results on four out of seven standard benchmarks, and competitive results on segmentation adaptation. We also demonstrate that our method composes well with another popular pixel-level adaptation method.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework that combines cycle-consistent adversarial domain adaptation, self-ensembling, and domain separation techniques to address the challenges of unsupervised visual domain adaptation. By integrating cycle-consistency constraints with discriminative adversarial learning, our model effectively aligns source and target domains at both pixel and feature levels without requiring labeled target data or aligned image pairs. Additionally, self-ensembling is employed to improve model robustness and generalization, while domain separation networks are utilized to explicitly model domain-specific and shared features, enhancing the extraction of domain-invariant representations. The proposed method achieves state-of-the-art performance on multiple benchmark tasks, including cross-domain digit classification, semantic segmentation, and object recognition, demonstrating its effectiveness in handling large domain shifts and generalizing to unseen classes.

original_abstract: Existing graph embedding models often have weaknesses in exploiting graph structure similarities, potential dependencies among nodes and global network properties. To this end, we present U2GAN, a novel unsupervised model leveraging on the strength of the recently introduced universal self-attention network (Dehghani et al., 2019), to learn low-dimensional embeddings of graphs which can be used for graph classification. In particular, given an input graph, U2GAN first applies a self-attention computation, which is then followed by a recurrent transition to iteratively memorize its attention on vector representations of each node and its neighbors across each iteration. Thus, U2GAN can address the weaknesses in the existing models in order to produce plausible node embeddings whose sum is the final embedding of the whole graph. Experimental results show that our unsupervised U2GAN produces new state-of-the-art performances on a range of well-known benchmark datasets for the graph classification task. It even outperforms supervised methods in most of benchmark cases.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for hierarchical graph representation learning that combines the strengths of convolutional neural networks for graphs, graph2vec embeddings, and differentiable pooling techniques. By integrating local graph convolution with global structural embeddings and hierarchical clustering, our approach enables efficient and expressive learning of graph-level representations. The model leverages relational inductive biases and message passing mechanisms to capture both local and global structural information, while the differentiable pooling module allows for the generation of multi-scale graph representations. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate significant improvements in graph classification and clustering tasks compared to existing methods, highlighting the effectiveness of the combined approach in capturing complex graph structures and relationships.

original_abstract: Explicit theory axioms are added by a saturation-based theorem prover as one of the techniques for supporting theory reasoning. While simple and effective, adding theory axioms can also pollute the search space with many irrelevant consequences. As a result, the prover often gets lost in parts of the search space where the chance to find a proof is low. In this paper we describe a new strategy for controlling the amount of reasoning with explicit theory axioms. The strategy refines a recently proposed two-layer-queue clause selection and combines it with a heuristical measure of the amount of theory reasoning in the derivation of a clause. We implemented the new strategy in the automatic theorem prover Vampire and present an evaluation showing that our work dramatically improves the state-of-the-art clause-selection strategy in the presence of theory axioms.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel application of advanced theorem proving techniques to the domain of network security analysis, combining the expressive power of first-order logic with a first-class boolean sort (FOOL), polymorphic arrays, and efficient quantified reasoning over term algebras. Building on the Vampire theorem prover's recent extensions and the trace logic framework for relational properties, we develop a new reasoning tool that enables automated verification of security-critical properties in cloud-based network configurations. Our approach encodes network reachability and compliance constraints into trace logic, leveraging FOOL's enhanced expressivity and efficient reasoning capabilities to handle complex quantified formulas arising from security policies. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this integration through an industrial case study involving AWS-based networks, showing that our method improves upon existing tools in both expressiveness and performance, enabling scalable and precise analysis of cloud infrastructure.

original_abstract: The role of robots in society keeps expanding, bringing with it the necessity of interacting and communicating with humans. In order to keep such interaction intuitive, we provide automatic wayfinding based on verbal navigational instructions. Our first contribution is the creation of a large-scale dataset with verbal navigation instructions. To this end, we have developed an interactive visual navigation environment based on Google Street View; we further design an annotation method to highlight mined anchor landmarks and local directions between them in order to help annotators formulate typical, human references to those. The annotation task was crowdsourced on the AMT platform, to construct a new Talk2Nav dataset with $10,714$ routes. Our second contribution is a new learning method. Inspired by spatial cognition research on the mental conceptualization of navigational instructions, we introduce a soft dual attention mechanism defined over the segmented language instructions to jointly extract two partial instructions -- one for matching the next upcoming visual landmark and the other for matching the local directions to the next landmark. On the similar lines, we also introduce spatial memory scheme to encode the local directional transitions. Our work takes advantage of the advance in two lines of research: mental formalization of verbal navigational instructions and training neural network agents for automatic way finding. Extensive experiments show that our method significantly outperforms previous navigation methods. For demo video, dataset and code, please refer to our project page: https://www.trace.ethz.ch/publications/2019/talk2nav/index.html
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel hybrid reinforcement learning framework that integrates model-free and model-based approaches with cognitive mapping, self-monitoring, and cross-modal reasoning to enhance vision-and-language navigation in complex, real-world environments. Building on prior advances in planned-ahead navigation, speaker-follower models, and cognitive mapping, our method combines a look-ahead policy with a dynamic environment model, a visual-textual co-grounding module, and a progress monitor to enable robust instruction following and generalization across unseen environments. Additionally, we incorporate reinforced cross-modal matching and self-supervised imitation learning to improve the alignment between language instructions and navigation trajectories, while a panoramic action space and pragmatic reasoning support more human-like decision-making. Evaluated on multiple benchmarks including Room-to-Room and StreetNav, our approach achieves significant improvements in success rates, with a 15.5% increase on unseen test sets and state-of-the-art performance across diverse navigation tasks.

original_abstract: Building upon the recent success of deep reinforcement learning methods, we investigate the possibility of on-policy reinforcement learning improvement by reusing the data from several consecutive policies. On-policy methods bring many benefits, such as ability to evaluate each resulting policy. However, they usually discard all the information about the policies which existed before. In this work, we propose adaptation of the replay buffer concept, borrowed from the off-policy learning setting, to create the method, combining advantages of on- and off-policy learning. To achieve this, the proposed algorithm generalises the $Q$-, value and advantage functions for data from multiple policies. The method uses trust region optimisation, while avoiding some of the common problems of the algorithms such as TRPO or ACKTR: it uses hyperparameters to replace the trust region selection heuristics, as well as the trainable covariance matrix instead of the fixed one. In many cases, the method not only improves the results comparing to the state-of-the-art trust region on-policy learning algorithms such as PPO, ACKTR and TRPO, but also with respect to their off-policy counterpart DDPG.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel deep reinforcement learning framework that combines trust region optimization, asynchronous training, and off-policy data utilization to achieve improved sample efficiency and stability in continuous control tasks. Building on generalized advantage estimation, trust region policy optimization, and asynchronous actor-critic methods, our approach integrates off-policy gradient estimation with on-policy updates using interpolated policy gradient techniques. We incorporate Kronecker-factored approximations for scalable natural gradient updates and employ experience replay to enhance data efficiency. The algorithm is evaluated on a range of challenging continuous control benchmarks, including 3D locomotion and visual navigation tasks, demonstrating superior performance in terms of sample efficiency, learning stability, and final policy quality compared to existing state-of-the-art methods.

original_abstract: Beam search optimization resolves many issues in neural machine translation. However, this method lacks principled stopping criteria and does not learn how to stop during training, and the model naturally prefers the longer hypotheses during the testing time in practice since they use the raw score instead of the probability-based score. We propose a novel ranking method which enables an optimal beam search stopping criteria. We further introduce a structured prediction loss function which penalizes suboptimal finished candidates produced by beam search during training. Experiments of neural machine translation on both synthetic data and real languages (German-to-English and Chinese-to-English) demonstrate our proposed methods lead to better length and BLEU score.
generated_abstract: This paper presents a novel end-to-end neural machine translation framework that integrates advanced sequence modeling techniques with optimized training and decoding strategies. Building on the encoder-decoder architecture with attention mechanisms, we incorporate soft alignment to enhance context modeling and employ minimum risk training to directly optimize translation quality with respect to evaluation metrics such as BLEU. To address the limitations of traditional beam search, we introduce an optimal beam search algorithm that dynamically determines when to terminate the search, ensuring the highest quality output while mitigating issues related to length bias and suboptimal beam sizes. Additionally, we leverage multi-reference training with pseudo-references to improve robustness and diversity in translation outputs. Experimental results demonstrate significant improvements in translation performance across multiple language pairs, outperforming existing state-of-the-art methods in both accuracy and efficiency.

original_abstract: This paper proposes a framework which is able to generate a sequence of three-dimensional human dance poses for a given music. The proposed framework consists of three components: a music feature encoder, a pose generator, and a music genre classifier. We focus on integrating these components for generating a realistic 3D human dancing move from music, which can be applied to artificial agents and humanoid robots. The trained dance pose generator, which is a generative autoregressive model, is able to synthesize a dance sequence longer than 5,000 pose frames. Experimental results of generated dance sequences from various songs show how the proposed method generates human-like dancing move to a given music. In addition, a generated 3D dance sequence is applied to a humanoid robot, showing that the proposed framework can make a robot to dance just by listening to music.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for generating music-driven choreography by integrating deep learning techniques from motion modeling, audio processing, and sequence generation. Building on systems such as chor-rnn and the auto-regressive encoder-decoder network, we propose a hybrid model that combines convolutional and recurrent architectures with quaternion-based motion representation to generate realistic and musically coherent dance sequences. Our approach leverages pre-trained deep representations for audio and motion, as explored in comparative studies on music representation learning, and incorporates multi-level feature aggregation and temporal indexing to enhance the alignment between musical structure and choreographic expression. The model is trained on a large-scale music-dance dataset and validated through both quantitative metrics and user studies, demonstrating its ability to produce natural, stylistically consistent dance movements that reflect the input music's rhythm, tempo, and emotional content. This work bridges the gap between audio and motion domains, offering a versatile tool for choreographic creation and human-machine collaboration in dance.

original_abstract: The merits of fast convergence and potentially better performance of the weight normalization family have drawn increasing attention in recent years. These methods use standardization or normalization that changes the weight $\boldsymbol{W}$ to $\boldsymbol{W}'$, which makes $\boldsymbol{W}'$ independent to the magnitude of $\boldsymbol{W}$. Surprisingly, $\boldsymbol{W}$ must be decayed during gradient descent, otherwise we will observe a severe under-fitting problem, which is very counter-intuitive since weight decay is widely known to prevent deep networks from over-fitting. In this paper, we \emph{theoretically} prove that the weight decay term $\frac{1}{2}\lambda||{\boldsymbol{W}}||^2$ merely modulates the effective learning rate for improving objective optimization, and has no influence on generalization when the weight normalization family is compositely employed. Furthermore, we also expose several critical problems when introducing weight decay term to weight normalization family, including the missing of global minimum and training instability. To address these problems, we propose an $\epsilon-$shifted $L_2$ regularizer, which shifts the $L_2$ objective by a positive constant $\epsilon$. Such a simple operation can theoretically guarantee the existence of global minimum, while preventing the network weights from being too small and thus avoiding gradient float overflow. It significantly improves the training stability and can achieve slightly better performance in our practice. The effectiveness of $\epsilon-$shifted $L_2$ regularizer is comprehensively validated on the ImageNet, CIFAR-100, and COCO datasets. Our codes and pretrained models will be released in this https URL.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel normalization framework that combines the benefits of weight normalization, group normalization, and switchable normalization to address the challenges of training deep neural networks with large minibatches and small batch sizes. By decoupling weight magnitudes from their directions and dynamically adapting normalization strategies across different layers and tasks, our approach improves optimization stability, accelerates convergence, and maintains high generalization performance. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this combined method on large-scale image classification tasks using ResNet-50 on ImageNet, achieving state-of-the-art accuracy with significantly reduced training time compared to traditional batch normalization and other normalization techniques. Our framework is particularly effective in micro-batch training scenarios and exhibits robustness across a wide range of batch sizes, making it suitable for both distributed and resource-constrained settings.

original_abstract: This work presents CLOTH3D, the first big scale synthetic dataset of 3D clothed human sequences. CLOTH3D contains a large variability on garment type, topology, shape, size, tightness and fabric. Clothes are simulated on top of thousands of different pose sequences and body shapes, generating realistic cloth dynamics. We provide the dataset with a generative model for cloth generation. We propose a Conditional Variational Auto-Encoder (CVAE) based on graph convolutions (GCVAE) to learn garment latent spaces. This allows for realistic generation of 3D garments on top of SMPL model for any pose and shape.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework that combines graph neural networks (GNNs) with synthetic data generation and 3D garment modeling to enable fast and accurate virtual dressing of 3D human avatars. By leveraging convolutional GNNs for learning graph-based representations of 3D human body and clothing structures, we integrate a synthetic dataset generation pipeline inspired by SURREAL to train deep models on large-scale, realistic, and annotated data. Our approach incorporates a conditional Mesh-VAE-GAN for generating diverse clothing geometries and a two-stream network architecture, similar to GarNet, to model cloth-body interactions efficiently. Additionally, we employ a multi-task curriculum transfer learning strategy to improve generalization across different body shapes and garment types. The proposed method achieves high-fidelity 3D cloth draping with minimal computational cost, enabling real-time applications such as virtual try-on and animation. Experimental results demonstrate superior performance in terms of accuracy, realism, and efficiency compared to existing methods, while also supporting detailed human shape estimation from clothed 3D scans and interactive garment design workflows.

original_abstract: We consider inpainting in an unsupervised setting where there is neither access to paired nor unpaired training data. The only available information is provided by the uncomplete observations and the inpainting process statistics. In this context, an observation should give rise to several plausible reconstructions which amounts at learning a distribution over the space of reconstructed images. We model the reconstruction process by using a conditional GAN with constraints on the stochastic component that introduce an explicit dependency between this component and the generated output. This allows us sampling from the latent component in order to generate a distribution of images associated to an observation. We demonstrate the capacity of our model on several image datasets: faces (CelebA), food images (Recipe-1M) and bedrooms (LSUN Bedrooms) with different types of imputation masks. The approach yields comparable performance to model variants trained with additional supervision.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for multimodal image inpainting that combines context-aware feature learning, cycle-consistent adversarial training, and latent code injection to address the challenges of filling in irregular and large missing regions with semantically coherent and diverse outputs. Building on context encoders, which learn rich visual representations through inpainting, we integrate a cycle-consistent adversarial network to enable unpaired learning and ensure consistency between the input and reconstructed image domains. To handle the ambiguity of inpainting tasks, we incorporate a latent code into the generator, allowing the model to sample from a distribution of plausible outputs and avoid mode collapse. Additionally, we employ partial convolutions and gated mechanisms to better handle irregular masks and improve texture synthesis. Our approach demonstrates superior performance on benchmark datasets, achieving both high perceptual quality and diversity in inpainted results, while maintaining computational efficiency.

original_abstract: Next-generation wireless networks (NGWN) have a substantial potential in terms of supporting a broad range of complex compelling applications both in military and civilian fields, where the users are able to enjoy high-rate, low-latency, low-cost and reliable information services. Achieving this ambitious goal requires new radio techniques for adaptive learning and intelligent decision making because of the complex heterogeneous nature of the network structures and wireless services. Machine learning algorithms have great success in supporting big data analytics, efficient parameter estimation and interactive decision making. Hence, in this article, we review the thirty-year history of machine learning by elaborating on supervised learning, unsupervised learning, reinforcement learning and deep learning, respectively. Furthermore, we investigate their employment in the compelling applications of NGWNs, including heterogeneous networks (HetNets), cognitive radios (CR), Internet of things (IoT), machine to machine networks (M2M), and so on. This article aims for assisting the readers in clarifying the motivation and methodology of the various machine learning algorithms, so as to invoke them for hitherto unexplored services as well as scenarios of future wireless networks.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework that integrates deep learning and reinforcement learning techniques to enhance the performance of wireless sensor networks (WSNs) in dynamic and unknown environments. By leveraging convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for wireless interference identification, deep Q-networks (DQNs) for dynamic multichannel access, and autoencoders for MIMO communications and channel estimation, the proposed system optimizes resource utilization, improves signal detection, and enhances spectrum efficiency. The framework enables adaptive transmission scheduling, optimal channel access, and robust interference management, all while minimizing computational overhead and power consumption. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the combined approach in achieving high classification accuracy, near-optimal throughput, and resilience to adversarial conditions, making it a promising solution for next-generation cognitive and IoT-based wireless networks.

original_abstract: What is the current state-of-the-art for image restoration and enhancement applied to degraded images acquired under less than ideal circumstances? Can the application of such algorithms as a pre-processing step to improve image interpretability for manual analysis or automatic visual recognition to classify scene content? While there have been important advances in the area of computational photography to restore or enhance the visual quality of an image, the capabilities of such techniques have not always translated in a useful way to visual recognition tasks. Consequently, there is a pressing need for the development of algorithms that are designed for the joint problem of improving visual appearance and recognition, which will be an enabling factor for the deployment of visual recognition tools in many real-world scenarios. To address this, we introduce the UG^2 dataset as a large-scale benchmark composed of video imagery captured under challenging conditions, and two enhancement tasks designed to test algorithmic impact on visual quality and automatic object recognition. Furthermore, we propose a set of metrics to evaluate the joint improvement of such tasks as well as individual algorithmic advances, including a novel psychophysics-based evaluation regime for human assessment and a realistic set of quantitative measures for object recognition performance. We introduce six new algorithms for image restoration or enhancement, which were created as part of the IARPA sponsored UG^2 Challenge workshop held at CVPR 2018. Under the proposed evaluation regime, we present an in-depth analysis of these algorithms and a host of deep learning-based and classic baseline approaches. From the observed results, it is evident that we are in the early days of building a bridge between computational photography and visual recognition, leaving many opportunities for innovation in this area.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel end-to-end framework that integrates deep learning techniques for robust image restoration under various quality distortions, including blur, noise, compression artifacts, and low resolution. Building on recent advances in deep convolutional networks, perceptual loss functions, and task-driven super-resolution, our approach combines automated texture synthesis, blind deblurring, and compression artifact reduction into a unified system. By leveraging residual learning, adversarial training, and multi-scale architectures, we achieve state-of-the-art performance in both quantitative and qualitative evaluations across diverse image restoration tasks. Furthermore, our method demonstrates significant improvements in downstream vision tasks such as object detection when applied as a preprocessing step, highlighting its practical utility in real-world applications.

original_abstract: A classifier trained on a dataset seldom works on other datasets obtained under different conditions due to domain shift. This problem is commonly addressed by domain adaptation methods. In this work we introduce a novel deep learning framework which unifies different paradigms in unsupervised domain adaptation. Specifically, we propose domain alignment layers which implement feature whitening for the purpose of matching source and target feature distributions. Additionally, we leverage the unlabeled target data by proposing the Min-Entropy Consensus loss, which regularizes training while avoiding the adoption of many user-defined hyper-parameters. We report results on publicly available datasets, considering both digit classification and object recognition tasks. We show that, in most of our experiments, our approach improves upon previous methods, setting new state-of-the-art performances.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for unsupervised domain adaptation that combines the strengths of multiple state-of-the-art techniques, including Adaptive Batch Normalization (AdaBN), Conditional Adversarial Domain Adaptation (CDAN), and Deep CORAL, with self-ensembling and domain separation strategies. By integrating AdaBN for feature normalization adaptation, CDAN for conditional adversarial alignment, and Deep CORAL for correlation-based distribution matching, our approach effectively reduces domain discrepancy while preserving discriminative information. Additionally, we incorporate self-ensembling to improve model robustness and domain separation networks to explicitly model domain-specific and shared features. The proposed method achieves superior performance on standard benchmark datasets, demonstrating its effectiveness in handling complex domain shifts with minimal reliance on labeled target data.

original_abstract: In order to answer semantically-complicated questions about an image, a Visual Question Answering (VQA) model needs to fully understand the visual scene in the image, especially the interactive dynamics between different objects. We propose a Relation-aware Graph Attention Network (ReGAT), which encodes each image into a graph and models multi-type inter-object relations via a graph attention mechanism, to learn question-adaptive relation representations. Two types of visual object relations are explored: (i) Explicit Relations that represent geometric positions and semantic interactions between objects; and (ii) Implicit Relations that capture the hidden dynamics between image regions. Experiments demonstrate that ReGAT outperforms prior state-of-the-art approaches on both VQA 2.0 and VQA-CP v2 datasets. We further show that ReGAT is compatible to existing VQA architectures, and can be used as a generic relation encoder to boost the model performance for VQA.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for Visual Question Answering (VQA) that integrates stacked attention networks, hierarchical co-attention mechanisms, graph-structured representations, and relational reasoning to address complex and diverse questions. By combining semantic attention with structured representations of both image content and question semantics, the model captures cross-region relationships and higher-level scene interactions. The framework leverages external knowledge sources and visual relation facts to enhance reasoning capabilities, particularly for questions requiring inference beyond the visual content. A multi-step attention mechanism, incorporating visual and semantic attention, is used to progressively refine the understanding of the question and image. Additionally, the model employs graph-based representations to capture question-specific interactions and utilizes relational reasoning to model complex visual and textual dependencies. Evaluated on multiple benchmark datasets, the proposed approach achieves state-of-the-art performance, demonstrating significant improvements in accuracy and interpretability.

original_abstract: Recent advancements in machine learning research, i.e., deep learning, introduced methods that excel conventional algorithms as well as humans in several complex tasks, ranging from detection of objects in images and speech recognition to playing difficult strategic games. However, the current methodology of machine learning research and consequently, implementations of the real-world applications of such algorithms, seems to have a recurring HARKing (Hypothesizing After the Results are Known) issue. In this work, we elaborate on the algorithmic, economic and social reasons and consequences of this phenomenon. We present examples from current common practices of conducting machine learning research (e.g. avoidance of reporting negative results) and failure of generalization ability of the proposed algorithms and datasets in actual real-life usage. Furthermore, a potential future trajectory of machine learning research and development from the perspective of accountable, unbiased, ethical and privacy-aware algorithmic decision making is discussed. We would like to emphasize that with this discussion we neither claim to provide an exhaustive argumentation nor blame any specific institution or individual on the raised issues. This is simply a discussion put forth by us, insiders of the machine learning field, reflecting on us.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework that combines reinforcement learning, evolutionary strategies, and random search to enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of neural architecture search (NAS). By integrating sequential model-based optimization with regularized evolution, we propose a method that systematically explores architectural spaces while maintaining computational efficiency. Our approach leverages transferable building blocks and incorporates early-stopping and weight-sharing mechanisms to improve search performance and reproducibility. Experimental results on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art accuracy while reducing computational costs compared to existing NAS techniques. Furthermore, we address the generalization concerns of current models by evaluating performance on newly created test sets, showing improved robustness to distribution shifts. This work provides a comprehensive evaluation of the search phase, emphasizing the importance of search strategy quality in discovering superior architectures.
