By combining the Two-Pathway Generative Adversarial Network (TP-GAN) with 3D Morphable Model (3DMM)-conditioned GANs and disentangled representation learning, our approach simultaneously captures global structures and local details while preserving identity and enabling attribute manipulation. The framework leverages a combination of adversarial, symmetry, identity preserving, and masked symmetry losses to ensure high-fidelity photorealistic synthesis. Additionally, it incorporates attribute-guided conditional CycleGAN and residual image learning strategies to allow flexible control over facial attributes such as pose, expression, and illumination. The proposed method supports open-set identity synthesis, enabling the generation of faces for subjects not present in the training data, and demonstrates superior performance in face frontalization, attribute morphing, and identity transfer across diverse and unconstrained datasets.

original_abstract: Although distributed computing can significantly reduce the training time of deep neural networks, scaling the training process while maintaining high efficiency and final accuracy is challenging. Distributed asynchronous training enjoys near-linear speedup, but asynchrony causes gradient staleness, the main difficulty in scaling stochastic gradient descent to large clusters. Momentum, which is often used to accelerate convergence and escape local minima, exacerbates the gradient staleness, thereby hindering convergence. We propose DANA: a novel asynchronous distributed technique which is based on a new gradient staleness measure that we call the gap. By minimizing the gap, DANA mitigates the gradient staleness, despite using momentum, and therefore scales to large clusters while maintaining high final accuracy and fast convergence. DANA adapts Nesterov's Accelerated Gradient to a distributed setting, computing the gradient on an estimated future position of the model's parameters. In turn, we show that DANA's estimation of the future position amplifies the use of a Taylor expansion, which relies on a fast Hessian approximation, making it much more effective and accurate. Our evaluation on the CIFAR and ImageNet datasets shows that DANA outperforms existing methods, in both final accuracy and convergence speed.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel distributed deep learning framework that combines elastic averaging SGD (EASGD), staleness-aware learning rate modulation, ternary gradient compression, and adaptive communication strategies to achieve efficient and accurate training of large-scale neural networks. By integrating EASGD's communication-efficient exploration with staleness-aware adjustments to the learning rate, the framework mitigates the instability and convergence issues inherent in asynchronous training. Ternary gradient compression further reduces communication overhead without significant accuracy loss, while adaptive communication strategies dynamically balance the trade-off between error and runtime. Experimental results on CIFAR, ImageNet, and WikiText-103 demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing approaches in terms of convergence speed, accuracy, and communication efficiency, making it a promising solution for large-scale distributed deep learning.

original_abstract: This paper provides, to the best of our knowledge, the first comprehensive and exhaustive study of adversarial attacks on human pose estimation. Besides highlighting the important differences between well-studied classification and human pose-estimation systems w.r.t. adversarial attacks, we also provide deep insights into the design choices of pose-estimation systems to shape future work. We compare the robustness of several pose-estimation architectures trained on the standard datasets, MPII and COCO. In doing so, we also explore the problem of attacking non-classification based networks including regression based networks, which has been virtually unexplored in the past. #R##N#We find that compared to classification and semantic segmentation, human pose estimation architectures are relatively robust to adversarial attacks with the single-step attacks being surprisingly ineffective. Our study show that the heatmap-based pose-estimation models fare better than their direct regression-based counterparts and that the systems which explicitly model anthropomorphic semantics of human body are significantly more robust. We find that the targeted attacks are more difficult to obtain than untargeted ones and some body-joints are easier to fool than the others. We present visualizations of universal perturbations to facilitate unprecedented insights into their workings on pose-estimation. Additionally, we show them to generalize well across different networks on both the datasets.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework that combines adversarial training, generative adversarial perturbations, and transferable attack methods to enhance the robustness of deep neural networks against adversarial examples in complex tasks such as semantic segmentation and object detection. Our method addresses the label leaking effect and improves transferability across different architectures and tasks, as demonstrated on ImageNet and Cityscapes. Furthermore, we show that adversarial examples generated using our approach are effective in black-box settings and can be used to evaluate and improve the robustness of semantic segmentation and optical flow networks. Experimental results confirm that our framework significantly enhances model robustness while maintaining performance on clean inputs.

original_abstract: Native speakers can judge whether a sentence is an acceptable instance of their language. Acceptability provides a means of evaluating whether computational language models are processing language in a human-like manner. We test the ability of computational language models, simple language features, and word embeddings to predict native English speakers judgments of acceptability on English-language essays written by non-native speakers. We find that much of the sentence acceptability variance can be captured by a combination of features including misspellings, word order, and word similarity (Pearson's r = 0.494). While predictive neural models fit acceptability judgments well (r = 0.527), we find that a 4-gram model with statistical smoothing is just as good (r = 0.528). Thanks to incorporating a count of misspellings, our 4-gram model surpasses both the previous unsupervised state-of-the art (Lau et al., 2015; r = 0.472), and the average non-expert native speaker (r = 0.46). Our results demonstrate that acceptability is well captured by n-gram statistics and simple language features.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework that integrates distributed word and phrase representations with unsupervised grammaticality prediction to enhance the modeling of syntactic and semantic structures in natural language. These representations are then combined with statistical language modeling and grammaticality quantification approaches to predict sentence acceptability and grammaticality on an ordinal scale. By leveraging the efficiency of modern word representation models and the constraint-based formalisms for grammaticality evaluation, our system demonstrates strong performance in capturing both syntactic regularities and acceptability judgments across diverse linguistic phenomena. The proposed approach offers a scalable and portable solution for improving language understanding tasks, with potential applications in natural language processing, language acquisition, and automated evaluation systems.

original_abstract: In this work we introduce a new self-supervised, semi-parametric approach for synthesizing novel views of a vehicle starting from a single monocular image. Differently from parametric (i.e. entirely learning-based) methods, we show how a-priori geometric knowledge about the object and the 3D world can be successfully integrated into a deep learning based image generation framework. As this geometric component is not learnt, we call our approach semi-parametric. #R##N#In particular, we exploit man-made object symmetry and piece-wise planarity to integrate rich a-priori visual information into the novel viewpoint synthesis process. An Image Completion Network (ICN) is then trained to generate a realistic image starting from this geometric guidance. #R##N#This careful blend between parametric and non-parametric components allows us to i) operate in a real-world scenario, ii) preserve high-frequency visual information such as textures, iii) handle truly arbitrary 3D roto-translations of the input and iv) perform shape transfer to completely different 3D models. Eventually, we show that our approach can be easily complemented with synthetic data and extended to other rigid objects with completely different topology, even in presence of concave structures and holes (e.g. chairs). #R##N#A comprehensive experimental analysis against state-of-the-art competitors shows the efficacy of our method both from a quantitative and a perceptive point of view. #R##N#Supplementary material, animated results, code and data are available at: this https URL
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a unified framework for novel view synthesis and image-to-image translation that combines the strengths of conditional adversarial networks, cascaded refinement networks, and 3D-aware generative models. By integrating appearance flow estimation, disentangled 3D representations, and shape-guided image generation, our approach enables high-quality synthesis of photorealistic images from semantic layouts, single-view inputs, and arbitrary viewpoints. The method leverages both 2D-to-3D alignment and multi-view consistency to address disocclusion and maintain fine-grained details, while also supporting efficient image completion and pose-based generation. Experimental results on a variety of object and scene categories demonstrate that our framework outperforms existing methods in perceptual quality, geometric accuracy, and generalization across different tasks.

original_abstract: Power systems are growing rapidly, due to the ever-increasing demand for electrical power. These systems require novel methodologies and modern tools and technologies, to better perform, particularly for communication among different parts. Therefore, power systems are facing new challenges such as energy trading and marketing and cyber threats. Using blockchain in power systems, as a solution, is one of the newest methods. Most studies aim to investigate innovative approach-es of blockchain application in power systems. Even though, many articles published to support the research activities, there has not been any bibliometric analysis which specifies the research trends. This paper aims to present a bibliographic analysis of the blockchain application in power systems related literature, in the Web of Science (WoS) database between January 2009 and July 2019. This paper discusses the research activities and performed a detailed analysis by looking at the number of articles published, citations, institutions, research areas, and authors. From the analysis, it was concluded that there are several significant impacts of research activities in China and the USA, in comparison to other countries.
generated_abstract: This paper presents a novel integrated framework that combines blockchain technology, advanced machine learning techniques, and robust dynamic state estimation to enhance the security, privacy, and reliability of modern smart grids. Drawing on the potential of blockchain for decentralized and secure energy trading, data integrity, and privacy preservation, the framework incorporates hash-based transaction generation, multi-signature authentication, and anonymous messaging streams to ensure secure direct load control and decentralized energy trading. To address the growing threat of cyber-attacks, particularly false data injection (FDI) attacks, the framework integrates supervised and unsupervised machine learning methods with heuristic feature selection and statistical correlation-based anomaly detection to improve the accuracy of attack detection. Additionally, a robust dynamic state estimation algorithm based on Markov chain theory and parallel processing techniques is employed to enhance the resilience of the power system against coordinated cyber-attacks. The proposed framework is evaluated using IEEE standard bus systems and simulation results demonstrate its effectiveness in improving grid security, reducing computational overhead, and ensuring reliable operation under various attack scenarios. This work contributes to the modernization of power systems by leveraging blockchain and machine learning for a more secure, efficient, and resilient smart grid ecosystem.

original_abstract: Deep learning based methods have achieved surprising progress in Scene Text Recognition (STR), one of classic problems in computer vision. In this paper, we propose a feasible framework for multi-lingual arbitrary-shaped STR, including instance segmentation based text detection and language model based attention mechanism for text recognition. Our STR algorithm not only recognizes Latin and Non-Latin characters, but also supports arbitrary-shaped text recognition. Our method wins the championship on Scene Text Spotting Task (Latin Only, Latin and Chinese) of ICDAR2019 Robust Reading Challenge on ArbitraryShaped Text Competition. Code is available at this https URL.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel single-shot object detection framework that integrates the efficiency of SSD with the multi-scale feature fusion capabilities of FPN and the architectural optimizations of EfficientDet. By combining a weighted bi-directional feature pyramid network with a single-stage detection head, our approach achieves state-of-the-art accuracy and efficiency across multiple object detection benchmarks. The proposed method eliminates the need for region proposal networks while maintaining high detection performance, and it is further optimized using compound scaling to balance model size and computational cost. Experimental results on PASCAL VOC, COCO, and ILSVRC demonstrate that our framework outperforms existing single-stage and two-stage detectors in both speed and accuracy, achieving a mAP of 53.5 on COCO with 48M parameters and 280B FLOPs, while maintaining a frame rate of 65 FPS on a GPU.

original_abstract: Question answering (QA) in natural language (NL) has been an important aspect of AI from its early days. Winograd's ``councilmen'' example in his 1972 paper and McCarthy's Mr. Hug example of 1976 highlights the role of external knowledge in NL understanding. While Machine Learning has been the go-to approach in NL processing as well as NL question answering (NLQA) for the last 30 years, recently there has been an increasingly emphasized thread on NLQA where external knowledge plays an important role. The challenges inspired by Winograd's councilmen example, and recent developments such as the Rebooting AI book, various NLQA datasets, research on knowledge acquisition in the NLQA context, and their use in various NLQA models have brought the issue of NLQA using ``reasoning'' with external knowledge to the forefront. In this paper, we present a survey of the recent work on them. We believe our survey will help establish a bridge between multiple fields of AI, especially between (a) the traditional fields of knowledge representation and reasoning and (b) the field of NL understanding and NLQA.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for multi-hop reading comprehension that integrates cross-document reasoning, coreference resolution, and commonsense knowledge. Building on existing datasets such as HotpotQA, Quoref, and Cosmos QA, we propose a unified task that requires models to retrieve, combine, and reason over information from multiple documents, resolve coreferential links, and apply contextual commonsense reasoning. We present a new dataset constructed using a multi-step methodology that ensures questions require multi-hop inference across thematically linked documents, while also incorporating coreference and commonsense challenges. Our experiments show that state-of-the-art models struggle with this combined task, achieving only 58.2% accuracy compared to human performance of 89.5%. We further explore methods to incorporate external knowledge and propose a novel architecture that improves performance by 14.3% over baseline models, highlighting the potential for future research in multi-modal and multi-step reasoning systems.

original_abstract: In recent years, much research effort on recommendation has been devoted to mining user behaviors, i.e., collaborative filtering, along with the general information which describes users or items, e.g., textual attributes, categorical demographics, product images, and so on. Price, an important factor in marketing --- which determines whether a user will make the final purchase decision on an item --- surprisingly, has received relatively little scrutiny. #R##N#In this work, we aim at developing an effective method to predict user purchase intention with the focus on the price factor in recommender systems. The main difficulties are two-fold: 1) the preference and sensitivity of a user on item price are unknown, which are only implicitly reflected in the items that the user has purchased, and 2) how the item price affects a user's intention depends largely on the product category, that is, the perception and affordability of a user on item price could vary significantly across categories. Towards the first difficulty, we propose to model the transitive relationship between user-to-item and item-to-price, taking the inspiration from the recently developed Graph Convolution Networks (GCN). The key idea is to propagate the influence of price on users with items as the bridge, so as to make the learned user representations be price-aware. For the second difficulty, we further integrate item categories into the propagation progress and model the possible pairwise interactions for predicting user-item interactions. We conduct extensive experiments on two real-world datasets, demonstrating the effectiveness of our GCN-based method in learning the price-aware preference of users. Further analysis reveals that modeling the price awareness is particularly useful for predicting user preference on items of unexplored categories.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel recommendation framework that integrates the strengths of Neural Factorization Machines (NFM), xDeepFM, and Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) to address the challenges of sparse and high-dimensional data in web-scale recommender systems. By combining explicit and implicit feature interaction modeling through a Compressed Interaction Network (CIN) with the non-linear modeling capabilities of deep neural networks, the proposed model effectively captures both low- and high-order feature interactions. Additionally, incorporating graph-based collaborative signals via GCNs enhances user and item representations by leveraging the underlying user-item interaction graph structure. The framework also integrates review-based information to further enrich user and item embeddings, improving the quality of recommendations. Experimental results on multiple real-world datasets demonstrate that the proposed model outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving significant improvements in recommendation accuracy and scalability.

original_abstract: Clustering artworks is difficult because of several reasons. On one hand, recognizing meaningful patterns in accordance with domain knowledge and visual perception is extremely hard. On the other hand, the application of traditional clustering and feature reduction techniques to the highly dimensional pixel space can be ineffective. To address these issues, we propose a deep convolutional embedding model for clustering digital paintings, in which the task of mapping the input raw data to an abstract, latent space is optimized jointly with the task of finding a set of cluster centroids in this latent feature space. Quantitative and qualitative experimental results show the effectiveness of the proposed method. The model is also able to outperform other state-of-the-art deep clustering approaches to the same problem. The proposed method may be beneficial to several art-related tasks, particularly visual link retrieval and historical knowledge discovery in painting datasets.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for automated analysis and discovery in artistic domains by integrating multi-task learning, context-aware embeddings, and spatially consistent feature learning. Building on large-scale artistic datasets such as OmniArt and the Behance Artistic Media dataset, we propose a unified approach that enhances visual representations with contextual artistic information, including author, school, and historical period, through both multi-task learning models and art-specific knowledge graphs. Our method also incorporates spatially consistent feature learning to improve the detection of near-duplicate patterns in art collections, addressing challenges posed by varying artistic media and copying imperfections. Additionally, we explore adaptive cross-layer correlation for style recognition and apply visual link retrieval techniques to uncover artistic influences and connections between artists. The framework is evaluated on multiple tasks, including author identification, style classification, and cross-modal retrieval, demonstrating significant improvements in performance, with up to 37.24% enhancement in retrieval accuracy. This work provides a comprehensive solution for analyzing and understanding artistic data, enabling new possibilities for cultural heritage research and digital art curation.

original_abstract: Data selection methods such as active learning and core-set selection are useful tools for machine learning on large datasets, but they can be prohibitively expensive to apply in deep learning. Unlike in other areas of machine learning, the feature representations that these techniques depend on are learned in deep learning rather than given, which takes a substantial amount of training time. In this work, we show that we can significantly improve the computational efficiency of data selection in deep learning by using a much smaller proxy model to perform data selection for tasks that will eventually require a large target model (e.g., selecting data points to label for active learning). In deep learning, we can scale down models by removing hidden layers or reducing their dimension to create proxies that are an order of magnitude faster. Although these small proxy models have significantly higher error, we find that they empirically provide useful rankings for data selection that have a high correlation with those of larger models. We evaluate this "selection via proxy" (SVP) approach on several data selection tasks. For active learning, applying SVP to Sener and Savarese [2018]'s recent method for active learning in deep learning gives a 4x improvement in execution time while yielding the same model accuracy. For core-set selection, we show that a proxy model that trains 10x faster than a target ResNet164 model on CIFAR10 can be used to remove 50% of the training data without compromising the accuracy of the target model, making end-to-end training time improvements via core-set selection possible.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel deep neural network architecture that combines the strengths of residual learning, dense connectivity, and stochastic depth to achieve state-of-the-art performance on multiple benchmark datasets. Building on the success of deep residual networks, wide residual networks, and densely connected networks, we propose a hybrid architecture that enhances feature reuse, alleviates vanishing gradients, and improves training efficiency. By integrating stochastic depth during training, we enable the network to scale to unprecedented depths while maintaining computational efficiency. Our approach demonstrates significant improvements in accuracy and efficiency on ImageNet, CIFAR, and COCO datasets, outperforming existing methods. The proposed architecture is modular, scalable, and provides a new direction for designing deep learning models with enhanced performance and training dynamics.

original_abstract: We introduce a framework for studying how distributional assumptions on the process by which data is partitioned into a training and test set can be leveraged to provide accurate estimation or learning algorithms, even for worst-case datasets. We consider a setting of $n$ datapoints, $x_1,\ldots,x_n$, together with a specified distribution, $P$, over partitions of these datapoints into a training set, test set, and irrelevant set. An algorithm takes as input a description of $P$ (or sample access), the indices of the test and training sets, and the datapoints in the training set, and returns a model or estimate that will be evaluated on the datapoints in the test set. We evaluate an algorithm in terms of its worst-case expected performance: the expected performance over potential test/training sets, for worst-case datapoints, $x_1,\ldots,x_n.$ This framework is a departure from more typical distributional assumptions on the datapoints (e.g. that data is drawn independently, or according to an exchangeable process), and can model a number of natural data collection processes, including processes with dependencies such as "snowball sampling" and "chain sampling", and settings where test and training sets satisfy chronological constraints (e.g. the test instances were observed after the training instances). #R##N#Within this framework, we consider the setting where datapoints are bounded real numbers, and the goal is to estimate the mean of the test set. We give an efficient algorithm that returns a weighted combination of the training set---whose weights depend on the distribution, $P$, and on the training and test set indices---and show that the worst-case expected error achieved by this algorithm is at most a multiplicative $\pi/2$ factor worse than the optimal of such algorithms. The algorithm, and its proof, leverage a surprising connection to the Grothendieck problem.
generated_abstract: We present a novel algorithmic framework for robust high-dimensional statistical learning in the presence of adversarial corruptions, combining recent advances in outlier-robust regression, list-decodable learning, and agnostic distribution learning. Our approach enables efficient estimation of mean and covariance matrices, robust regression, and learning of fundamental distribution classes such as Gaussians and product distributions, even when a significant fraction of the data is arbitrarily corrupted. By leveraging the sum-of-squares method and certifiably hypercontractive or anti-concentrated data distributions, we achieve dimension-independent error guarantees and provide computationally efficient solutions to problems previously thought to be intractable. Our results unify and extend prior work on robust learning, offering practical algorithms for a wide range of applications in machine learning and statistics.

original_abstract: We are witnessing a confluence of vision, speech and dialog system technologies that are enabling the IVAs to learn audio-visual groundings of utterances and have conversations with users about the objects, activities and events surrounding them. Recent progress in visual grounding techniques and Audio Understanding are enabling machines to understand shared semantic concepts and listen to the various sensory events in the environment. With audio and visual grounding methods, end-to-end multimodal SDS are trained to meaningfully communicate with us in natural language about the real dynamic audio-visual sensory world around us. In this work, we explore the role of `topics' as the context of the conversation along with multimodal attention into such an end-to-end audio-visual scene-aware dialog system architecture. We also incorporate an end-to-end audio classification ConvNet, AclNet, into our models. We develop and test our approaches on the Audio Visual Scene-Aware Dialog (AVSD) dataset released as a part of the DSTC7. We present the analysis of our experiments and show that some of our model variations outperform the baseline system released for AVSD.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel end-to-end dialogue system that integrates multimodal attention mechanisms, hierarchical recurrent neural networks, and pretrained word embeddings to generate contextually rich and coherent responses in audio-visual scene-aware dialogues. Building on recent advances in video captioning, visual question answering, and dialogue systems, our approach employs a hierarchical framework that combines temporal and spatial attention for visual analysis, along with modality-specific attention to effectively fuse audio, visual, and textual information. We leverage the AVSD dataset, which contains dialogues about videos of human activities, to train and evaluate our model. Our experiments demonstrate that incorporating multimodal attention and pretrained GloVe embeddings significantly improves the quality of generated responses, achieving state-of-the-art performance in scene-aware dialogue tasks. This work bridges the gap between visual understanding and natural language generation, enabling more realistic and context-aware conversational agents.

original_abstract: The lack of annotated data in many languages is a well-known challenge within the field of multilingual natural language processing (NLP). Therefore, many recent studies focus on zero-shot transfer learning and joint training across languages to overcome data scarcity for low-resource languages. In this work we (i) perform a comprehensive comparison of state-ofthe-art multilingual word and sentence encoders on the tasks of named entity recognition (NER) and part of speech (POS) tagging; and (ii) propose a new method for creating multilingual contextualized word embeddings, compare it to multiple baselines and show that it performs at or above state-of-theart level in zero-shot transfer settings. Finally, we show that our method allows for better knowledge sharing across languages in a joint training setting.
generated_abstract: This paper presents a novel framework for cross-lingual natural language processing that integrates advances in unsupervised machine translation, multilingual sentence embeddings, and cross-lingual alignment of contextual representations. By combining monolingual corpora-based translation models with robust self-learning techniques for cross-lingual word embeddings, our approach enables zero-shot translation and transfer learning across multiple languages without reliance on parallel data. Furthermore, we leverage contextual embeddings and self-attention mechanisms to improve robustness to syntactic and lexical differences, achieving state-of-the-art results in cross-lingual named entity recognition and dependency parsing. Our method also incorporates multilingual sentence representations trained on a large-scale parallel corpus, allowing for effective cross-lingual classification and document understanding. Experimental results demonstrate significant improvements in translation quality, cross-lingual transfer performance, and zero-shot learning capabilities across diverse language pairs and tasks.

original_abstract: Abstract   We present a new method for improving the performances of variational autoencoder (VAE). In addition to enforcing the deep feature consistent principle thus ensuring the VAE output and its corresponding input images to have similar deep features, we also implement a generative adversarial training mechanism to force the VAE to output realistic and natural images. We present experimental results to show that the VAE trained with our new method outperforms state of the art in generating face images with much clearer and more natural noses, eyes, teeth, hair textures as well as reasonable backgrounds. We also show that our method can learn powerful embeddings of input face images, which can be used to achieve facial attribute manipulation. Moreover we propose a multi-view feature extraction strategy to extract effective image representations, which can be used to achieve state of the art performance in facial attribute prediction.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for generating high-quality artistic images by combining deep neural networks with unsupervised representation learning and recurrent adversarial training. Building on the neural algorithm for artistic style, we integrate deep feature consistency from variational autoencoders with the disentangled representations learned by InfoGAN to separate and recombine content and style in a more interpretable manner. Our approach leverages the hierarchical feature learning of deep convolutional generative adversarial networks (DCGANs) and incorporates a recurrent adversarial network structure to iteratively refine image generation. By using learned similarity metrics and perceptual losses, we enhance visual fidelity and enable manipulation of high-level visual features such as pose, lighting, and expressions. The proposed method achieves state-of-the-art results in generating visually realistic and semantically meaningful images, offering new possibilities for both artistic creation and perceptual understanding in computer vision.

original_abstract: Recent efforts show that neural networks are vulnerable to small but intentional perturbations on input features in visual classification tasks. Due to the additional consideration of connections between examples (\eg articles with citation link tend to be in the same class), graph neural networks could be more sensitive to the perturbations, since the perturbations from connected examples exacerbate the impact on a target example. Adversarial Training (AT), a dynamic regularization technique, can resist the worst-case perturbations on input features and is a promising choice to improve model robustness and generalization. However, existing AT methods focus on standard classification, being less effective when training models on graph since it does not model the impact from connected examples.  In this work, we explore adversarial training on graph, aiming to improve the robustness and generalization of models learned on graph. We propose Graph Adversarial Training (GraphAT), which takes the impact from connected examples into account when learning to construct and resist perturbations. We give a general formulation of GraphAT, which can be seen as a dynamic regularization scheme based on the graph structure. To demonstrate the utility of GraphAT, we employ it on a state-of-the-art graph neural network model --- Graph Convolutional Network (GCN). We conduct experiments on two citation graphs (Citeseer and Cora) and a knowledge graph (NELL), verifying the effectiveness of GraphAT which outperforms normal training on GCN by 4.51% in node classification accuracy. Codes are available via: https://github.com/fulifeng/GraphAT.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel semi-supervised learning framework that integrates graph convolutional networks (GCNs), adversarial training, and robustness mechanisms to enhance graph representation learning. Building on recent advances in spectral graph convolutions, adversarial network embedding, and adversarial attacks on graph-structured data, our approach combines the strengths of GCNs in capturing local graph structure with adversarial learning to improve robustness and generalization. We propose a hybrid model that employs a generator to produce synthetic samples in low-density regions of the graph, while an adversarial discriminator ensures the generated representations align with the underlying data distribution. Additionally, we incorporate a variance-based attention mechanism to mitigate the impact of adversarial perturbations during message passing. Experimental results on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that our method significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art approaches in terms of node classification accuracy and robustness against adversarial attacks, while maintaining scalability and inductive capabilities for unseen nodes.

original_abstract: The use of machine learning or artificial intelligence (ML/AI) holds substantial potential toward improving many functions and needs of the public sector. In practice however, integrating ML/AI components into public sector applications is severely limited not only by the fragility of these components and their algorithms, but also because of mismatches between components of ML-enabled systems. For example, if an ML model is trained on data that is different from data in the operational environment, field performance of the ML component will be dramatically reduced. Separate from software engineering considerations, the expertise needed to field an ML/AI component within a system frequently comes from outside software engineering. As a result, assumptions and even descriptive language used by practitioners from these different disciplines can exacerbate other challenges to integrating ML/AI components into larger systems. We are investigating classes of mismatches in ML/AI systems integration, to identify the implicit assumptions made by practitioners in different fields (data scientists, software engineers, operations staff) and find ways to communicate the appropriate information explicitly. We will discuss a few categories of mismatch, and provide examples from each class. To enable ML/AI components to be fielded in a meaningful way, we will need to understand the mismatches that exist and develop practices to mitigate the impacts of these mismatches.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for enhancing transparency, accountability, and trust in AI systems by integrating and extending existing practices such as datasheets for datasets, model cards, supplier's declarations of conformity, and software engineering best practices for AI development. Drawing on empirical studies of GitHub data and lessons learned from AI integration in software engineering, we propose a unified documentation standard that combines dataset metadata, model performance across diverse groups, ethical and safety considerations, and software engineering practices for AI systems. This framework aims to support responsible AI development by providing a comprehensive, standardized approach to documenting AI systems throughout their lifecycle, from data collection to deployment, while addressing the unique challenges of AI integration in software engineering.

original_abstract: Very deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have been firmly established as the primary methods for many computer vision tasks. However, most state-of-the-art CNNs are large, which results in high inference latency. Recently, depth-wise separable convolution has been proposed for image recognition tasks on computationally limited platforms such as robotics and self-driving cars. Though it is much faster than its counterpart, regular convolution, accuracy is sacrificed. In this paper, we propose a novel decomposition approach based on SVD, namely depth-wise decomposition, for expanding regular convolutions into depthwise separable convolutions while maintaining high accuracy. We show our approach can be further generalized to the multi-channel and multi-layer cases, based on Generalized Singular Value Decomposition (GSVD) [59]. We conduct thorough experiments with the latest ShuffleNet V2 model [47] on both random synthesized dataset and a large-scale image recognition dataset: ImageNet [10]. Our approach outperforms channel decomposition [73] on all datasets. More importantly, our approach improves the Top-1 accuracy of ShuffleNet V2 by ~2%.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for efficiently deploying deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) on resource-constrained devices by combining structured pruning, filter removal, and low-rank approximations. Building on recent advances in parameter pruning, channel selection, and structured sparsity, our method systematically reduces computational and memory demands while maintaining high accuracy. We employ a multi-granularity pruning strategy that includes feature map-wise, kernel-wise, and intra-kernel strided sparsity, enabling efficient implementation on embedded systems and parallel computing platforms. Additionally, we incorporate filter pruning techniques that remove entire filters and their associated feature maps, significantly reducing computation without requiring sparse convolution libraries. To further optimize performance, we apply low-rank expansions and exploit linear redundancies within convolutional layers. Experimental results on benchmark datasets such as CIFAR-10, ImageNet, and others demonstrate that our approach achieves up to 70% parameter reduction, 4x speedup, and less than 1% accuracy loss across multiple architectures including VGG-16, ResNet, and MobileNet. This integrated method provides a comprehensive solution for accelerating CNNs while preserving their accuracy and compatibility with existing hardware and software infrastructures.

original_abstract: We propose a differentiable sphere tracing algorithm to bridge the gap between inverse graphics methods and the recently proposed deep learning based implicit signed distance function. Due to the nature of the implicit function, the rendering process requires tremendous function queries, which is particularly problematic when the function is represented as a neural network. We optimize both the forward and backward pass of our rendering layer to make it run efficiently with affordable memory consumption on a commodity graphics card. Our rendering method is fully differentiable such that losses can be directly computed on the rendered 2D observations, and the gradients can be propagated backward to optimize the 3D geometry. We show that our rendering method can effectively reconstruct accurate 3D shapes from various inputs, such as sparse depth and multi-view images, through inverse optimization. With the geometry based reasoning, our 3D shape prediction methods show excellent generalization capability and robustness against various noise.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for high-fidelity 3D mesh reconstruction from single RGB images by combining the strengths of implicit surface representations, differentiable rendering, and graph-based deformation networks. Building on recent advances in occupancy networks, level set methods, and pixel-to-mesh approaches, our method employs an end-to-end trainable architecture that implicitly represents 3D surfaces as continuous decision boundaries while leveraging perceptual features for accurate geometry estimation. A differentiable renderer is integrated to enable image-based supervision without requiring explicit 3D ground truth, and a graph convolutional network is used to iteratively refine the mesh through cross-view deformation. Additionally, a hierarchical strategy is adopted to enhance resolution around predicted surfaces while maintaining computational efficiency. Our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance in both single-view and multi-view 3D reconstruction tasks, producing visually plausible and physically accurate mesh models that generalize across object categories and input conditions.

original_abstract: Scene graph prediction --- classifying the set of objects and predicates in a visual scene --- requires substantial training data. However, most predicates only occur a handful of times making them difficult to learn. We introduce the first scene graph prediction model that supports few-shot learning of predicates. Existing scene graph generation models represent objects using pretrained object detectors or word embeddings that capture semantic object information at the cost of encoding information about which relationships they afford. So, these object representations are unable to generalize to new few-shot relationships. We introduce a framework that induces object representations that are structured according to their visual relationships. Unlike past methods, our framework embeds objects that afford similar relationships closer together. This property allows our model to perform well in the few-shot setting. For example, applying the 'riding' predicate transformation to 'person' modifies the representation towards objects like 'skateboard' and 'horse' that enable riding. We generate object representations by learning predicates trained as message passing functions within a new graph convolution framework. The object representations are used to build few-shot predicate classifiers for rare predicates with as few as 1 labeled example. We achieve a 5-shot performance of 22.70 recall@50, a 3.7 increase when compared to strong transfer learning baselines.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for scene graph generation that integrates multi-level semantic understanding, global context modeling, and efficient subgraph-based inference. Building on associative embedding, iterative message passing, and motif-based architectures, our approach combines object detection, relationship prediction, and region captioning into a unified end-to-end model. By leveraging dynamic graph alignment, spatial-weighted message passing, and external knowledge refinement, we achieve robust and efficient scene graph generation. Our method outperforms existing state-of-the-art approaches on the Visual Genome and Visual Relationship Detection datasets, demonstrating significant improvements in both accuracy and inference speed.

original_abstract: This paper proposes a new defense called $n$-ML against adversarial examples, i.e., inputs crafted by perturbing benign inputs by small amounts to induce misclassifications by classifiers. Inspired by $n$-version programming, $n$-ML trains an ensemble of $n$ classifiers, and inputs are classified by a vote of the classifiers in the ensemble. Unlike prior such approaches, however, the classifiers in the ensemble are trained specifically to classify adversarial examples differently, rendering it very difficult for an adversarial example to obtain enough votes to be misclassified. We show that $n$-ML roughly retains the benign classification accuracies of state-of-the-art models on the MNIST, CIFAR10, and GTSRB datasets, while simultaneously defending against adversarial examples with better resilience than the best defenses known to date and, in most cases, with lower classification-time overhead.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework that combines input transformation, adversarial training, and ensemble diversity to enhance the robustness of deep neural networks against adversarial examples. Building on recent advances in adversarial defense, we integrate non-differentiable input transformations such as total variance minimization and image quilting with adversarial training techniques that leverage fast single-step attacks and ensemble-based methods. Additionally, we incorporate diversity training to ensure that models in the ensemble have uncorrelated loss gradients, reducing the likelihood of successful transfer-based attacks. Our approach demonstrates significant improvements in defending against both white-box and black-box adversarial attacks, as validated on benchmark datasets such as MNIST, CIFAR-10, and ImageNet. Experimental results show that our framework achieves high robustness while maintaining strong classification accuracy, offering a practical and effective solution for securing deep learning models in real-world applications.

original_abstract: Learning predictive models from interaction with the world allows an agent, such as a robot, to learn about how the world works, and then use this learned model to plan coordinated sequences of actions to bring about desired outcomes. However, learning a model that captures the dynamics of complex skills represents a major challenge: if the agent needs a good model to perform these skills, it might never be able to collect the experience on its own that is required to learn these delicate and complex behaviors. Instead, we can imagine augmenting the training set with observational data of other agents, such as humans. Such data is likely more plentiful, but represents a different embodiment. For example, videos of humans might show a robot how to use a tool, but (i) are not annotated with suitable robot actions, and (ii) contain a systematic distributional shift due to the embodiment differences between humans and robots. We address the first challenge by formulating the corresponding graphical model and treating the action as an observed variable for the interaction data and an unobserved variable for the observation data, and the second challenge by using a domain-dependent prior. In addition to interaction data, our method is able to leverage videos of passive observations in a driving dataset and a dataset of robotic manipulation videos. A robotic planning agent equipped with our method can learn to use tools in a tabletop robotic manipulation setting by observing humans without ever seeing a robotic video of tool use.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for unsupervised video prediction and physical interaction learning by combining action-conditioned video prediction, probabilistic motion modeling, and hierarchical structure encoding. Drawing from recent advances in predictive coding, adversarial training, and variational autoencoders, our model learns to generate diverse and physically plausible future frames while capturing both high-level scene dynamics and low-level pixel motion. By integrating a dual motion GAN architecture with a stochastic variational prior, the model explicitly enforces consistency between predicted frames and optical flows, enabling robust prediction of long-term video sequences. Additionally, the framework incorporates a disentangled representation learning mechanism that separates static and dynamic components of video content, facilitating generalization to novel objects and environments. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach on a variety of synthetic and real-world video datasets, as well as in robotic manipulation tasks, where the model enables accurate visual foresight and action planning without requiring labeled data or prior knowledge of object identities.

original_abstract: We propose a new approach to video face recognition. Our component-wise feature aggregation network (C-FAN) accepts a set of face images of a subject as an input, and outputs a single feature vector as the face representation of the set for the recognition task. The whole network is trained in two steps: (i) train a base CNN for still image face recognition; (ii) add an aggregation module to the base network to learn the quality value for each feature component, which adaptively aggregates deep feature vectors into a single vector to represent the face in a video. C-FAN automatically learns to retain salient face features with high quality scores while suppressing features with low quality scores. The experimental results on three benchmark datasets, YouTube Faces, IJB-A, and IJB-S show that the proposed C-FAN network is capable of generating a compact feature vector with 512 dimensions for a video sequence by efficiently aggregating feature vectors of all the video frames to achieve state of the art performance.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for video-based face recognition that integrates deep embedding learning, neural aggregation, and robust feature extraction techniques. By combining a multi-patch deep CNN with deep metric learning, we achieve highly discriminative low-dimensional features for face verification. A meta-attention-based aggregation network is proposed to effectively exploit discriminative information across video frames, while maintaining robustness to blur, occlusion, and pose variations. The framework also incorporates an L2-constrained softmax loss and additive margin softmax to enhance discriminative power and generalization. Experimental results on challenging datasets such as IJB-A, YouTube Faces, and LFW demonstrate that our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance in both verification and identification tasks, with significant improvements in accuracy and efficiency compared to existing methods.

original_abstract: We investigate the relationship between the frequency spectrum of image data and the generalization behavior of convolutional neural networks (CNN). We first notice CNN's ability in capturing the high-frequency components of images. These high-frequency components are almost imperceptible to a human. Thus the observation leads to multiple hypotheses that are related to the generalization behaviors of CNN, including a potential explanation for adversarial examples, a discussion of CNN's trade-off between robustness and accuracy, and some evidence in understanding training heuristics. Our observation also immediately inspire methods related to the adversarial attack and defense methods.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework that combines adversarial training with gradient interpretability and detection mechanisms to enhance the robustness of deep neural networks (DNNs) against adversarial attacks while maintaining high accuracy. Drawing on recent advances in adversarial robustness, we incorporate spectral normalization and margin loss extensions to improve generalization and reduce the accuracy-robustness trade-off. Additionally, we integrate a detector subnetwork inspired by MagNet to identify adversarial perturbations, complementing adversarial training with an orthogonal defense strategy. Our approach also leverages insights from TRADES to balance robustness and accuracy through a principled trade-off mechanism. Experimental results across multiple datasets and architectures demonstrate that our framework significantly improves adversarial robustness without substantial accuracy degradation, while also enabling more interpretable gradient behavior. The proposed method is evaluated against a variety of attack scenarios, including white-box, gray-box, and black-box attacks, and shows strong generalization capabilities.

original_abstract: We present an adaptive regularization algorithm that can be effectively applied to the optimization problem in deep learning framework. Our regularization algorithm aims to take into account the fitness of data to the current state of model in the determination of regularity to achieve better generalization. The degree of regularization at each element in the target space of the neural network architecture is determined based on the residual at each optimization iteration in an adaptive way. Our adaptive regularization algorithm is designed to apply a diffusion process driven by the heat equation with spatially varying diffusivity depending on the probability density function following a certain distribution of residual. Our data-driven regularity is imposed by adaptively smoothing a simplified objective function in which the explicit regularization term is omitted in an alternating manner between the evaluation of residual and the determination of the degree of its regularity. The effectiveness of our algorithm is empirically demonstrated by the numerical experiments in the application of image classification problems, indicating that our algorithm outperforms other commonly used optimization algorithms in terms of generalization using popular deep learning models and benchmark datasets.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel deep convolutional network architecture that combines the strengths of residual learning, dense connectivity, and advanced regularization techniques to achieve state-of-the-art performance on large-scale image recognition tasks. Building on the residual learning framework, which enables the training of substantially deeper networks, we incorporate dense connections to enhance feature propagation and reuse, reducing the number of parameters while improving accuracy. To address overfitting and improve generalization, we integrate stochastic pooling and Swapout regularization, which provide effective noise injection and implicit parameter tying across layers. Additionally, we leverage batch normalization to accelerate training and stabilize learning dynamics by reducing internal covariate shift. Our proposed model demonstrates significant improvements in accuracy and efficiency on benchmark datasets such as ImageNet, CIFAR-10, and CIFAR-100, achieving results comparable to or exceeding those of much deeper ResNet models with fewer computational resources. The combination of these techniques not only enhances model performance but also provides a deeper understanding of the interplay between network depth, regularization, and training dynamics in deep learning.

original_abstract: Communication is a key bottleneck in distributed training. Recently, an \emph{error-compensated} compression technology was particularly designed for the \emph{centralized} learning and receives huge successes, by showing significant advantages over state-of-the-art compression based methods in saving the communication cost. Since the \emph{decentralized} training has been witnessed to be superior to the traditional \emph{centralized} training in the communication restricted scenario, therefore a natural question to ask is "how to apply the error-compensated technology to the decentralized learning to further reduce the communication cost." However, a trivial extension of compression based centralized training algorithms does not exist for the decentralized scenario. key difference between centralized and decentralized training makes this extension extremely non-trivial. In this paper, we propose an elegant algorithmic design to employ error-compensated stochastic gradient descent for the decentralized scenario, named $\texttt{DeepSqueeze}$. Both the theoretical analysis and the empirical study are provided to show the proposed $\texttt{DeepSqueeze}$ algorithm outperforms the existing compression based decentralized learning algorithms. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first time to apply the error-compensated compression to the decentralized learning.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces Compressed Gradient Aggregation with Adaptive Sparsification (CGAS), a novel framework that combines ternary gradient quantization, gradient sparsification, and error-compensated communication to achieve efficient and scalable distributed deep learning. Building on prior works that demonstrate the effectiveness of ternary gradients, sparsification, and quantization in reducing communication overhead, CGAS introduces an adaptive mechanism to dynamically select the most informative gradient components while compensating for accumulated quantization and sparsification errors. The proposed method ensures convergence guarantees under standard assumptions, with theoretical analysis showing convergence rates comparable to full-precision methods. Experimental results on deep neural networks such as ResNet and GoogLeNet demonstrate that CGAS achieves up to 10x communication reduction with negligible accuracy loss, outperforming existing techniques in both centralized and decentralized settings. The framework is validated across various network topologies and scales effectively with increasing numbers of workers, making it a promising approach for large-scale distributed learning.

original_abstract: Natural question generation (QG) is a challenging yet rewarding task, that aims to generate questions given an input passage and a target answer. Previous works on QG, however, either (i) ignore the rich structure information hidden in the word sequence, (ii) fail to fully exploit the target answer, or (iii) solely rely on cross-entropy loss that leads to issues like exposure bias and evaluation discrepancy between training and testing. To address the above limitations, in this paper, we propose a reinforcement learning (RL) based graph-to-sequence (Graph2Seq) architecture for the QG task. Our model consists of a Graph2Seq generator where a novel bidirectional graph neural network (GNN) based encoder is applied to embed the input passage incorporating the answer information via a simple yet effective Deep Alignment Network, and an evaluator where a mixed objective function combining both cross-entropy loss and RL loss is designed for ensuring the generation of semantically and syntactically valid text. The proposed model is end-to-end trainable, and achieves new state-of-the-art scores and outperforms all previous methods by a great margin on the SQuAD benchmark.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a unified framework for generating high-quality question-answer pairs from text, combining advances in attention-based sequence learning, deep reinforcement learning, and answer-focused modeling. Building on prior work that emphasizes end-to-end training, syntactic awareness, and the integration of answer information, our model incorporates a generator-evaluator architecture that directly optimizes question quality through task-specific rewards. The generator employs a sequence-to-sequence model with copy and coverage mechanisms, enhanced by a clue-guided approach that leverages syntactic dependency trees and multi-task learning to distinguish between copying and generating words. Additionally, the model integrates answer separation and position-aware mechanisms to ensure interrogative words align with answer types and contextually relevant words are selected. Experimental results on the SQuAD benchmark demonstrate significant improvements in both automatic and human evaluations, with generated questions rated as more natural, diverse, and challenging. Our approach advances the automation of reading comprehension assessment and provides a robust foundation for improving question-answering systems through enhanced question generation.

original_abstract: Text summarization aims at compressing long documents into a shorter form that conveys the most important parts of the original document. Despite increased interest in the community and notable research effort, progress on benchmark datasets has stagnated. We critically evaluate key ingredients of the current research setup: datasets, evaluation metrics, and models, and highlight three primary shortcomings: 1) automatically collected datasets leave the task underconstrained and may contain noise detrimental to training and evaluation, 2) current evaluation protocol is weakly correlated with human judgment and does not account for important characteristics such as factual correctness, 3) models overfit to layout biases of current datasets and offer limited diversity in their outputs.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel hybrid model for abstractive document summarization that integrates the strengths of extractive and abstractive approaches, while addressing their individual limitations. Building on attention-based encoder-decoder frameworks, sequence-to-sequence models, and reinforcement learning techniques, our model employs a graph-based attention mechanism to enhance saliency detection and content selection. It incorporates a bottom-up content selector to guide phrase selection, a syntactic compression module for grammatical fluency, and a deep reinforcement learning component to mitigate exposure bias and improve readability. Additionally, a unified inconsistency loss function ensures coherence between sentence-level and word-level attention mechanisms. The model is trained end-to-end on large-scale datasets, achieving state-of-the-art ROUGE scores while producing more informative and human-like summaries. Human evaluations confirm the superiority of our approach in terms of fluency, coherence, and abstraction level compared to existing methods.

original_abstract: Recent research towards understanding neural networks probes models in a top-down manner, but is only able to identify model tendencies that are known a priori. We propose Susceptibility Identification through Fine-Tuning (SIFT), a novel abstractive method that uncovers a model's preferences without imposing any prior. By fine-tuning an autoencoder with the gradients from a fixed classifier, we are able to extract propensities that characterize different kinds of classifiers in a bottom-up manner. We further leverage the SIFT architecture to rephrase sentences in order to predict the opposing class of the ground truth label, uncovering potential artifacts encoded in the fixed classification model. We evaluate our method on three diverse tasks with four different models. We contrast the propensities of the models as well as reproduce artifacts reported in the literature.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework that integrates visualization techniques for neural compositionality, rationalization of predictions, and probing of sentence embeddings to enhance interpretability and performance in natural language understanding tasks. Drawing on methods for visualizing salience and compositionality in neural models, we combine these with approaches for generating rationales that justify predictions, and with probing tasks that assess the linguistic properties encoded in sentence embeddings. Our framework is evaluated on natural language inference and sentiment analysis tasks, demonstrating improved model transparency and performance. By addressing annotation artifacts and leveraging hypothesis-only baselines, we provide insights into the limitations of current datasets and the potential of domain-invariant attention mechanisms. The results highlight the value of combining interpretability techniques with probing methods to better understand and improve the semantic capabilities of deep learning models in NLP.

original_abstract: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have been very successful at solving a variety of computer vision tasks such as object classification and detection, semantic segmentation, activity understanding, to name just a few. One key enabling factor for their great performance has been the ability to train very deep CNNs. Despite their huge success in many tasks, CNNs do not work well with non-Euclidean data which is prevalent in many real-world applications. Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) offer an alternative that allows for non-Eucledian data as input to a neural network similar to CNNs. While GCNs already achieve encouraging results, they are currently limited to shallow architectures with 2-4 layers due to vanishing gradients during training. This work transfers concepts such as residual/dense connections and dilated convolutions from CNNs to GCNs in order to successfully train very deep GCNs. We show the benefit of deep GCNs with as many as 112 layers experimentally across various datasets and tasks. Specifically, we achieve state-of-the-art performance in part segmentation and semantic segmentation on point clouds and in node classification of protein functions across biological protein-protein interaction (PPI) graphs. We believe that the insights in this work will open a lot of avenues for future research on GCNs and transfer to further tasks not explored in this work. The source code for this work is available for Pytorch and Tensorflow at this https URL and this https URL respectively.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel deep learning framework that integrates graph-based and point cloud processing techniques to enable efficient and effective representation learning on complex, non-Euclidean data. Building on graph convolutional networks, dynamic graph CNNs, and parameterized convolutional filters, our approach combines localized spectral convolutions, edge-conditioned filters, and deformable convolutions to capture both structural and geometric properties of data. By incorporating jumping knowledge mechanisms and deep architectures inspired by residual and dilated connections, our model achieves superior performance on a range of tasks, including graph classification, point cloud segmentation, and semi-supervised learning. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our framework outperforms existing methods, offering a unified and scalable solution for learning on graph-structured and point cloud data.

original_abstract: Executable semantic parsing is the task of converting natural language utterances into logical forms that can be directly used as queries to get a response. We build a transfer learning framework for executable semantic parsing. We show that the framework is effective for Question Answering (QA we experiment with public data sets such as Overnight and NLmaps as well as with commercial SLU data. The experiments carried out on data sets that are different in nature show how executable semantic parsing can unify different areas of NLP such as Q&A and SLU.
generated_abstract: This paper presents a novel multi-task sequence-to-sequence framework for semantic parsing that integrates cross-domain adaptation, zero-shot learning, and structured representation induction. By combining multi-task learning strategies with data recombination and paraphrasing-based domain adaptation, the model effectively leverages auxiliary tasks and external knowledge to improve parsing accuracy in both in-domain and unseen domains. The approach introduces a hierarchical semantic representation that captures compositional structures, while also incorporating dependency-based compositional semantics to model logical forms without explicit annotations. Additionally, the model utilizes standardized pre-trained embeddings and lexical alignment techniques to enhance generalization across languages and domains, including code-switching scenarios. Experimental results on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate significant improvements in semantic parsing accuracy, with state-of-the-art performance on the Overnight and NLmaps corpora, and strong zero-shot capabilities across diverse domains.

original_abstract: This paper introduces and evaluates the GestureKeeper, a robust hand-gesture recognition system based on a wearable inertial measurements unit (IMU). The identification of the time windows where the gestures occur, without relying on an explicit user action or a special gesture marker, is a very challenging task. To address this problem, GestureKeeper identifies the start of a gesture by exploiting the underlying dynamics of the associated time series using a recurrence quantification analysis (RQA). RQA is a powerful method for nonlinear time-series analysis, which enables the detection of critical transitions in the system's dynamical behavior. Most importantly, it does not make any assumption about the underlying distribution or model that governs the data. Having estimated the gesture window, a support vector machine is employed to recognize the specific gesture. Our proposed method is evaluated by means of a small-scale pilot study at FORTH and demonstrated that GestureKeeper can identify correctly the start of a gesture with a 87\% mean balanced accuracy and classify correctly the specific hand-gesture with a mean accuracy of over 96\%. To the best of our knowledge, GestureKeeper is the first automatic hand-gesture identification system based only on accelerometer. The performance analysis reveals the predictive power of the features and the system's robustness in the presence of additive noise. We also performed a sensitivity analysis to examine the impact of various parameters and a comparative analysis of different classifiers (SVM, random forests). Most importantly, the system can be extended to incorporate a large dictionary of gestures and operate without further calibration for a new user.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for human activity and hand gesture recognition that integrates recurrence plots (RPs), matrix and tensor completion techniques, and deep learning models. By leveraging inertial sensor data from mobile devices, the approach first employs RPs to transform raw acceleration signals into texture-like visual patterns, which are then classified using convolutional neural networks (CNNs) without the need for manual feature engineering. To address the challenge of missing data, matrix and tensor completion methods are applied to reconstruct subsampled sensor streams, enhancing the robustness of the classification system. Additionally, long short-term memory (LSTM) networks are incorporated to enable continuous gesture recognition. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves high accuracy and recall across a variety of activities and gestures, outperforming traditional feature-based methods and demonstrating effectiveness even with sparse data inputs. The integration of these techniques provides a comprehensive and adaptive solution for real-world activity and gesture recognition applications.

original_abstract: The redundancy is widely recognized in Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), which enables to remove unimportant filters from convolutional layers so as to slim the network with acceptable performance drop. Inspired by the linear and combinational properties of convolution, we seek to make some filters increasingly close and eventually identical for network slimming. To this end, we propose Centripetal SGD (C-SGD), a novel optimization method, which can train several filters to collapse into a single point in the parameter hyperspace. When the training is completed, the removal of the identical filters can trim the network with NO performance loss, thus no finetuning is needed. By doing so, we have partly solved an open problem of constrained filter pruning on CNNs with complicated structure, where some layers must be pruned following others. Our experimental results on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet have justified the effectiveness of C-SGD-based filter pruning. Moreover, we have provided empirical evidences for the assumption that the redundancy in deep neural networks helps the convergence of training by showing that a redundant CNN trained using C-SGD outperforms a normally trained counterpart with the equivalent width.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework that combines structured pruning, filter-level optimization, and channel sparsity enforcement to achieve efficient and accurate deep neural network compression. Building on recent advances in filter pruning, channel selection, and structured sparsity, our method simultaneously reduces model size, computational complexity, and memory footprint while maintaining high accuracy. By integrating auto-balanced filter pruning, ThiNet-style filter importance estimation, and network slimming techniques, we achieve significant reductions in FLOPs and parameters across multiple architectures, including VGG-16, ResNet, and LeNet. Our approach avoids irregular sparsity patterns by enforcing structured sparsity at multiple levels, enabling compatibility with standard BLAS libraries and efficient deployment on embedded systems. Experimental results demonstrate that our method achieves up to 79.7% reduction in inference cost on CIFAR-10 with less than 1% accuracy loss, and up to 20× model size reduction on VGGNet with minimal performance degradation. This unified approach provides a scalable and effective solution for deploying deep learning models in resource-constrained environments.

original_abstract: Deep clustering (DC) and utterance-level permutation invariant training (uPIT) have been demonstrated promising for speaker-independent speech separation. DC is usually formulated as two-step processes: embedding learning and embedding clustering, which results in complex separation pipelines and a huge obstacle in directly optimizing the actual separation objectives. As for uPIT, it only minimizes the chosen permutation with the lowest mean square error, doesn't discriminate it with other permutations. In this paper, we propose a discriminative learning method for speaker-independent speech separation using deep embedding features. Firstly, a DC network is trained to extract deep embedding features, which contain each source's information and have an advantage in discriminating each target speakers. Then these features are used as the input for uPIT to directly separate the different sources. Finally, uPIT and DC are jointly trained, which directly optimizes the actual separation objectives. Moreover, in order to maximize the distance of each permutation, the discriminative learning is applied to fine tuning the whole model. Our experiments are conducted on WSJ0-2mix dataset. Experimental results show that the proposed models achieve better performances than DC and uPIT for speaker-independent speech separation.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel single-channel speech separation framework that integrates deep clustering, permutation invariant training (PIT), and deep extractor networks to address the cocktail-party problem with improved robustness and performance. By combining discriminative embeddings from deep clustering with end-to-end signal approximation and permutation invariant training, the proposed model effectively handles arbitrary source permutations and unknown numbers of speakers. Additionally, a deep extractor network is incorporated to enhance target speaker recovery using a short anchor utterance, improving separation quality in complex mixtures. The framework also integrates pitch-aware features to further distinguish overlapping speakers, particularly in same-gender mixtures. Experimental results on the WSJ0-2mix and Wall Street Journal datasets demonstrate significant improvements in signal-to-distortion ratio (SDR) and word error rate (WER), achieving up to 12.0 dB SDR improvement and a 30.8% WER reduction, showcasing the effectiveness of the combined approach in real-world speech separation tasks.

original_abstract: Implicit discourse relation recognition is a challenging task due to the absence of the necessary informative clue from explicit connectives. The prediction of relations requires a deep understanding of the semantic meanings of sentence pairs. As implicit discourse relation recognizer has to carefully tackle the semantic similarity of the given sentence pairs and the severe data sparsity issue exists in the meantime, it is supposed to be beneficial from mastering the entire training data. Thus in this paper, we propose a novel memory mechanism to tackle the challenges for further performance improvement. The memory mechanism is adequately memorizing information by pairing representations and discourse relations of all training instances, which right fills the slot of the data-hungry issue in the current implicit discourse relation recognizer. Our experiments show that our full model with memorizing the entire training set reaches new state-of-the-art against strong baselines, which especially for the first time exceeds the milestone of 60% accuracy in the 4-way task.
