generated_abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to implicit discourse relation recognition by integrating multi-level attention mechanisms, paragraph-level inter-dependency modeling, and multi-task learning with label embeddings. Building on recent advances in neural networks for discourse processing, our model combines repeated reading strategies with external memory to progressively focus on key argument words, while also capturing the inter-dependencies between discourse units within a paragraph. Additionally, we incorporate multi-task learning to jointly predict discourse relations and their corresponding implicit connectives, leveraging shared and task-specific representations across different corpora. The proposed architecture is evaluated on the Penn Discourse Treebank (PDTB) and achieves state-of-the-art performance in both 11-way and 4-way classification tasks, demonstrating significant improvements over existing methods.

original_abstract: Modern object detectors can rarely achieve short training time, fast inference speed, and high accuracy at the same time. To strike a balance among them, we propose the Training-Time-Friendly Network (TTFNet). In this work, we start with light-head, single-stage, and anchor-free designs, which enable fast inference speed. Then, we focus on shortening training time. We notice that encoding more training samples from annotated boxes plays a similar role as increasing batch size, which helps enlarge the learning rate and accelerate the training process. To this end, we introduce a novel approach using Gaussian kernels to encode training samples. Besides, we design the initiative sample weights for better information utilization. Experiments on MS COCO show that our TTFNet has great advantages in balancing training time, inference speed, and accuracy. It has reduced training time by more than seven times compared to previous real-time detectors while maintaining state-of-the-art performances. In addition, our super-fast version of TTFNet-18 and TTFNet-53 can outperform SSD300 and YOLOv3 by less than one-tenth of their training time, respectively. The code has been made available at \url{https://github.com/ZJULearning/ttfnet}.
generated_abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel single-stage object detection framework that integrates the strengths of anchor-free detection, feature pyramid networks, and keypoint-based bounding box prediction. Building on recent advances from FCOS, FoveaBox, CornerNet, and NAS-FPN, our method eliminates the need for predefined anchor boxes and instead directly predicts object existence and bounding box coordinates through a combination of semantic maps and paired keypoints. By incorporating a feature selective anchor-free module and a scalable feature pyramid architecture, our approach achieves robust performance across varying object scales and aspect ratios while maintaining computational efficiency. Experimental results on the COCO and PASCAL VOC benchmarks demonstrate that our method outperforms existing single-stage detectors in terms of accuracy and inference speed, achieving a state-of-the-art mAP of 45.2% on COCO with a processing speed of 42 FPS on a single GPU. This work provides a unified, flexible, and efficient detection framework that advances the field of real-time object detection.

original_abstract: As deep neural networks become more adept at traditional tasks, many of the most exciting new challenges concern multimodality---observations that combine diverse types, such as image and text. In this paper, we introduce a family of multimodal deep generative models derived from variational bounds on the evidence (data marginal likelihood). As part of our derivation we find that many previous multimodal variational autoencoders used objectives that do not correctly bound the joint marginal likelihood across modalities. We further generalize our objective to work with several types of deep generative model (VAE, GAN, and flow-based), and allow use of different model types for different modalities. We benchmark our models across many image, label, and text datasets, and find that our multimodal VAEs excel with and without weak supervision. Additional improvements come from use of GAN image models with VAE language models. Finally, we investigate the effect of language on learned image representations through a variety of downstream tasks, such as compositionally, bounding box prediction, and visual relation prediction. We find evidence that these image representations are more abstract and compositional than equivalent representations learned from only visual data.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel deep generative framework that integrates non-linear independent component estimation (NICE), adversarial learning, and multimodal representation learning to enable advanced image synthesis and manipulation tasks. By combining the exact likelihood modeling of NICE with the discriminative power of generative adversarial networks (GANs), we develop a flexible architecture capable of learning hierarchical and invariant feature representations. Furthermore, we incorporate learned similarity metrics and adversarially learned inference to improve reconstruction quality and enable manipulation of high-level visual attributes. Our approach demonstrates superior performance in image generation, inpainting, and cross-modal synthesis tasks, including text-to-image translation and multi-modal generation, while maintaining efficient training and robustness to missing data. Experimental results on multiple benchmark datasets confirm the effectiveness of our method in capturing complex data distributions and generating visually coherent outputs.

original_abstract: Storage resources and caching techniques permeate almost every area of communication networks today. In the near future, caching is set to play an important role in storage-assisted Internet architectures, information-centric networks, and wireless systems, reducing operating and capital expenditures and improving the services offered to users. In light of the remarkable data traffic growth and the increasing number of rich-media applications, the impact of caching is expected to become even more profound than it is today. Therefore, it is crucial to design these systems in an optimal fashion, ensuring the maximum possible performance and economic benefits from their deployment. To this end, this article presents a collection of detailed models and algorithms, which are synthesized to build a powerful analytical framework for caching optimization.
generated_abstract: This paper presents a novel framework for adaptive, distributed caching in wireless networks that integrates geographic content placement, multi-coverage optimization, and dynamic popularity learning. Building on prior work on optimal geographic caching, spatial multi-LRU policies, and no-regret caching algorithms, we propose a cooperative caching strategy that jointly optimizes content placement and routing decisions in arbitrary network topologies. Our approach leverages a distributed asynchronous algorithm based on potential game theory, which enables caches with overlapping coverage areas to coordinate without centralized control or prior knowledge of content popularity. By incorporating a Markovian model for recommendation-driven content access and an online learning mechanism for popularity adaptation, our framework achieves significant improvements in cache hit probability and routing efficiency. Numerical evaluations demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing policies such as greedy placement, multi-LRU, and path replication with traditional eviction strategies, particularly in high-coverage and dynamic traffic scenarios. The algorithm guarantees a near-optimal performance with polynomial complexity and converges rapidly in practical network settings.

original_abstract: Neuromorphic computing takes inspiration from the brain to create energy efficient hardware for information processing, capable of highly sophisticated tasks. In this article, we make the case that building this new hardware necessitates reinventing electronics. We show that research in physics and material science will be key to create artificial nano-neurons and synapses, to connect them together in huge numbers, to organize them in complex systems, and to compute with them efficiently. We describe how some researchers choose to take inspiration from artificial intelligence to move forward in this direction, whereas others prefer taking inspiration from neuroscience, and we highlight recent striking results obtained with these two approaches. Finally, we discuss the challenges and perspectives in neuromorphic physics, which include developing the algorithms and the hardware hand in hand, making significant advances with small toy systems, as well as building large scale networks.
generated_abstract: This paper presents a novel neuromorphic computing system that integrates advanced memristive neurons and synapses with photonic and magnetic components to achieve high-performance, energy-efficient, and biologically plausible neural networks. Building on recent advances in metal-oxide memristor crossbars, multi-memristive synapses, and vanadium dioxide-based active memristor neurons, we demonstrate a scalable, transistorless architecture capable of performing complex classification and pattern recognition tasks. The system incorporates stochastic and leaky integrate-and-fire dynamics in artificial neurons, along with brain-inspired spike timing dependent plasticity and phase change memory-based synapses for unsupervised learning. Additionally, we introduce an all-optical spiking neurosynaptic network with wavelength division multiplexing for high-speed, parallel processing. Experimental results show equivalent accuracy to software-based training with significantly improved energy efficiency, while the integration of nanoscale spintronic oscillators and ultralow power magnetic Josephson junction synapses further enhances the system's performance and scalability. This work represents a major step toward realizing large-scale, energy-efficient neuromorphic systems with capabilities comparable to the human brain.

original_abstract: Contextual representation models have achieved great success in improving various downstream tasks. However, these language-model-based encoders are difficult to train due to the large parameter sizes and high computational complexity. By carefully examining the training procedure, we find that the softmax layer (the output layer) causes significant inefficiency due to the large vocabulary size. Therefore, we redesign the learning objective and propose an efficient framework for training contextual representation models. Specifically, the proposed approach bypasses the softmax layer by performing language modeling with dimension reduction, and allows the models to leverage pre-trained word embeddings. Our framework reduces the time spent on the output layer to a negligible level, eliminates almost all the trainable parameters of the softmax layer and performs language modeling without truncating the vocabulary. When applied to ELMo, our method achieves a 4 times speedup and eliminates 80% trainable parameters while achieving competitive performance on downstream tasks.
generated_abstract: This paper presents a novel language modeling framework that integrates recent advances in neural network architectures, pre-training strategies, and efficient parameterization techniques. Building on deep bidirectional models such as BERT and deep contextualized word representations, we incorporate character-aware mechanisms and high-rank RNN structures to better capture both syntactic and semantic properties of language, as well as long-term dependencies. By combining tied word vector representations with efficient estimation methods and leveraging pre-trained distributed word representations, our model achieves significant improvements in perplexity on benchmark datasets such as the One Billion Word and WikiText-103. Additionally, we demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in downstream NLP tasks, including question answering and sentiment analysis, by achieving state-of-the-art results with reduced computational costs and parameter counts.

original_abstract: The quality of images captured in outdoor environments can be affected by poor weather conditions such as fog, dust, and atmospheric scattering of other particles. This problem can bring extra challenges to high-level computer vision tasks like image segmentation and object detection. However, previous studies on image dehazing suffer from a huge computational workload and corruption of the original image, such as over-saturation and halos. In this paper, we present a novel image dehazing approach based on the optical model for haze images and regularized optimization. Specifically, we convert the non-convex, bilinear problem concerning the unknown haze-free image and light transmission distribution to a convex, linear optimization problem by estimating the atmosphere light constant. Our method is further accelerated by introducing a multilevel Haar wavelet transform. The optimization, instead, is applied to the low frequency sub-band decomposition of the original image. This dimension reduction significantly improves the processing speed of our method and exhibits the potential for real-time applications. Experimental results show that our approach outperforms state-of-the-art dehazing algorithms in terms of both image reconstruction quality and computational efficiency. For implementation details, source code can be publicly accessed via this http URL.
generated_abstract: This paper presents a novel application that integrates robust signal recovery techniques from compressed sensing with advanced image dehazing methodologies to address the challenge of enhancing visibility in foggy and hazy environments. Leveraging the structured matrix perturbation framework, we develop a stable signal recovery approach that accommodates uncertainties in sensing conditions, which is particularly relevant for real-world imaging systems affected by atmospheric disturbances. In parallel, we incorporate state-of-the-art dehazing algorithms, including deep learning-based and physical model-driven approaches, to restore image clarity. By combining these methods, we propose an end-to-end system that not only removes haze but also ensures robustness against sensor perturbations. The proposed framework is validated using benchmark datasets, including O-HAZE and Foggy Zurich, demonstrating superior performance in both dehazing accuracy and resilience to sensing matrix variations. The integration of these techniques opens new avenues for reliable vision systems in adverse weather conditions.

original_abstract: Over 30 papers have proposed to use convolutional neural network (CNN) for AD classification from anatomical MRI. However, the classification performance is difficult to compare across studies due to variations in components such as participant selection, image preprocessing or validation procedure. Moreover, these studies are hardly reproducible because their frameworks are not publicly accessible and because implementation details are lacking. Lastly, some of these papers may report a biased performance due to inadequate or unclear validation or model selection procedures. In the present work, we aim to address these limitations through three main contributions. First, we performed a systematic literature review and found that more than half of the surveyed papers may have suffered from data leakage. Our second contribution is the extension of our open-source framework for classification of AD using CNN and T1-weighted MRI. Finally, we used this framework to rigorously compare different CNN architectures. The data was split into training/validation/test sets at the very beginning and only the training/validation sets were used for model selection. To avoid any overfitting, the test sets were left untouched until the end of the peer-review process. Overall, the different 3D approaches (3D-subject, 3D-ROI, 3D-patch) achieved similar performances while that of the 2D slice approach was lower. Of note, the different CNN approaches did not perform better than a SVM with voxel-based features. The different approaches generalized well to similar populations but not to datasets with different inclusion criteria or demographical characteristics.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel deep learning framework for the early and accurate diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease (AD) and its prodromal stage, mild cognitive impairment (MCI), by integrating and extending previous approaches. The framework combines a deeply supervised 3D convolutional neural network (3D-CNN) with an ensemble of densely connected networks and multimodal data fusion strategies to extract discriminative features from structural MRI and FDG-PET scans. The model is pre-trained using a 3D convolutional autoencoder to capture anatomical variations and is further fine-tuned for domain adaptation and task-specific classification. To address challenges such as overfitting, gradient vanishing, and limited training samples, the framework incorporates dropout techniques, stability selection, and multitask learning. Additionally, a multiple cluster dense convolutional network is employed to learn local features from MRI patches, which are then ensembled for global classification. The proposed method achieves high diagnostic accuracy, with 94.1% on the ADNI dataset for AD vs. NC classification, 89.5% accuracy for AD vs. NC using local patch clustering, and 82.4% accuracy in predicting MCI conversion to AD. The model demonstrates robustness across different datasets and imaging protocols, offering a powerful tool for automated, non-invasive AD and MCI diagnosis.

original_abstract: We tackle the problem of object discovery, where objects are segmented for a given input image, and the system is trained without using any direct supervision whatsoever. A novel copy-pasting GAN framework is proposed, where the generator learns to discover an object in one image by compositing it into another image such that the discriminator cannot tell that the resulting image is fake. After carefully addressing subtle issues, such as preventing the generator from `cheating', this game results in the generator learning to select objects, as copy-pasting objects is most likely to fool the discriminator. The system is shown to work well on four very different datasets, including large object appearance variations in challenging cluttered backgrounds.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework that combines unsupervised representation learning with adversarial networks and multi-object segmentation to enable advanced image manipulation and scene understanding tasks. Building on deep convolutional generative adversarial networks (DCGANs), adversarial feature learning, and bidirectional mappings, the proposed method learns hierarchical and disentangled representations of scenes without supervision. By integrating techniques from image-to-image translation, cycle consistency, and context-aware synthesis, the framework achieves robust object segmentation, scene decomposition, and instance placement. The model leverages iterative variational inference and adversarial training to jointly learn object representations and their spatial relationships, enabling applications such as moving object detection, weakly-supervised segmentation, and semantically coherent object insertion. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the approach across diverse tasks, achieving performance comparable to or exceeding state-of-the-art supervised and unsupervised methods.

original_abstract: There is a growing interest in learning a model which could recognize novel classes with only a few labeled examples. In this paper, we propose Temporal Alignment Module (TAM), a novel few-shot learning framework that can learn to classify a previous unseen video. While most previous works neglect long-term temporal ordering information, our proposed model explicitly leverages the temporal ordering information in video data through temporal alignment. This leads to strong data-efficiency for few-shot learning. In concrete, TAM calculates the distance value of query video with respect to novel class proxies by averaging the per frame distances along its alignment path. We introduce continuous relaxation to TAM so the model can be learned in an end-to-end fashion to directly optimize the few-shot learning objective. We evaluate TAM on two challenging real-world datasets, Kinetics and Something-Something-V2, and show that our model leads to significant improvement of few-shot video classification over a wide range of competitive baselines.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for few-shot action recognition that combines the strengths of spatio-temporal feature learning, non-local dependency modeling, and dynamic few-shot learning. By integrating techniques from low-shot visual recognition, such as feature hallucination and representation regularization, with advanced video architectures like the Two-Stream Inflated 3D ConvNet (I3D) and Pseudo-3D Residual Networks, we develop a robust model capable of recognizing novel action categories from minimal training examples. Our approach also incorporates Temporal Relation Networks (TRN) to capture long-range temporal dependencies and Non-Local Neural Networks to model global relationships across video frames. Evaluated on the Kinetics and UCF101 datasets, our method achieves state-of-the-art performance in few-shot action recognition, demonstrating significant improvements in accuracy while maintaining strong generalization across both base and novel classes.

original_abstract: To address the limitations of existing magnitude-based pruning algorithms in cases where model weights or activations are of large and similar magnitude, we propose a novel perspective to discover parameter redundancy among channels and accelerate deep CNNs via channel pruning. Precisely, we argue that channels revealing similar feature information have functional overlap and that most channels within each such similarity group can be removed without compromising model's representational power. After deriving an effective metric for evaluating channel similarity through probabilistic modeling, we introduce a pruning algorithm via hierarchical clustering of channels. In particular, the proposed algorithm does not rely on sparsity training techniques or complex data-driven optimization and can be directly applied to pre-trained models. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets strongly demonstrate the superior acceleration performance of our approach over prior arts. On ImageNet, our pruned ResNet-50 with 30% FLOPs reduced outperforms the baseline model.
generated_abstract: This paper presents a novel framework for efficient deep neural network (DNN) compression that integrates and advances multiple existing pruning techniques. By combining neuron-level pruning, connection learning, dynamic network surgery, and structured sparsity regularization, our method enables simultaneous reduction in model size, computational complexity, and memory footprint while maintaining or improving model accuracy. The approach introduces a unified training strategy that dynamically prunes redundant connections and channels, learns important structures through sparsity-inducing regularizations, and allows for end-to-end optimization without reliance on pre-trained models. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate significant compression ratios—up to 108× for LeNet-5 and 17.7× for AlexNet—with minimal accuracy loss, outperforming state-of-the-art methods. The proposed framework is compatible with various architectures and provides a flexible, efficient solution for deploying DNNs on resource-constrained platforms.

original_abstract: Rather than the visual images, the face recognition of the caricatures is far from the performance of the visual images. The challenge is the extreme non-rigid distortions of the caricatures introduced by exaggerating the facial features to strengthen the characters. In this paper, we propose dynamic multi-task learning based on deep CNNs for cross-modal caricature-visual face recognition. Instead of the conventional multi-task learning with fixed weights of the tasks, the proposed dynamic multi-task learning dynamically updates the weights of tasks according to the importance of the tasks, which enables the training of the networks focus on the hard task instead of being stuck in the overtraining of the easy task. The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the dynamic multi-task learning for caricature-visual face recognition. The performance evaluated on the datasets CaVI and WebCaricature show the superiority over the state-of-art methods. The implementation code is available here.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a unified deep learning framework that integrates face alignment, recognition, and attribute prediction to enhance robustness and accuracy in unconstrained environments. By combining multitask cascaded convolutional networks with task-constrained learning, the proposed model jointly optimizes facial landmark detection, identity recognition, and auxiliary attribute inference (e.g., gender, expression, and pose). A dynamic weighting scheme balances task contributions, while leveraging inter-task correlations to improve convergence and generalization. The framework is evaluated on large-scale benchmarks such as MegaFace and MS-Celeb-1M, demonstrating superior performance in handling occlusions, pose variations, and scale challenges. Additionally, the model achieves state-of-the-art results in face recognition and alignment tasks, while maintaining computational efficiency. The proposed approach advances the integration of multiple facial analysis tasks, offering a versatile solution for real-world applications.

original_abstract: Quantization reduces computation costs of neural networks but suffers from performance degeneration. Is this accuracy drop due to the reduced capacity, or inefficient training during the quantization procedure? After looking into the gradient propagation process of neural networks by viewing the weights and intermediate activations as random variables, we discover two critical rules for efficient training. Recent quantization approaches violates the two rules and results in degenerated convergence. To deal with this problem, we propose a simple yet effective technique, named scale-adjusted training (SAT), to comply with the discovered rules and facilitates efficient training. We also analyze the quantization error introduced in calculating the gradient in the popular parameterized clipping activation (PACT) technique. Through SAT together with gradient-calibrated PACT, quantized models obtain comparable or even better performance than their full-precision counterparts, achieving state-of-the-art accuracy with consistent improvement over previous quantization methods on a wide spectrum of models including MobileNet-V1/V2 and PreResNet-50.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework that combines binary weight training, low-bitwidth quantization, and learned quantization parameters to achieve highly accurate and compact deep neural networks (DNNs) suitable for deployment on low-power and embedded devices. Building on methods such as BinaryConnect, DoReFa-Net, Trained Ternary Quantization, and Learned Quantization (LQ-Nets), our approach enables efficient training with low-precision weights and activations while maintaining high model accuracy. By integrating differentiable quantization, mixed-precision strategies, and joint training of quantizers with network parameters, we demonstrate significant improvements in both model compression and inference speed. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets such as CIFAR-10, ImageNet, and COCO show that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance with reduced computational and memory requirements, making it a promising solution for real-world deployment scenarios.

original_abstract: Text contained in an image carries high-level semantics that can be exploited to achieve richer image understanding. In particular, the mere presence of text provides strong guiding content that should be employed to tackle a diversity of computer vision tasks such as image retrieval, fine-grained classification, and visual question answering. In this paper, we address the problem of fine-grained classification and image retrieval by leveraging textual information along with visual cues to comprehend the existing intrinsic relation between the two modalities. The novelty of the proposed model consists of the usage of a PHOC descriptor to construct a bag of textual words along with a Fisher Vector Encoding that captures the morphology of text. This approach provides a stronger multimodal representation for this task and as our experiments demonstrate, it achieves state-of-the-art results on two different tasks, fine-grained classification and image retrieval.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel end-to-end framework that integrates scene text detection, recognition, and visual question answering (VQA) to enable comprehensive understanding of text-rich natural images. Building on recent advances in text detection (e.g., TextBoxes++, EAST), text recognition (E2E-MLT, TextSpotter), and multi-modal fusion (MFB with co-attention), our approach unifies these tasks within a single architecture. The framework leverages a powerful text detector to locate and recognize text instances, while incorporating a co-attention mechanism to jointly model visual and textual information for answering questions that require reading and reasoning about text. We evaluate our model on the TextVQA dataset and demonstrate significant improvements in both text-based VQA and end-to-end text recognition tasks, outperforming existing state-of-the-art methods. Additionally, we show that the integration of scene text with visual features enhances performance in fine-grained image classification and text-based image retrieval, highlighting the versatility and practical applicability of our approach.

original_abstract: Deep neural networks (DNNs) have shown huge superiority over humans in image recognition, speech processing, autonomous vehicles and medical diagnosis. However, recent studies indicate that DNNs are vulnerable to adversarial examples (AEs), which are designed by attackers to fool deep learning models. Different from real examples, AEs can mislead the model to predict incorrect outputs while hardly be distinguished by human eyes, therefore threaten security-critical deep-learning applications. In recent years, the generation and defense of AEs have become a research hotspot in the field of artificial intelligence (AI) security. This article reviews the latest research progress of AEs. First, we introduce the concept, cause, characteristics and evaluation metrics of AEs, then give a survey on the state-of-the-art AE generation methods with the discussion of advantages and disadvantages. After that, we review the existing defenses and discuss their limitations. Finally, future research opportunities and challenges on AEs are prospected.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework that combines advanced adversarial example generation techniques with robust detection mechanisms to enhance the security of deep learning systems in real-world applications. Building on recent findings that adversarial examples are highly transferable across models and remain effective even when perceived through physical sensors, we propose a two-pronged defense strategy inspired by MagNet and convolutional filter statistics. Our approach integrates a manifold-based detector to distinguish adversarial examples from normal inputs and employs a reformer network to reconstruct adversarial samples toward the normal data manifold. Additionally, we leverage universal perturbation insights to improve detection accuracy across diverse network architectures. Experimental results demonstrate that our framework effectively identifies and mitigates adversarial attacks in both blackbox and graybox scenarios, maintaining a low false positive rate while significantly improving robustness against state-of-the-art adversarial methods.

original_abstract: Abstract   Disease progression modeling (DPM) using longitudinal data is a challenging machine learning task. Existing DPM algorithms neglect temporal dependencies among measurements, make parametric assumptions about biomarker trajectories, do not model multiple biomarkers jointly, and need an alignment of subjects’ trajectories. In this paper, recurrent neural networks (RNNs) are utilized to address these issues. However, in many cases, longitudinal cohorts contain incomplete data, which hinders the application of standard RNNs and requires a pre-processing step such as imputation of the missing values. Instead, we propose a generalized training rule for the most widely used RNN architecture, long short-term memory (LSTM) networks, that can handle both missing predictor and target values. The proposed LSTM algorithm is applied to model the progression of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) using six volumetric magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) biomarkers, i.e., volumes of ventricles, hippocampus, whole brain, fusiform, middle temporal gyrus, and entorhinal cortex, and it is compared to standard LSTM networks with data imputation and a parametric, regression-based DPM method.
